zh:
数月前，一艘商船随着海浪来到浙江渡口，卸货途中，一只浑身雪白的小猫儿悄悄跃下甲板，穿梭在人潮中。商队卸货很快，也无人注意它，待港口的人发现小猫儿的踪影，商船早已消失在海天尽头。
孤身留下的猫儿在港口讨生活，身上沾了灰尘，脸也花了，只有一对眼睛依旧蓝哇哇，好像番邦商人带来的宝石，又像沉在海水里的月儿。在港口劳作的人为了生计奔波，有时连说话的工夫都有不曾有，可每每瞧见猫儿，却忍不住慢下步子与它玩闹一番，仿佛日子里的苦闷也淡了。小白猫得了月儿的名，每日都有新鲜的鱼肉吃，瞧着十分快活，只是月上梢头的时候，当它望向翻涌的海浪，心中还会偶尔想起那艘海浪上的航船。
en:
Months ago, a merchant ship rode the waves into a port along the Zhejiang Crossing. While the cargo was being unloaded, a little snow-white kitten quietly leapt down from the deck and slipped into the crowd. The merchants unloaded their goods swiftly, and none took notice. By the time the folk at the harbor spotted the cat's trail, the merchant ship had already vanished beyond the edge of sea and sky.
Left to fend for itself, the cat scraped out a living at the harbor. Dust clung to its fur and its face grew smudged, yet its eyes remained ever so blue, like gemstones brought by merchants from foreign lands, or like the moon sunk beneath the sea. Those who toiled at the harbor, ever rushing about for their livelihood, scarcely had time even to exchange words with one another. Yet whenever they caught sight of the cat, they could not help but slow their steps to play with it a while, as though the bitterness of their days grew a little lighter. The little white cat came to be called Yue'er, and each day it was fed fresh fish, seeming quite content. Yet when the moon climbed above the treetops, and it gazed upon the churning waves, its heart would sometimes still recall that ship upon the sea.

所谓话术，因人而异，便如与夏虫言冰，不可同日而语。好比儒生之话术，满口“之乎者也”，道士之话术，不是“无量”便是“天尊”，而和尚之话术，则是释迦牟尼佛、金刚不坏佛、宝光佛、龙尊王佛、精进军佛、精进喜佛、宝火佛、宝月光佛、现无愚佛、宝月佛、无垢佛、离垢佛、勇施佛、清净佛、清净施佛、婆留那佛、水天佛、坚德佛、旃檀功德佛、无量掬光佛、光德佛、无忧德佛、那罗延佛、功德华佛、莲华光游戏神通佛、财功德佛、德念佛、善名称功德如来、红炎幢王如来、善游步功德如来、斗战胜如来、善游步如来、周匝庄严功德如来、宝华游步如来、宝莲华善住娑罗树王如来……众生平等，观者之话术，与贫僧之话术，虽各有不同，却无上下高低之分。和尚所言，为和尚所用，非为汝所用，若于汝有用，则为和尚之幸，亦为观者之幸，观者即为众生，此即为众生之幸，能以和尚一言普度众生，便不枉和尚苦思冥想，笔录此卷，善哉、善哉。
……
（此后大段篇幅，足有数千字，观其内容废话连篇，又臭又长，颠三倒四，不知所云）

宋九批注：实为夜间无眠之良友，出恭必备之美材！
en:
The so-called "art of speech" varies from person to person, like discussing ice with summer insects, utterly incomparable. A Confucian scholar's rhetoric brims with "zhihu-zheye". A Daoist priest's is either "Boundless Virtue" or "Heavenly Venerable". While a monk's litany invokes "Sakyamuni Buddha, Vajra-Indestructible Buddha, Radiant Treasure Buddha, Dragon-Honored King Buddha, Zealous Army Buddha, Joyous Zeal Buddha, Blazing Treasure Buddha, Moonlight Treasure Buddha, Wisdom-Manifest Buddha, Lunar Treasure Buddha, Stainless Buddha, Beyond-Defilement Buddha, Courageous Almsgiver Buddha, Pure Buddha, Pure Offering Buddha, Varuna Buddha, Water-Celestial Buddha, Steadfast Virtue Buddha, Sandalwood-Merit Buddha, Immeasurable Light-Gathering Buddha, Luminous Virtue Buddha, Sorrowless Virtue Buddha, Narayana Buddha, Merit-Blossom Buddha, Lotus-Light Playful Miracle Buddha, Wealth-Merit Buddha, Virtue-Remembrance Buddha, Well-Named Merit Tathagata, Crimson Flame Banner King Tathagata, Skillful Stride Merit Tathagata, Victorious in Battle Tathagata... All beings are equal. The observer's rhetoric and this humble monk's may differ, yet neither is superior. What a monk speaks serves the monk, not necessarily you. If it aids you, then it is the monk's fortune, the observer's fortune, and thus all beings' fortune. That a single phrase of mine might universally deliver souls justifies the sleepless nights spent scribbling this scroll. Well said, well said....
(The following section spans thousands of characters, rambling, repetitive, and utterly incoherent.)

Comment by Song Jiu: A fine companion for sleepless nights, and excellent privy reading material!

zh:
姜隗记得，找到阿姐尸骨的那晚，风清月明，天色极好。
他几乎扒遍了整个坟场，才终于在一个棺椁内找到了熟悉的簪子。那是他幼年时送予阿姐的。

儿时的他总是喧闹，父母疲于生计，只有他的阿姐会抚着他的头，听他叽叽喳喳的讲那些漫无边际的畅想。
他很爱他的阿姐，总想让她快乐起来。阿姐爱美，他便学着为阿姐画眉。阿姐爱挽发，他便花了好几个月，为阿姐做了一支桃花纹的木簪。
阿姐拿到木簪的那天，那脸上的笑容，让他很是欣喜。
但一日他在外头捡松子归来，阿姐却不见了。而他的父母同他说，阿姐嫁人了。
嫁给谁了？什么时候回来？为什么都不同他说一声？他叽叽喳喳地问，却没人答。
再后来，阿姐就好像从世间消失了一般……但他们家的日子却一天天好起来了。

过了好多好多年后，姜隗才知道，原来他们家的好日子，是用阿姐的性命，以及无数像阿姐那样的女子的性命，换来的。
“你们把她卖给了死人？”他几乎不敢相信。
“吵什么？女子生下来，便是为了给家里添财的。”他的父亲躺在摇椅上，不以为然，“嫁了活人，家里头能靠着聘礼过上个把月的好日子，是笔划算的买卖。若能嫁死人，那便是家里烧了高香！”
“就是，这么好的买卖，只做一笔，岂不可惜？”他的大伯靠在墙边，把玩着手上的鎏金指环。
那一刻， 彻骨的冷席卷了姜隗。
en:
Jiang Wei remembers the night he found his sister's remains: the wind was gentle, the moon bright, a perfect sky.
He'd searched nearly every grave in the cemetery before finding the familiar hairpin in a rotting coffin. He'd crafted it for her as a child.

In those early years, he had been a boisterous boy. His parents were consumed by toil, leaving only his elder sister to stroke his hair and listen to his endless, rambling dreams.
He adored her. Longed to see her happy. Knowing she loved beauty, he learned to paint her brows. Knowing she cherished her hair, he spent months carving her a wooden pin adorned with peach blossoms.
The day she received it, her smile had filled him with joy.
But one day, he'd returned from gathering pine nuts to find her gone. His parents had said she'd "married".
To whom? When would she return? Why hadn't they told him? His questions spilled out in frantic chirps, met only with silence.
Afterward, it was as if his sister had vanished from the earth... yet the family's fortunes slowly improved.

Years later, Jiang Wei understood. Their comfort had been bought with his sister's life and the lives of countless girls like her.
"You sold her to a corpse?" His voice trembled with disbelief.
"Quiet down," his father had snapped from his rocking chair. "Girls are born to bring wealth. Marrying a live man might give us a month of good living with the bride price. But marrying a dead man? That's a blessing from heaven!"
"Aye, why stop at one such bargain?" His uncle leaned against the wall, toying with a gilded ring.
In that moment, Jiang Wei had felt an icy chill penetrate his bones.

zh:
一
那天的雪下得很安静。
她坐在院中，膝盖上盖着一条薄毯，手里捧着一碗热汤。汤是丈夫煮的，放了枣，甜。她从不知道他会煮汤。成亲三个月，她每天都在发现他不会的事，和他会的事。
他不会劈柴。劈出来的柴长短不齐，码在墙角像一排歪倒的牙。他会在劈柴之前，先把最齐整的那根挑出来，削成小马，塞进她手里。
“给你。”他说，“我小时候，我爹就是这么给我做的。”
她握着那匹小马。木刺扎进指腹，她不觉得疼。
那是她第一次觉得，日子可以这么过。不是刀尖上舔血，不是今朝有酒今朝醉，是早上醒来，身边有人，锅里温着粥。是晚上睡去，不必担心半夜有人推门。
门被推开的时候，她正把那匹小马放在窗台上。阳光照在上面，木纹清晰，像真的马在跑。
她甚至没来得及回头。

二
她没有哭。
丈夫拦在她面前，喊着她快跑，被人一刀贯穿的时候，她没有哭。她只是看着他，看着他的眼睛从睁着变成半阖，看着他嘴角那滴血慢慢凝固。她伸出手，想帮他擦掉，手伸到一半，被人拽了回去。
她突然没有力气了，她也没有挣扎。她的手就那样伸着，五指张开，像是要抓住什么。什么也没有抓住。
后来她才想起，那滴血，她没有擦掉。
那滴血就那样留在他脸上，留了一辈子。在她的记忆里，他永远带着那滴血，永远闭不上眼睛。
她被拖走的时候，经过了那扇窗。窗台上的小马还在，阳光还在，木纹还是很清晰。
她看了它一眼。
她还是没有哭。

三
牢房很小。
她蜷缩在角落里，膝盖抵着下巴。这个姿势她熟悉。小时候被抄家，她也是这么蜷着，在那间堆满杂物的柴房里。
那时候她还很小，只知道家里来了一群穿官服的人，把所有人都赶到了院子里。母亲在哭，父亲被按着跪在地上，头上的帽子掉了，露出一片白花花的头皮。她想跑，被一只大手拎了起来，和家里的女眷一起，都被关起来。她被扔进了柴房，要等着明天押送出去。

她从牢房里醒来时，脸上湿了一片。
不是眼泪。是水。有人往她脸上泼了一碗冷水。她抬起头，看见监牢的铁栅外站着一个人，面目模糊。
“你怀孕了。”那人说。
她的手下意识地放在肚子上。平的。什么都没有。但那人不会骗她。骗她有什么意义呢？
她闭上眼。
心里有一个声音说：我要活。
这个声音不是从脑子里来的。是从肚子里来的。是从那个她还感觉不到的小东西来的。它还没成形，还没心跳，还没长出手脚，但它已经在她身体里了，像一匹还没削好的小木马。
只要它还在，他就还在。
只要它还在，那个院子就在，那碗枣汤就在，那匹站在窗台上的小木马就在。
只要它还在，她就还活着。不是那种“还没死”的活着，是真正的、暖暖的、想明天的活着。
她想活。

第六次逃跑失败后，牢房里来了一个人。不是审她的，是来跟她谈的。
“你知道的，我们可以杀了你。”那人坐在她对面，语气平淡，像在说今天天气不错，“按规矩，你早该死了。”
她没有说话。
“但我们也舍不得。要养一个杀手，很贵。”那人顿了顿，“所以，给你一个机会。继续当影子杀手去做事。做成一单，准你看一次孩子。”
她低着头，看着自己的手指。指甲断了，指尖还在渗血。
“孩子生下来，要给我。”
她抬起头。
那人轻笑了一声。

孩子生下来的那天，她没有听到哭声。
她醒过来的时候，身边是空的。有人告诉她，是个男孩。
她想看一眼。但只收到了新的指令，要杀一个叫高木春的人。

四
客栈的门是虚掩着的。
她悄悄进去的时候，老板正背对着她，蹲在地上收拾柴火。
她没有犹豫。
刀很快。那瘸子老板甚至没有叫出声。他扑倒在地上，手里还攥着一根木柴。
她低下头，看着那根木柴。劈得歪歪扭扭，长短不齐。就像——
什么也不像。
她没有管，继续检查。直到在房间里发现了一个孩子，睡得正香。
她应该杀了这孩子的。
但是她没有。她走神了，她想，未满月的孩子会说话吗？她的孩子会也睡得这么香，她的孩子此刻是不是在睡梦中喊了一声——
喊了谁？
反正不是她。
她转身走了。她没有杀那个孩子。
她走神了，因此没有注意到，在她转身后，那孩子睁开了眼，很冷的眼。

第二天，她把那个孩子托给了常来送菜的马车夫。
她当然没有出面。只是让客栈里新来的客人帮忙传话。那客人一脸困惑，但还是答应了。
“这孩子可怜。”她说，“带他走吧。”
她没有说“可怜”是什么意思。那客人也没有问。
她是杀手。杀手不能有善心。
善心是刀上的缺口。有了缺口，刀就不快了。刀不快了，就会死。
她知道，她知道，她都知道。

五
但她还是出了手。
那天客栈里有人争吵。她没有多想，瓶子就砸出去了。那个人倒在血泊里。
没人看见她出手，那个女人也早就晕了。
她赶紧退回去，直到有人发现了尸体，开始叫唤，开始指认，开始审判。
有人从那晕倒的女人的房间里搜出一张纸——《放良书》。
上面写着这个女人的名字，慕容秋。
她站在那里，看着那三个字，像是在看别人的名字。
耳边忽然响起另一个声音。很远，很轻，像从十几年前飘来的。
“小小姐，快跑。快跑。”
那是桃花的声音。
那时候的她还不是杀手白毫，她叫慕容秋。她还是那个被抄家的小姐。那时候面前的女人还不叫慕容秋，她叫桃花，是那个总跟在她身后的小玩伴，小丫鬟。
抄家的那天，桃花悄悄打开了柴房的门。
“小小姐，快跑。”桃花推着她，“从后门走，快点。”
她跑了。她跑了很远。她没有回头。
她不知道桃花被抓去替了她。她不知道桃花被当成她，送进了教坊司。她不知道桃花后来顶着慕容秋的名字，受尽苦楚，活着，站在她面前。
她什么都不知道。
她只知道跑。
她跑了十几年，跑到了这里，跑到了这张放良书面前。
跑到了桃花面前。

她看着桃花。众人看着桃花，桃花只是在哭。
慕容秋忽然想起了很多事。想起小时候桃花和她在家里捉蝴蝶，想起桃花偷偷帮她藏了话本子，想起桃花那天把她推进了光里，而自己留在了黑暗中。
她想起了自己的丈夫。他劈柴的样子，他削小马的样子，他端着枣汤向她走来的样子。
她想起了自己从未见过的孩子。他吃得好吗？他睡得好吗？
她想起了自己这一辈子。
被人追杀，也追杀别人。被人关押，也关押过别人。被人拯救，也拯救过别人——但她拯救的，永远不是她想拯救的那一个。
命运对所有人都这么恶毒。
让她和桃花在这样的地方重逢。
让她在做完这一切之后，才发现自己从抄家的那天开始就错了。
她可以继续错下去。像被抄家那晚一样，转身走，不回头。
但她累了。
她不想再跑了。

六
她做了一个决定。
她要救桃花。不止是救她活着，是要把她从这场风雪里彻底推出去。让桃花去青州，去那个想了半辈子的小院子。
她还要拿到高木春带的宝物。那东西一定能换回她的孩子。
她不知道能不能成。她只知道，这是她这辈子，最后的善心了。
刀已经卷刃了。但它还能砍最后一次。
她回了房，想出了一个计划。把真老板的尸体拖出来，假死的计划。
窗外，雪还在下。
阳光照在窗台上，木纹清晰，好像有一匹小马站在那里，像真的在跑。
她会回到那扇有小木马的窗户下的。
en:
I
The snow fell in absolute silence that day.
She sat in the courtyard with a thin blanket draped over her knees, cradling a bowl of hot soup. Her husband had made it, simmered with jujubes until sweet. She never knew he could cook soup. In their three short months of marriage, every day brought new discoveries of what he could not do, and what he could.
He could not chop firewood. His logs were always uneven, stacked in the corner like a crooked row of teeth. Yet before lifting the axe, he would always pick out the straightest piece, whittle it into a little horse, and press it into her hand.
"For you," he would say. "My father made these for me when I was a boy."
She held the little wooden horse. A splinter pricked her finger, but she felt no pain.

For the first time, she realized life could be lived like this. Not tasting blood on the edge of a blade, not drowning today's dread in wine, but waking to someone breathing beside her, with porridge warm on the stove. It was falling asleep without fear that the door might be kicked open in the dead of night.

When the door gave way, she was just setting the little horse upon the windowsill. The sunlight fell across it, illuminating the grain so clearly the horse seemed to gallop.
She did not even have time to turn around.

II
She did not cry.
When her husband threw himself in front of her, shouting for her to run, and took a blade straight through his chest, she did not cry. She only watched him. Watched his eyes slip half-shut. Watched that single drop of blood at the corner of his mouth slowly congeal. She reached out, trying to wipe it away, but was violently dragged back before her fingers could touch him.

Her strength left her all at once. She did not struggle. Her hand hung frozen in the air, fingers splayed, grasping for something. There was nothing.
Only much later did she realize she never wiped that drop of blood away.
It remained on his face for a lifetime. In her memory, he would forever wear that crimson mark, his eyes never quite closed.

As she was dragged away, she passed the window. The little horse still stood on the sill in the sunlight, its grain distinct.
She gave it one last glance.
Still, she did not cry.

III
The cell was impossibly small.
She huddled in the corner, knees pressed tight against her chin. A posture etched into her memory. Years ago, when her family estate was seized, she had curled in the woodshed the exact same way.

She had been so young then, remembering only a swarm of officials herding everyone into the courtyard. Her mother weeping. Her father forced to his knees, his hat knocked loose to bare his pale scalp. She tried to run, only to be scooped up by a massive hand and locked away with the household women in the woodshed, awaiting the morning march into servitude.

When she woke in the cell, her face was wet.
Not with tears, but cold water dashed across her face. Looking up through the gloom, she saw a shadowed figure outside the iron bars.
"You are with child," the voice said.

Her hand drifted instinctively to her belly. It was flat. Empty. But that person had no reason to lie. What was the point in lying to her?
She closed her eyes.
A voice rose within her: I must live.

The voice came not from her mind, but from her womb. From that tiny seed she could not yet feel. It had no shape, no heartbeat, no limbs, but it was already within her, like a little wooden horse waiting to be carved.
As long as it remained, he remained.
As long as it remained, the courtyard, the warm jujube soup, and the little horse upon the windowsill were all still real.
As long as it remained, she was truly alive. Not just surviving, but warm, breathing, and looking forward to tomorrow.
She wanted to live.

After her sixth failed escape, a visitor came. Not to interrogate, but to bargain.
"You know we could kill you," the man said, taking a seat across from her, his voice as casual as discussing the weather. "By law, you should have been dead long ago."
She said nothing.
"Yet it would be a waste. Training an assassin is costly." He paused. "Here is your chance: serve once more as a shadow assassin. Complete a contract, and you earn one visit with your child."
She kept her head down, staring at her broken fingernails, the tips still oozing blood.
"Once born, the child belongs to us."
She looked up.
The man gave a quiet chuckle.

The day the child was born, she heard no cry.
When she woke, the space beside her was cold. They told her it was a boy.
She begged for a single glance, but received only a new order: kill a woman named Gao Muchun.

IV
The inn door was left ajar.
When she slipped inside, the innkeeper was crouching with his back turned, gathering firewood.
She did not hesitate.
Her blade was swift. The crippled man did not even cry out as he collapsed, fingers still clutching a split log.
She looked down at the wood. It was uneven and crooked, cut wildly awry. Just like...
Just like nothing at all.

She brushed the thought aside and searched the rooms, finding a boy fast asleep.
She should have killed him.
Yet she hesitated. Is her own child sleeping just as soundly? Can a baby under a month old speak? Is he crying out in his dreams?
Calling for whom?
Not for her.

She turned and left, sparing the boy.
Lost in thought, she never noticed that the moment she turned her back, the boy opened his eyes, cold and calculating.

The next morning, she entrusted the child to a regular carter.
She did not show her face, sending word through a newly arrived guest who looked puzzled but agreed.
"The child is pitiful," she said. "Take him away."
She did not explain what she meant, and the guest did not ask.
She was an assassin. Assassins cannot harbor mercy.
Mercy is a notch in the blade. A notched blade loses its edge, and a dull blade brings death.
She knew. She knew it all too well.

V
Yet she still intervened.
That day, a fight broke out in the inn. Before thinking, she hurled a jug, sending the man crashing into a pool of blood.
No one saw her strike. The woman had already fainted.
She slipped back into hiding, watching as the body was discovered, the shouting erupted, and the accusations began.

Someone searched the unconscious woman's belongings and pulled out a single sheet: a Deed of Manumission.
Across it was inscribed the woman's name: Murong Qiu.
She stood watching the three characters, as if reading the name of a stranger.

A whisper echoed in her ears, faint and distant, drifting from over a decade ago.
"Young Mistress, run. Run!"
It was Taohua's voice.

Back then, she was not the assassin White Plume; she was Murong Qiu, daughter of a ruined noble family. And the woman on the floor was not Murong Qiu; she was Taohua, her childhood playmate, the loyal maid who always followed behind her.
On the day of the raid, it was Taohua who secretly unlatched the woodshed door.
"Young Mistress, run," Taohua urged, pushing her toward the door. "Take the back gate, quickly!"

She ran. She ran far and never looked back.
She never knew Taohua was captured in her stead. She never knew Taohua was taken under her name to endure the horrors of servitude. She never knew Taohua had borne the name Murong Qiu through years of suffering, surviving only to stand before her today.
She had known nothing.
She only knew how to run.
She ran for ten years, running all the way here, straight to this deed of freedom.
Straight back to Taohua.

She looked at Taohua. The crowd watched Taohua, who only wept.
Memories rushed back: chasing butterflies in the courtyard, Taohua hiding storybooks for her, Taohua shoving her into the light while remaining in the dark.
She remembered her husband: the way he chopped wood, whittled little horses, and walked toward her with warm jujube soup.
She remembered her unseen son: was he eating well, sleeping soundly?
She thought of her entire life: hunted and hunting; imprisoned and imprisoning; rescued and rescuing, yet never saving the one she truly wished to save.

Fate was cruel, orchestrating this reunion in such a place, forcing her to realize that everything had been wrong since the night of the raid.
She could keep running, just like that night, turning away without looking back.
But she was tired.
She did not want to run anymore.

VI
She made her decision.
She would save Taohua. Not just keep her alive, but push her completely out of this blizzard, sending her toward Qingzhou to the quiet courtyard she had dreamed of for half a lifetime.
And she would claim the treasure carried by Gao Muchun. That relic would buy back her son.

She did not know if she would succeed, but she knew this was the final act of mercy left in her life.
Her blade was notched, but it could strike one last time.

Returning to her room, she devised a plan to drag out the true innkeeper's body and fake her own death.
Outside, the snow fell on.
Sunlight touched the windowsill, highlighting the grain of the wood as though a little wooden horse stood there, frozen mid-gallop.
She would find her way back to that window, and back to her little wooden horse.

自高山下雪水，依势开暗渠，引潜流，坎儿井成，清泉可饮，村居始生。然沙暴过境，井枯村危，有将领持图而来，定井成之约。代代挖井人燃油灯、挥锄镐，不辞劳苦，无问岁月，惟愿掘得活水，惠泽后人。

天少遂人愿，旦夕埋祸福。风沙骤暴起，村毁人声灭。暮色四合，忽燃一粒星火。原是去者归来，誓继祖业。聚世代之力改天地造化，集子孙之志建沙中绿洲，春秋代序，薪火长明。
en:
They tapped the mountain peaks, tunneling deep to drain the earth of its hidden water. Thus, the Karez well was born—a source of life where the villages took root. But when the sandstorms hit, the wells went dry and hope withered. A general marched in with a map, sealing a pact to bring the water back. Generation after generation, they swung their pickaxes by the dim light of oil lamps, fighting the relentless earth. They didn't care about time—only about finding the lifeblood for those to come.

But the heavens had other plans. A sudden, brutal storm wiped the village off the map. In the silence that followed, a single spark ignited. The departed returned, vowing to finish the job. They united the power of the past to conquer the desert, turning shifting sands into a lush oasis. The years pass, but their fire burns unquenchable.

I've heard that Han Changli of the previous dynasty wrote "On Horses", claiming, "Thousand-mile horses are common, but Bo Le's are rare"—what impassioned rhetoric, unmatched through the ages... but in truth, utter rubbish! Horses come in inferior and fine, just as men are fools or horse tamers. Only when a fine horse falls into the hands of a master tamer can they achieve mutual greatness—like beauty with talent, sword with hero... Thus, I record all the fine horses my ancestors and I have tamed, to warn descendants: Skip that drivel titled "On Horses"! Han Yu was just a pedant who didn't know whether to trim hooves or heat iron first for shoeing—follow his advice and you'll end up in a ditch!

Few know the Coffin Master duo are not master and servant, but father and son. Once powerful warriors, they were captured by Aureate Pavilion and transformed into Sleeping Puppets. Miraculously, they retained consciousness—yet the son's bones were shattered, forcing him to dwell in a coffin, while the father lost his voice, condemned to silence. 
Since outsiders only hear the coffin's occupant giving orders to the bearer, they mistook them for master and servant, hence the name "Coffin Master." 
The Coffin Master had always refused to be a puppet of Aureate Pavilion.. The father-and-son duo escaped during its invasion of Qinghe. They have searched endlessly for a way to restore their bodies, but all in vain.

en:
Su Wangting's first year in the capital. Kaifeng City was a world apart from his village: official roads smooth as a whetstone, Revelry Hall ablaze every night, and the market's din never-failing.
Yet he found shadows of home even here: the gaunt, sallow faces of the commoners, and refugees wandering with nowhere to call their own...
Thus, he wrote the Memorial on Land Reclamation and Husbandry, vowing that even as a failed scholar, his words would reach the ears of the Emperor.

zh:
“若是我要去江湖，要带上什么！”
八岁的萧史扎着马步，问爹给他请来的江湖师父。
那老头坐在他们府上的假山上，哼了一声，把一块石子掷到他的腿上：“带上什么？带上你爹的骂。”

小时候的萧史顶了天地擅长上房揭瓦，离家出走，拿着木剑和同辈的玩伴动手更是多了去，总之，能惹他爹吹胡子瞪眼的事，他一样不落，件件上心，一把年纪的萧副指挥使可怜白日头疼朝堂的事，夜里在床上翻来覆去惊醒，还得骂一句混账儿子。萧府后头的屋子便成了犯错的萧史常来常往的地方——来几次取决于他犯了几次错，住上多久取决于这事儿是让他爹半夜醒了几次。
家中的仆役每次听到那屋内传来的——“救人啊！杀人犯法！”之类的声音，便低低地叹一口气，“少爷今天又招惹老爷不高兴了。”

最近，萧副指挥使在那小屋上落了两把锁。
这是萧史和他爹闹得最厉害得一次，“你要是敢把老子放出来，老子一刻也不待这儿破地方，老子要去浪迹江湖。”“什么沈家小姐，你就是打死我我也不会和她过日子。”骂完破地方的那个清晨，这小屋上头又多了一把锁，骂完打死也不过日子的那个晌午，萧副指挥使狠狠地在关他的屋门上踹了几下：“不分好赖。”
萧史自觉不是不分好赖的人，他早就想好了，他这儿的事只有两种分好赖，他喜欢的便是好，不喜欢的便是赖，他自觉只做好事。
他早就想好了，他早晚不在这儿待着，若他有一日去了江湖，他要带上什么，他要带上一笛一剑，剑用来与人比武，笛用在比武之后赢了便吹上一曲，再去讲自个儿听到的故事，遇到的故事。

“那你的故事讲给谁听？”
“讲给谁听不重要，重要的是故事！——不过呢，反正不会讲给那沈小姐听，我是真不喜欢她。”
en:
"What should I bring if I'm heading to the jianghu?"

Eight-year-old Xiao Shi asked the martial arts master his father had hired, legs locked in a horse stance.

The old man, sitting on top of a rockery in their courtyard, snorted and tossed a pebble at his knee.

"What should you bring? Your father's curses."

Back then, Xiao Shi was a walking disaster—climbing rooftops, running off from home, brawling other kids with wooden swords. If there was a way to infuriate his father, he'd find it and do it twice. Deputy General Xiao, already burdened with court affairs by day, would wake in the middle of the night muttering, "That damn brat," before tossing and turning again. The little house on the backside of the Xiao estate became Xiao Shi's regular haunt. How often he stayed depended on how many times he'd driven his father out of bed cursing.

Whenever the servants heard shouts like "Help! Murder's a crime!" Echoing from that room, they'd sigh and mutter, "Young Master's upset the lord again."

Lately, the deputy commander had added two more locks to that door.

This was their worst fight yet.

"If you dare let me out, I swear I'll leave this wretched place in a heartbeat! I'm going to roam the jianghu!"

"As for that Miss Shen, even if you beat me to death, I'm not marrying her!"

After that "wretched place" rant, one more lock was added the next morning. By midday, after the "beat me to death" declaration, Deputy General Xiao gave the door a good kicking:

"No sense of right or wrong!"

But Xiao Shi didn't think he lacked a sense of right and wrong. He already had it figured out. There were only two kinds of things in this world—what he liked and what he didn't. What he liked was right. What he didn't was wrong. And he had already decided to only do the right things.

He knew from long ago he wouldn't stay here forever. If he ever went out into the jianghu, he'd take just two things: a flute and a sword. The sword to spar. The flute to play after winning, and to tell stories. Stories he heard, stories he lived.

"And who would you tell them to?"

"Doesn't matter who hears them. What matters is the story itself! But I can tell you one thing—it sure won't be Miss Shen. I really don't like her."

When the automaton and the Sky Shuttle, having weathered the vast world, finally meet at the summit, do they recall the mutual respect of a passing glance? Do they marvel at a chance meeting once glimpsed only in a dream?
Their dreams are beyond our ken, yet it is through them that we realize what once existed only in ours.
As we gaze toward distant horizons, let us not forget to sleep well and dream a good dream.

zh: 野山参被誉为百草之王，最早的文字记载出现于《神农本草经》中。古人认为野山参能“补五脏之不足，安精神，定魂魄，止惊悸，除邪气，明目开心”。唐代诗人皮日休曾以诗答谢赠予自己山参的友人：神草延年出道家，是谁披露记三桠。开时的定涵云液，劚后还应带石花。名士寄来消酒渴，野人煎处撇泉华。从今汤剂如相续，不用金山焙上茶。
en: Wild ginseng is revered as the "King of Herbs," with its earliest textual records appearing in  "Shen Nong's Compendium of Herbs". Ancient practitioners believed it could "tonify weakened organs, calm the spirit and mind, relieve palpitations, and improve immunities and eyesight while reducing depression". Tang poet Pi Rixiu once wrote a poem thanking a friend who gifted him wild ginseng: "Leafy cap above dewy mound, cloudy bloom and crystal-bound; On silver plate or in earthen pot, help yourself and worry not!"

许多年前，原初菩提根还只是一棵平平无奇的菩提树，菩提苦海还不是一片沼泽，六猫神僧还不叫六猫神僧，猫儿也听不懂经书。
罪业塔发生了那场浩劫，逃出的老僧来到菩提树下，回望来时的苦海，不知前路在何方，忽闻喵声糯糯，转头见树洞中有六只未睁眼的幼猫挤作一团。老僧潸然泪下。
苦海依旧无涯，但树下却多了一名老僧，与六只长尾巴的小施主。
en:
Many years ago, the original Bodhi Root was just an ordinary tree. And the Bodhi Sea wasn't a swamp. The Six Cats Monk wasn't a monk yet, and cats couldn't understand sutras yet. 
When disaster struck the Pagoda of Karma, an old monk fled and came to the Bodhi Tree. Looking back across the bitter sea, uncertain of the path ahead. Suddenly he heard a soft meow, he turned and found six newborn kittens curled together inside a hollow. The monk shed silent tears. 
The Bitter Sea remained endless. But now beneath the tree sat one old monk, and six tiny, long-tailed disciples.

zh:
崽崽自认为是只顶顶聪明的小狗，因为它有很多本领：会摇尾巴，会找骨头，会刨土，还会汪汪叫。
最近，有个女人收养了它。崽崽觉得女人收养了自己这只聪明狗，肯定会笑得合不拢嘴。
可女人却哭了——在它渴了喝脏水的时候，在它熟练地钻进在垃圾堆里找骨头的时候。
崽崽不明白她为什么流眼泪，赶紧把找到的骨头叼过去，放到她脚边。
主人擦擦眼泪，摸着它的头，终于笑了。
崽崽蹭着她的手心，明白了，原来它的主人是饿了！
en:
Cub considers himself an extremely clever dog. He has many talents: wagging his tail, finding bones, digging holes, and barking properly.
Recently, a woman adopted him. Cub figures this woman must be overjoyed to adopt such a clever dog.
But the woman cries when he drinks dirty water when thirsty, when he expertly digs through trash for bones.
Cub doesn't understand her tears. He quickly fetches the bone he found and places it at her feet.
She wipes her eyes, strokes his head, and finally smiles.
Cub rubs against her palm and understands that his owner must be hungry!

zh:
宫中的花十分娇贵，要日日打理照料，浇水、捉虫，保暖，样样离不得人。而这样琐碎的步骤，对太后娘娘来说，倒是每日消遣时光的乐趣之一。那时，太后娘娘的身体还算康健。
在众多花卉中，太后娘娘更喜爱又红又艳的牡丹，她说这花开得极精神，又大又饱满，颜色更是亮眼极了，瞧着便心生喜爱。因此，太后娘娘每每起了兴致插花，都会先寻一朵牡丹。
不过那日，先被挑出来的是一朵开得极大的山茶花，那是官家挑的。太后娘娘瞧见官家与府尹大人来了升平楼，便让两人也一块陪她插插花、聊聊天。问到官家为何选了这朵，他便说这花开得同他脸一样大，定是相当珍贵，理应选它。于是山茶占了花瓶正中，让人一眼便能瞧个正着。
太后娘娘呢，她也不须想，伸手便挑了几朵最爱的牡丹，环绕在山茶的四周，仿若一个怀抱。
最后，这插花雅事里，就剩下府尹大人未选花了。府尹大人瞧了瞧被饱满艳丽花束盛得八分满的花器，就着它缓缓绕了一圈，似是轻轻皱了皱眉，又叹了口气，这才挑起花来。
府尹大人挑得极细，品种、色泽、乃至枝长都要一一看过。官家还亲自举荐了几枝他中意的芍药，也未见府尹大人选中。倒是太后娘娘不紧不慢，府尹大人拿不准的花束，也会帮忙看上一眼。
大抵过了一刻钟，一枝白梅被府尹大人挑了出来。那白梅是在密室用汤气久熏才开，又细又长，颜色像雪，模样也像，仿佛只摇一摇，那白梅便也会摇摆着落入人的掌中。不过，哪怕府尹大人在花器边上又转了一圈，才将这枝白梅装入牡丹的怀抱中，在高处慢悠悠地晃着，那白雪也未曾落下。
就这样，经由三人之手，山茶、牡丹与白梅难得地组成了一束花。若说三者是否各具风格，相差甚远，确实如此。可这三者放在一块，却也从不相冲，倒是格外融洽。只是这样的好光景，后来便没有了。
en:
The flowers in the palace are exceedingly delicate and have to be tended every day. Watering, picking off insects, and keeping them warm...not one of these tasks could be left unattended. Yet for Her Majesty the Empress Dowager, such small, fiddly chores were one of the ways she liked to pass the time. At that time, her health was still fairly sound.

Among all flowers, Her Majesty was especially fond of peonies in the brightest, richest reds. She said they bloomed with such spirit, full and generous in form, with colors so vivid they delighted her at once. And so, whenever she took a fancy to flower arranging, she would always begin by choosing a peony.

That day, however, the first flower selected was a large camellia in full bloom. It was chosen by His Majesty. When Her Majesty saw that His Majesty and the Prefect had come to Shengping Tower, she bade the two of them join her in arranging flowers and passing the time in conversation. When she asked His Majesty why he had chosen that bloom, he replied that it was as big as his face, which surely meant it must be something precious, and so it ought to be chosen. Thus, the camellia took the center of the vase, where it would catch the eye at once.

As for Her Majesty, she had no need to deliberate. She simply reached out and selected several of her favorite peonies, placing them around the camellia like they were embrace it.

At the end of this elegant pastime, only the Prefect had yet to choose a flower. He looked at the vessel, already nearly full with those lush, brilliant blooms, and slowly circled it once. He frowned, then gave a quiet sigh before finally making his choice.

The Prefect chose with the greatest care. He examined each flower one by one, considering the variety, the color, even the length of the stem. His Majesty even personally recommended several cuttings of peonies he was particularly taken with, yet the Prefect chose none of them. Her Majesty, by contrast, remained entirely unhurried, and whenever the Prefect found himself uncertain about a bloom, she would offer her opinion as well.

After about a quarter of an hour, the Prefect selected a single stalk of white plum blossom. That plum blossom had been coaxed into bloom by prolonged exposure to warmth in a heated chamber. Slender and fine, white as snow and almost as delicate as snow, it seemed as though the lightest shake would send petals fluttering down. Yet even after the Prefect circled the vase once more before finally setting that stalk of white plum blossom into the embrace of the red peonies. It swayed gently while towering high above, but it never fell apart.

And so, by the hands of the three of them, camellias, peonies, and plum blossoms were brought together into a unique arrangement. If one were to say that each had its own beauty and that those beauties differed greatly, that would be true enough. Yet set together, they did not clash in the least, and instead seemed to rest in singular harmony. Only, such a pleasing scene was never seen again.
Xi Mingqi
Huang Chuan

zh: 少年张淮深拜入狂澜时，庭前秋梧正披霜。其师郭怀烈将一把陌刀放在他的手里：先练陌刀，再言学枪。 淮深愕然——师父以长枪威震河西，为何要他练这形如门板的兵刃？ 然师命如山，自此夜夜对月挥刀，寒暑不辍。 百日晨昏后，刀势初成。郭怀烈召淮深入狂澜英烈阁——案前供一柄残刀，刃口倒卷如败鳞，旁置半副残甲。 "昔年，安西孤军困守绝城，郭昕将此陌刀残刃、安西铁甲交予我门祖师。——凌振于绝域，烈切于昔贤。" 淮深方知此陌刀法源自安西军，劈砍之势暗含军阵轮转，强敌铁骑亦难挡其锋。 自此淮深愈加勤勉，刻苦练刀。每练劈风式，总觉列阵喊杀声萦耳；研回旋斩时，又似见沙场狼烟迎面而来。 淮深将此心得感悟化入刃势，新招旧式融会贯通——及至主掌归义军，亲训陌刀队百余悍卒，每逢战前必再三吟诵："誓守山河，百死不悔。" 张淮深创此武学，狂澜弟子循习至今。承安西忠魂，守疆域；铸归义锐魄，护生民。 碧血丹心，百代未易。

师兄亲启：

伏惟珍重。
en:
Dear Elder Brother,

Lately, Chang'an is rife with gossip and mockery, all saying that a disciple of the Masked Troupe came to his end in a common brawl with street ruffians. Even our own records note your passing as "death in a street fight."
You lived your whole life with straightforward honor, and yet now you are left to be misread and sneered at by all. Though I know the truth of your staged death, I cannot rid my heart of the grief and indignation it has left there. You did what you did to recover the treasure taken away by the Prince of Wuwei, and you did it to save the world from ruin.
My illness grows heavier by the day, and I feel myself fading. In the idle fears that come with sickness, I find myself thinking: if you should one day return and find both the Master and me already gone, who will be left to speak for you and clear your name? I ask that you keep this letter, Elder Brother. Should the day come when you need it, let these words stand in my place and bear witness to your loyal heart.
I pray you keep well and take care.

zh:
泰山之巅，水陆十八道高手皆聚于此，却俱是满面乌云。只因这一年之中，武林已遭两大惊天祸事。
其一，乃年初之时，武林盟主宇文岳一家老小，与其庄中护卫上下一百余口，一夜之间尽数被戮，无一活口。
其二，乃不久之前，天河高家家主高群被一忽然现身的白发妖人一掌穿心，当场身陨。那白发妖人疯疯癫癫，却有一身诡异武功。高家剩余高手将其团团围住，仍奈何他不得，被他以浑厚掌力破围而出，不知所踪。
两庄惨案，皆有江湖名宿惨死，一时间江湖人人自危。若两桩惨案，皆是那白发妖人所为，真真可称魔头！
陆缘乃一云游四方的墨家门徒，站在那一群高手之间，轻轻敲了敲自己一路背来的机关巨匣。
“那魔头，不会是你吧？”
匣子里头，正是陆缘前些时日救下的一昏迷白发病人。因其白发招摇，故藏于匣中。
初时匣中无声，待高手们又谈论许久之后，病人却忽然逼音成线，传于陆缘耳中。
“你先行离开，我有要杀之人。”
陆缘大吃一惊，自己竟真救下那魔头。正欲劝阻，魔头已破匣而出。只见他抓向人群中一人，只一爪，便了断了那人性命！
山巅高手群聚而起，围攻向那魔头，竟一时拿之不下！
“那墨家子弟与其同行，定然有鬼，先拿她一问！”
本已杀出重围的白发魔头听闻此言，竟重返杀阵，将陆缘护住，拼出一身伤口，杀出重围。
是夜，至一破落庙宇。陆缘怒斥那白发魔头，怎可滥杀无辜。谁知白日所向无敌的魔头，闻言竟只落泪不语。见魔头身上皆是为救自己所留之上，陆缘心下不忍，只好问其缘由。
“我说了，你便信吗？”
白发魔头自知如今自己形貌与常人有异，只觉那陆缘未必肯信。
————————欲知后事如何，且听下回分解——————————
en:
At the summit of Mount Tai, eighteen masters across the jianghu have gathered, their brows all knit in a grim gloom, for within this single year, the jianghu has been rocked by two brutal calamities.
First was the massacre of the Martial Alliance Chief, Yuwen Yue. His entire kin, along with over a hundred estate guards, were slaughtered overnight. Not a soul was left alive.
Then came the fall of Gao Qun, Master of the Tianhe region. A white-haired wraith appeared from nowhere and pierced his heart with a single palm-strike, killing him instantly. The white-haired madman seemed possessed by insanity, yet his martial prowess was as erratic as it was lethal. Though the remaining Gao warriors surged forward to hem him in, he shattered their formation with a surge of inner power and vanished without a trace.
With renowned luminaries falling in both slaughters, a shadow of dread has fallen over the jianghu; every warrior now fears for their own life. Should both atrocities be the handiwork of that white-haired fiend, he is nothing less than a demon incarnate!
Lu Yuan, a wandering disciple of the Mohist, stands amidst the giants. She gives a soft, rhythmic tap to the massive mechanical case strapped to her back:
"That demon... could it be you?"
Hidden within that case is the unconscious, white-haired patient she pulled from the brink of death days ago. His snow-white hair is too conspicuous, forcing her to conceal him within the device...
At first, the casket was silent. But after the others whispered for some time, the patient suddenly channeled his voice into a focused thread of sound, vibrating directly into Lu Yuan's ear:
"Leave now. There is a life I must take."
Lu Yuan is stunned. She has actually rescued the very demon. Before she can utter a word of protest, the demon erupts from the case. With a predatory lung, his fingers curve into a claw, snaring a man from the crowd. A single strike, and the life is snuffed out.
The masters spring to their feet and launch their attack, yet none can bring him down!
"That Mohist girl is his accomplice! There's foul play here. Seize her for questioning!"
Hearing that, the white-haired demon, who has already broken through the siege, plunges back into the lethal fray to shield Lu Yuan. Drenched in fresh blood and braving a rain of blades, he carves a path through the encirclement once more.
By nightfall, they find sanctuary within the crumbling walls of a derelict temple. Lu Yuan lashes out at the white-haired fiend, demanding how he could spill the blood of the innocent so ruthlessly. To her surprise, the man who seemed invincible in the daylight now only weeps in a heavy, hollow silence. Seeing the injuries he's suffered protecting her, Lu softens and presses him for an explanation.
"If I were to speak the truth... would you even have the heart to believe me?"
The demon is well aware that his unusual appearance makes it hard for others to trust him.
To find out what happens next, stay tuned for the next episode.

zh:
长兴四年，元月十五
至洛阳孟津，观鱼跃龙门。
冯公曰：“龙门之高，过者寥寥。然水再高一尺当何如？吾等知民之道必当由此而始。”
我知其刻《九经》，开书院之壮举。与其数日论道，更邀我共校蒙书手稿。然每读其蒙学手稿，心中惶然。千载儒学，史可为鉴，广开蒙学，真可使水再高一尺？忽见一蛙跃水而出，泥鳅、玄龟，甚至米虾亦在其列。跃“龙门”者非独鲤也！
心有所感，遂问冯公：“老农听《关雎》，可能穑事？巧匠诵《论语》，可会纺车？”
天下非唯鲤，亦非唯龙门也。启智之蒙，不应只有儒学，可立格物书院，补蒙学之缺，或可使水再高一尺，托万民而上。
此为，启天下人之智以兴天下。
……

天福二年，六月初六
别冯公后，游学数载，求道于民，终有所得。天文地理，百业千行，唯数唯工可为格物之蒙。工者有墨，数者，当不出孤云。不意孤云之辈顽如槁木，甚于墨门。吾心有不忿，遂赴神算试较技，教孤云自堕颜面！
然，此人之题乎？
幸遇小友孟时良，其人亦有知民之志，我二人秉烛夜谈，引为知己，亦算不负此行。
唯惜小友初入孤云……
……

天福三年，六月初五
五月，神算试将至，小友时良已为孤云翘楚，邀我共习算学。
学算月余，叹时良之才，竟已通晓孤云方、粟、广、均四门！
吾心有成算，此番如愿矣。
入夜，邀时良作谢。酒酣之际，以鲁班锁缚之。
有此贤良，何须舍近求远？
汝当与吾共建格物书院也。
en:
15th Day of the First Month, 933 CE
I arrived at Mengjin in Luoyang and watched the fish leap the Dragon Gate.
Master Feng said, "The Dragon Gate stands high, and few make it over. But what if the water were raised another chi? The way to truly reach the people must begin here."
I already knew of his great undertaking, engraving the Nine Classics and founding an academy. We spent several days discussing the Way, and he even invited me to help revise his primers. Yet whenever I read those texts for beginners, I could not shake a sense of unease. Confucian learning has endured for a thousand years, and history may indeed bear it out. But if basic learning is opened to all, can Confucian teaching alone really raise the waters another chi?
Then I saw a frog leap from the water. Loaches, black turtles, even tiny river shrimp were there as well. It is not carp alone that can leap the Dragon Gate.
Moved by the thought, I asked Master Feng, "If an old farmer hears the Guan Ju, will it help him work the fields? If a skilled craftsman recites the Analects, will he know how to build a spinning wheel?"
Under Heaven, there are not only carp, nor only the Dragon Gate. The first awakening of the mind should not rest on Confucian learning alone. We could found schools devoted to understanding the world, to make up for what basic learning lacks. Then perhaps the waters truly could be raised another chi, lifting the common people with them.
That is how the minds of all under Heaven may be awakened, and how the world itself may be renewed.
...
6th Day of the Sixth Month, 937 CE
After parting from Master Feng, I spent several years traveling and learning among the people, and in time I gained some understanding. Of astronomy and geography, of the hundred trades and thousand callings, only number and craft can serve as the first lessons in understanding the world. Craftsmen have the Mohists. For the art of numbers, none should surpass Lone Cloud.
Yet to my surprise, the people of Lone Cloud were stubborn as dead wood, even more so than the Mohists. I could not swallow the insult, so I went to the Calculation Exam to test my skill against them and make Lone Cloud lose face.
But what a ridiculous set of questions that was.
By good fortune I met the young Meng Shiliang, who also shared this wish to serve the people. We talked by candlelight deep into the night and became true kindred spirits. In that alone, the journey was not wasted.
Only, it is a pity that young Shiliang had only just entered Lone Cloud...
...
5th Day of the Sixth Month, 938 CE
With the Calculation Exam drawing near, Shiliang, already the finest talent in Lone Cloud, invited me to study mathematics with him. After more than a month, I could only marvel at his gifts. He had already mastered Lone Cloud's four disciplines: field reckoning, grain calculation, excess and deficit, and equitable distribution.
Now I know this can be done. This time, my wish will be fulfilled.
That night, I invited Shiliang out for drinks to thank him. Once the wine had gone to his head, I bound him with a Lu Ban Lock.
With someone this capable before me, why should I search far afield?
You are coming with me to build this school.

五香豆沫在琳琅满目的早餐里简直是自成一派。这种黄绿色稠嘟嘟的豆沫是以黄豆，小米，花椒、茴香等熬制而成。若说它口味重，重不过胡辣汤，清淡又淡不过豆腐脑。它的立身之本是茴香和其他香料的搭配。这饭虽有千百种，但只要坚持自己独特的香气，便总有好这一口的人不辞辛苦的在小巷子里七转八拐的来吃一碗。
en:
14. Spiced Doumo (Bean and Millet Porridge)

Among the endless breakfast options, this spiced doumo stands on its own. It's a thick, yellow-green bowl simmered from soybeans and millet, with Sichuan pepper, fennel, and other aromatics.

It's not as punchy as hulatang, and it's not as delicate as tofu pudding either. What holds it together is the fennel and the way the spices are balanced.

There may be a thousand things to eat, but as long as a dish keeps its own unmistakable aroma, someone will always take the long way through twisting lanes just to find a bowl.

zh:
收缴唐钱之策行与不行，是赵匡胤心头的一大难题。

唐钱入宋自是江南国的司马昭之心，可收缴唐钱岂是易事？唐钱早已是大宋通用钱币之一，一朝禁用收缴，便是从百姓手中夺财，必将引得民怨。若是闲日，倒可补以铜钱，然而荆湖内乱求援，正值战机在即，军费尚有缺口，又如何能够还之百姓？
终究是长痛不如短痛，收缴唐钱而不返还，速取荆湖，直捣江南、蜀地，待到一统后，再还天下财富于民，方是上策。
然而伤民心，便是伤社稷之根基，因此纵是上策，也无人敢宣之于口。

——唯有赵光义站了出来。
目光交汇时，赵匡胤仿佛透过他的眼睛看到了多年前的那个清晨，年幼的弟弟摇头晃脑地跟自己重复着那句他深信不疑的话——
“大仁，则必舍小义。在其位，谋其政。”
en:
Whether or not to implement the Tang Coin Confiscation Policy weighed heavily on Zhao Kuangyin's mind.

The circulation of Tang coins in Song territory was no secret, a strategic move by Jiangnan to maintain influence. But confiscating them was no simple task: Tang coins had become a backbone of Song currency. Banning them overnight would amount to stripping wealth from the people, sure to ignite resentment. In peacetime, replacing them with Song copper coins might soften the blow, but with internal rebellions in Jinghu demanding immediate military response and war funds still lacking, how could the court afford to reimburse citizens?
Ultimately, Zhao Kuangyin concluded that long-term pain was preferable to prolonged crisis. Confiscating Tang coins without reimbursement would secure quick victories in Jinghu, followed by campaigns to conquer Jiangnan and Shu. Only after unification could wealth be restored to the people, a harsh but necessary strategy.
Yet no one dared voice this plan aloud, for harming public trust risked undermining the dynasty's foundation.

—Except Zhao Guangyi. As their eyes met, Zhao Kuangyin was transported back to a dawn years prior, when his young brother had earnestly repeated the creed he held dear:
"Great benevolence requires sacrificing small virtues. To hold power is to bear its responsibilities."

zh:
慈心镇，地处璧泉山以西。旧名石工镇，民以采石为生。唐开元年间，上于石工镇畔设法华禅院，藏经纶千卷。有杨姓巧匠率弟子不远万里而来，落脚石工镇，往返镇落与禅寺间，耗时经年，阅佛法经纶，塑佛雕万千，凡所塑罗汉、观音、菩萨石像，兼具雕工与神韵，时人称道。石工镇由此更名慈心镇。
自唐以来，慈心镇民以佛雕为业。然前朝禁绝佛教，佛雕由盛转衰，已数年矣。今至慈心镇，徒见旧佛倾倒，没于荒草，苔痕染绿，不复旧日宝相庄严。诸佛雕师亦不知星散何处，石场尽芜，雕坊空寂，唯有数十土人昼夜颠覆，于镇内外遍植怪花，以自身饲之，行止诡异，令人毛骨惧耸。
en:
West of Jadebrook Mountain lies Mercyheart Town, once called Stonemason Town, where the people made their living by quarrying stone.
During the Kaiyuan era of the Tang Dynasty, the emperor established the Fahua Temple on the town's outskirts, enshrining thousands of Buddhist scriptures. A master sculptor surnamed Yang arrived from afar with his disciples, settling in the town. For years, they journeyed between the quarry and the monastery, studying the sutras, sculpting countless stone figures. Arhats, Guanyin, and bodhisattvas flowed from their chisels, each statue imbued with both exquisite detail and divine spirit. Their work was praised throughout the land, and so Stonemason Town came to be known as Mercyheart Town.
For generations thereafter, the townsfolk made their livelihood through Buddhist sculpture. But in the last dynasty, with Buddhism banned, the craft fell into decline. Now, upon entering Mercyheart Town, one sees only toppled statues buried in wild grass, moss creeping over faces once radiant with sacred grace. The master sculptors are long gone—scattered, forgotten. The quarries are choked with weeds; the carving halls echo with silence.
Only a few dozen villagers remain. Day and night, they move through the town with strange purpose, planting grotesque flowers in every corner. They nourish them with their very flesh. Their presence, their rituals—unnatural. The sight alone chills the blood.

《玉篇》有云，“骁勇也。”骠，马行疾貌，又指毛色中夹杂点点斑纹。吐谷浑马中有此纹理者，为青骠。
相传秦时甘陇一带产良马，时称“秦马”。西汉景帝年间，在西北边郡设马苑，养秦马万千，后有吐谷浑人驻牧。《隋书》有云：“吐谷浑有青海，中有小山。其俗至动辄方牝马与其上，言其龙种。尝得波斯草马放入海，因生骢驹，日行千里。”书中所云骢驹即为“吐谷浑马”。
吐谷浑马骨充肌丰，体躯舒展，健而有力，温顺易驯。喜群居，好游走，群马中必有公马为首。耳聪目明，性机敏，记心强，同类相惜，认主不忘。可乘骑，可轻挽，为中原最常见的马种。
en:
As The Jade Book records: "Valiant and brave." The term "biao" describes both a swift gallop and a coat marked with speckled patches. Among Tuyuhun Horses, such markings define the Qingbiao - Azure Dappled Courser. 
Legend holds that during the Qin dynasty, the fertile lands of Ganlong produced exceptional steeds known as "Qin Horse." In the reign of Emperor Jing of the Western Han, a vast imperial stud farm was founded in the northwest to raise thousands of these horses. Later, the Tuyuhun people came to pasture here. The Book of Sui recounts: "Tuyuhun lies near Qinghai, where stands a small sacred hill. They believe dragons mate with mares atop it, thus their horses are of dragon blood. It's said a Persian grass-fed stallion once swam across the sea, and sired a dappled colt that ran a thousand miles a day." This legendary colt is known as the Tuyuhun Horse. 
Broad of chest and smooth of frame, the Tuyuhun Horse is powerful, yet gentle and easy to tame. Fond of roaming in herds, it always follows a lead stallion. With keen ears and sharp eyes, it is intelligent and loyal, and bonding closely with its kin. It is well-suited for riding and light draft work, and is among the most common breeds in the Central Plains.

zh: 斗草为中国民间游戏，斗草又称斗百草 ，南北朝时称“踏百草”，唐代称“斗草”或“斗百草”。是一种由采草药衍生而成的民间游戏。斗草有“文斗”与“武斗”两种主要形式。“文斗”即对花草名，以对仗形式互报草名，多者为赢；“武斗”则是以草茎或叶柄相勾，互相拉拽，断者为输。
en: Originating from the ancient practice of foraging for medicinal herbs, stem tugging is a beloved traditional Chinese folk game. First known as "Stepping on a Hundred Grasses" during the Northern and Southern Dynasties, it evolved into its classic, enduring form during the Tang Dynasty. The game was traditionally played in two distinct ways: a "literary battle" and a "martial battle." The literary variation was a battle of wits and botanical knowledge, where players competed by trading the names of flowers and herbs in matching poetic couplets. The one who could recite the most emerged victorious. The martial variation, on the other hand, was a physical test of strength. Players would cross and hook the tough stems of grasses or leaves together and pull. The first to have their stem snap was declared the loser.

zh:
郎君展信安：

   展笺之日，妾已乘扁舟离杭，烟波千里，不复返矣。前日有江宁客至，许妾荣华安稳。辗转反侧，思虑累日，至昨日方决。此去，为妾一身计，亦为郎君计。

   郎君乃赤诚之人，日日寻借口前来只为一见，其心欲盖，其情弥彰。故那日奴笑问，何不另寻他法，保全自家颜面？彼时正雨，檐下水帘如织，郎君立于阶上无言良久，次日复来如常。

  然妾之一生，如坠罗网，此身锦绣皆为谎言织就。所谓高门贵女，是假；所谓心性淡泊，喜雅爱兰，是假；善结同心结者也是身边婆婆而非妾身，此事又为一假；所谓只见知音、不理俗客更是假。若无连篇谎言傍身，怎能在这杭州城中出头，结识世家子弟，好飞上枝头变凤凰，一改贱命。

    妾本不堪，实不配郎君深情。郎君心性纯良，才思过人，当潜心向学，他日金榜题名，成一方人物。莫为儿女私情，误了前程。

    （信的中间被烧焦，还有一些暗红色的痕迹，无法识别）
    ……万勿以妾为念……

    （信的中间被烧焦，还有一些暗红色的痕迹，无法识别）
    柳郎呵……万万盼你……
en:
My dear,

By the time you read this, I will have left Hangzhou by boat. I shall travel far, and I will not return. A man from Jiangning recently offered me a life of comfort and security. I spent days thinking it over and nights unable to sleep. Yesterday, I finally made my decision. I am leaving for my sake, and for yours.

You have always been so sincere. Every day, you found some excuse to visit, just to see me. The harder you tried to hide your feelings, the more obvious they became. That was why I teased you that day, asking whether you couldn't find some less embarrassing way to do this. It was raining, water pouring from the eaves. You stood on the steps for a long time without a word. The next day, you came back as usual.

But I have trapped myself in lies. Everything you see, right down to my fine clothes, is part of the deception. I am not the daughter of a noble family. I am not some unworldly soul devoted to art and orchids. Even the union knots are the old woman's work, not mine. And my claim that I receive only kindred spirits and turn away ordinary visitors? Another lie. Without these stories, how could I have made a name for myself in Hangzhou? How could I have met the sons of wealthy families and hoped to escape the life I was born into?

I do not deserve your devotion. You are kind and gifted. Apply yourself to your studies, pass the examinations, and make something of yourself. Do not throw away your future for me.

(The middle of the letter is scorched and marked with dark red stains. Parts are unreadable.)
...Please, do not think of me...

(The middle of the letter is scorched and marked with dark red stains. Parts are unreadable.)
My dear Liu... more than anything, I hope you...

en:
#YAutumn seed. Gather when dry. Keep high. Keep from damp...#E
Supplementary note added after Sang Yu sought instruction: Seed gathered in winter should likewise be thoroughly sun dried, and always stored in a high place, to guard against ground damp.

#YWinter wheat. Cover with straw. Keep roots safe.#E
Supplementary note added after Tian Mo sought instruction: Wheat kept through the winter should be covered with dry straw. This protects the roots from frost and helps hold the warmth in the soil.

#YThird month sow. Fourth month plant out. Fifth month weed. Sixth month clear channels. Seventh month water. Eighth month change water. Ninth month dry field.#E
Supplementary note added after Tang Wenyao sought instruction: In Hebei Circuit, sowing is mostly done in the third month. In the fourth and fifth months, the seedlings are transplanted. Once the roots have hardened, the weeds must be cleared regularly. In the sixth month, the channels are opened to keep enough water in the fields. By the eighth month, the water level may be alternated between high and low. In the ninth month, the fields are dried and the grain brought in.

#YLiu Sinong's note: Well written.#E

zh: 其中有一位人称五公，熟记诗文，掌故精熟。舣舟湖东，谓此处乃前朝李泌引西湖水所开之井，甘泉入户，今有余泽。移船湖北，湖光如镜，芙蓉千叠，有长堤横卧如玉带，四围石砌，道中铺沙，夹种桃柳。此乐天相公所遗，"绿杨阴里白沙堤"也。仰观则又有峰岫峥嵘，幽僻出尘，唤作葛岭，晋人抱朴子葛洪炼丹于此。继而转西，苍山交横，流泉千缕。下饮平湖，上接云脚，郁郁葱葱，如浮屠展臂，灵隐诸峰也。诗仙太白曾游其间，有"天竺森在眼，松风飒惊秋。览云测变化，弄水穷清幽"之诗。
en: It was on one such skiff that I met Elder Wu, a boatman whose mind overflowed with poetry and ancient lore. Guiding us to the eastern shore, he told the tale of Li Mi, a figure from a bygone dynasty who drew from the lake to carve out six wells. Even now, that sweet spring water nourishes the common folk, a blessing that has outlasted empires. As we drifted north, the lake smoothed into a sheet of glass, dappled with unfurling lotus blossoms. A long causeway spanned the water like a ribbon of carved jade. Paved with sand, bordered by stone, and sheltered by peach blossoms and weeping willows, this was the White Sand Causeway. It is the very path bequeathed to us by Bai Juyi, immortalized in his verse: "The white sand causeway veiled in the shade of weeping willows." Looking up, we beheld soaring, ethereal peaks that seemed entirely untethered from the mortal world. This was Ge Ridge, where the alchemist Ge Hong once forged his alchemical elixirs. As we drifted farther west, a rich tapestry of overlapping emerald slopes and winding streams unfolded before us. Spring water cascaded from the heights to meet the placid lake, while the verdant ridges stretched out like the welcoming arms of a grand stupa. These were the peaks of Lingyin. When the Poet Immortal, Li Bai, wandered through these very hills, he wrote: "The Indian deep forests rise before my eyes, as sighing pine winds wake the autumn skies. I watch the shifting clouds to fathom how they sweep and trace the quiet waters, still and deep."

zh:
昔有五百猕猴，游行林中。俱至大树下，树下有井，井中有月影现。
时猕猴主见是月影，语诸伴曰：
“月今日死，落于井中，当共出之，莫令世间长夜暗冥。”
共作议言：云何能出？时猕猴主言：我知出法。我捉树枝，汝捉我尾。展转相连，乃可出之。时诸猕猴，即如主语，展转相捉。树弱枝折，一切猕猴堕井水中。
en:
Once there were five hundred monkeys wandering through the forest. Together they came to a great tree. Beneath the tree was a well, and in the well appeared the reflection of the moon.
When the monkey chief saw the moon's reflection, he said to the others:
"The moon has fallen into the well and perished. We must rescue it together and not let the world be plunged into endless darkness."
The monkeys discussed it among themselves, saying, "How can we get it out?"
Then the monkey chief said, "I know a way. I will grab hold of the tree branch, and you will grab my tail. Then each of you can hold on to the next, one after another. That way we can pull it out."
So the monkeys did exactly as their chief said, each clutching the next in turn. But the branch was too weak and snapped, and all the monkeys fell into the well.

紫色及以上品质装备调律至最高调律等级后可消耗定音石完成定音，获得定音技。
调律词条和定音技依附于装备，更换装备后需要对新装备重新培养。
追忆装备无法进行调律和定音培养。

100阶及以上的紫金品质装备可重置调律，重置后只保留初始词条，可重新调律定音。
弓决、承音和归燕装备无法进行调律重置。
每件装备调律重置都有限次和间隔。
en:
Consume same-tier gear or Tuning Stones to increase your Tuning Level and roll a random Tuning Affix.
Once Epic or higher gear reaches max Tuning Level, spend an Attunement Stone to unlock an Attunement Skill.
Tuning Affixes and Attunement Skills are tied to the gear. If you replace the gear, you'll need to tune and attune the new piece again.
Memoir Gear cannot be tuned or attuned.

Tier 100+ Epic or higher gear can have its tuning reset. After reset, only the initial affixes will remain. Can be tuned or attuned again.
Archery Arts, Relaying, and Swallowcall gear cannot reset tuning.
Tuning resets are limited per gear and have a cooldown.

zh:
——性静情逸，心动神疲。
——岳宗泰岱，禅主云亭。
黑猫的四爪按在这两句话上时，安一飞注视着它绿幽幽的一双眼睛，恍惚间竟然看出几分慈悲。待它矫健跳开，安一飞也不敢强行将它揽回怀中，只是小声嘀咕：“静宗？主动？难道是静宗主神？浮夸，太浮夸了猫猫。”

痴儿，痴儿，又错啦。
此神非彼神。不是神祇之神，而是九命之神。猫有灵性，其命有九，通、灵、静、正、觉、光、精、气、神，如今，已然是它的最后一命了。
每一命的消逝它都不曾后悔，或许也算得上悟道成神呢？
净宗本尊平和地舔了舔爪子。
en:
—When the heart is tranquil, one moves through life with grace and ease; but when the mind is unsettled, the spirit grows weary and burdened.

 
—Throughout the ages, emperors have honored the heavens atop Mount Tai and embraced meditation rituals amidst the serene peaks. 
The black cat pressed its paws onto these words, and in its deep green eyes, An Yifei glimpsed a spark of compassion. But as it leapt away, An wondered if the cat had soul in it. 

Foolish one, foolish one—you've misunderstood. 
Cats carry nine lives, each brimming with essence—intelligence, spirit, tranquility, righteousness, awakening, light, vitality, energy, and soul. Now, this is its final life. 
It never lamented the loss of each precious life; perhaps this is enlightenment itself—the true path to becoming a god. 
Sacred Master calmly licked its paw, serene and wise.

zh:
骄傲的高门公子在中渡桥遭遇了人生第一次失败。
一次失败的劝谏，一次失败的谋划，也是一次失败的，救援。

被杜重威大军兵戈加身，被踩在地上时，
显贵的家族不在他身边，信赖的朋友不在他身边，大儒师父不在他身边，剑，也不在身边。

最后一个老兵救了他。
他惭愧地低下头，低到地里。为他的失败，也为曾经的“志得意满”。
他伏下风度的腰杆，来背起老妇，背起伤员，背起稚童。救人，救更多的人。

后来，十五岁的林险生回到冯道身边。
离开时，他说，百姓如羊群，我为牧羊人，风雨庇护。
回来后，他说，我如牛马，驮负天下，为百姓耕。
他把自己埋进了土里，再站起时，扛着的不是天下，是万民。
en:
The proud noble son met his first failure in life at Zhongdu Bridge.
A failed counsel, a failed plan, and a failed rescue.

Surrounded by Du Chongwei's army and ground into the dirt,
His noble family was not there, his trusted friends were not there, his great luminary and master was not there, and his sword was not there.

At last, an old soldier saved him.
He lowered his head in shame, deep into the earth: for his failure, and for his former self-satisfaction.
He lowered his proud back to carry the elderly, the wounded, and the children. Saving people—saving as many as possible.

Later, fifteen-year-old Lin Xiansheng returned to Feng Dao's side.
When he left, he said, "The people are a flock, and I am the shepherd, providing shelter from the wind and rain."
Upon his return, he said, "I am as a beast of burden, carrying the world and plowing for the people."
He buried himself in the soil; when he rose again, he bore not the weight of the realm, but the weight of the masses.

【士丧礼第十二】

士丧礼。死于适室，幠用敛衾。复者一人以爵弁服，簪裳于衣，左何之，扱领于带；升自前东荣、中屋，北面招以衣，曰：“皋某复！」三，降衣于前。受用箧，升自阼阶，以衣尸。复者降自后西荣。
楔齿用角柶。缀足用燕几。奠脯醢、醴酒。升自阼阶，奠于尸东。帷堂。
乃赴于君。主人西阶东，南面，命赴者，拜送。有宾，则拜之。
入，坐于床东。众主人在其后，西面。妇人侠床，东面。亲者在室。众妇人户外北面，众兄弟堂下北面。
君使人吊。彻帷。主人迎于寝门外，见宾不哭，先入，门右北面。吊者入，升自西阶，东面。主人进中庭，吊者致命。主人哭，拜稽颡，成踊。宾出，主人拜送于外门外。
君使人襚。彻帷。主人如初。襚者左执领，右执要，入，升致命。主人拜如初。襚者入衣尸，出。主人拜送如初。唯君命，出，升降自西阶。遂拜宾，有大夫则特拜之。即位于西阶下，东面，不踊。大夫虽不辞，入也。
亲若襚，不将命，以即陈。庶兄弟襚，使人以将命于室，主人拜于位，委衣于尸东床上。朋友襚，亲以进，主人拜，委衣如初，退，哭，不踊。彻衣者，执衣如襚，以适房。
为铭，各以其物。亡，则以缁长半幅，<赤巠>末长终幅，广三寸。书铭于末，曰：“某氏某之柩。」竹杠长三尺，置于宇西阶上。

en:
【The Twelfth Book of the Mourning Rites: The Mourning Rites of a Scholar-Official】

The mourning rites for a scholar-official. When he dies in the main chamber, he is covered with the burial shroud. One summoner, wearing the dark ceremonial cap and robes, pins the skirt to the upper garment, carries it over his left shoulder, and tucks the collar into his sash. He ascends from the front eastern eave, reaches the center of the roof, faces north, and waves the garment, calling out: "Alas, O so-and-so, return!" Three times he calls, then lowers the garment from the front. It is received in a basket, and he descends by the eastern steps to lay the garment over the corpse. The summoner then descends from the rear western eave.
The teeth are wedged apart with a horn ladle. The feet are secured with the swallow-feast table. Offerings of dried meat, pickled vegetables, and sweet wine are set out. They are carried up the eastern steps and placed to the east of the corpse. The hall is then screened off.
Thereupon, the death is announced to the ruler. The chief mourner stands to the east of the western steps, facing south, to dispatch the messenger, and bows to see him off. If there are guests, he bows to them as well.
He then enters and sits to the east of the bed. The other male relatives stand behind him, facing west. The women sit flanking the bed, facing east. Close kin remain in the chamber. The other women stand outside the door, facing north, and the other brothers stand below the hall, facing north.
The ruler sends a messenger to offer condolences. The screen is removed. The chief mourner goes out to meet him outside the inner gate. Seeing the guest, he does not weep but enters first and stands to the right of the gate, facing north. The mourner enters, ascends by the western steps, and faces east. The chief mourner advances to the middle of the courtyard, and the mourner delivers the ruler's message. The chief mourner weeps, bows with his forehead to the ground, and performs the leap of grief. The guest departs, and the chief mourner bows to see him off outside the outer gate.
The ruler sends a messenger to present grave goods. The screen is removed. The chief mourner acts as before. The presenter holds the collar in his left hand and the waist in his right, enters, ascends, and delivers the message. The chief mourner bows as before. The presenter enters, lays the garments on the corpse, and departs. The chief mourner bows to see him off as before. Only on the ruler's command does he go out, ascending and descending by the western steps. He then bows to the guests; if there are high officials, he bows to each individually. He takes his position below the western steps, facing east, and does not leap. Even if the high officials do not decline, he enters.
If close kin present grave goods, they do not send a messenger but bring them directly to the display. If younger brothers present them, they send someone to announce it in the chamber, and the chief mourner bows in his place, and the garments are laid on the bed to the east of the corpse. If friends present them, they come forward in person, and the chief mourner bows; the garments are laid as before, and they withdraw, weeping but not leaping. Those who remove the garments take them up as when they were presented and carry them to the side chamber.
For the inscription banner, each is made according to one's rank. If there is none, then black cloth is used, half a breadth in length, with a red hem at the end a full breadth in length and three inches wide. The inscription is written on the end: "The bier of so-and-so of such-and-such clan." The bamboo pole is three feet long and is placed to the west of the eaves by the steps.
The field officer digs a pit between the steps, slightly to the west. A furnace is built beneath the western wall, facing east. New basins, trays, jars, a discarded earthenware vessel, and a set of tripod cauldrons are all washed and placed below the western steps.
The garments for dressing the corpse are laid out in the side chamber, with the collars facing west, arranged from south to north, not in a continuous fold. The bright garment is made of cloth. The hairpin is of mulberry wood, four inches long, with a cord through the middle. The cloth kerchief is a full breadth in circumference, without an opening. The face cover is of fine white silk, a full breadth in width and five feet long, with the ends split. The ear plugs are of white floss silk. The eye cover is of black silk, one foot two inches square, with a red lining, stuffed, and fastened with cords. The hand coverings are of dark silk with a light red lining, one foot two inches long and five inches wide, with a seam allowance of one inch at the sides, stuffed, and fastened with cords. The thumb ring is of fine jujube wood or wild jujube wood, with a cord fastening, and two floss silk pads. The shroud has a dark upper part, reaching level with the hands, and a red lower part that covers the feet. The dark cap and robes, plain garments, the leather cap and robes, the unlined robe, the dark sash, the red knee cover, and the bamboo tablet. In summer, hemp sandals; in winter, white shoes, all with embroidered edges, dark toe caps and trims, and cord fastenings attached at the heels. Grave goods presented by others are laid out in succession but are not used.

zh:
大多时候，慕容延钊已经糊涂了，但勉强清醒的某个瞬间，他的眼前偶尔会出现很多奇怪的人。
与旧友结伴纵马的少年，意气风发的将士，戎马天下的将军，数度陈情的朝臣，苦劝不止的旧友，还有手刃好友的罪人。
奇怪的是，分明衣着不同，神情不同，每一张脸都如此相像，如此熟悉。
那是谁呢？他记不起来了。
终于他低头看见一双苍老又枯槁的手，不像是一个将军的手，也不像是一个壮年之人的手。
这是现在的自己。
那些是过去的自己。

他摆动手脚上的锁链，那刺耳的声响有时是去往清醒的钥匙，有时叩开的是昏聩的门，他为何会在这里呢？他偶尔忘记，又偶尔想起，他听见那些幻影在他面前走过，他们对他说。
“你既不够忠，又不够友，因此你沦落至此。”
“你既不够勇，也不够惧，因此你步步行错。”
“你既然杀了他，就不该放不下他，因此你恶疾不退。”
“你既然选了归顺赵宋，就不该还为友人求情，你若是选了友人，便不该归顺赵宋。”
“你是自己将自己送在了锁链之中。”
他听出了，那人是他自己。

原来是他活该至此！原来是他活该至此！
坐在轮椅之间，那具曾经只在战场上因伤而涌出鲜血的身体里，涌出一滴又一滴泪来。
en:
Most of the time, Murong Yanzhao was muddled, but in rare moments of clarity, strange figures would flicker before his eyes.
A youth riding freely with old friends, a high-spirited soldier, a general who'd conquered battlefields, a courtier pleading tirelessly, a persistent old friend begging him to stop, and a sinner who'd slain a friend.
Oddly, though they wore different clothes and bore different expressions, every face looked strikingly alike, hauntingly familiar.
Who were they? He couldn't recall.
Finally, he looked down at his own aged, withered hands, no longer those of a general, nor of a man in his prime.
This was the present him.
Those were the past hims.

He rattled the chains on his wrists and ankles. Sometimes the harsh clatter unlocked clarity. Other times, it opened the door to delirium. Why was he here? He forgot, then remembered, as the phantoms paced before him, speaking with his own voice:
"You were neither loyal enough nor a true friend, thus you fall to this."
"You were neither brave enough nor fearful enough, thus every step was a mistake."
"If you killed him, you should not cling to him, thus your illness lingers."
"If you choose to submit to the Song court, you should not plead for your friend. If you chose your friend, you should not have submitted."
"You chained yourself here."
He recognized the voice. So this was his fate!

He had done this to himself!
Seated in his wheelchair, tears trickled from a body that had once shed only blood on the battlefield.

从什么时候开始的呢……阿然想起来，对了，是那天晚上，有人唱歌的晚上。
有人在唱歌，所以她醒过来，坐在窗边听。
有人在怒吼，所以她朝着声音来的方向探出身，更专注地听。
起风了，叶子刷刷响，才叫回阿然的心神。
然后……然后呢？然后大侠就来啦，街上的叫卖多了，木头的朽味道少了。爹爹回来了！
对了，阿然还没有跟爹爹说过，大侠把金叶子带回来的那天晚上，她做了一个梦呢，梦见——
#Y【开封城】——那是阿然没有“看见”过的开封城，但阿然听见过。真正的开封城，有花开的声音，有人哭的声音，有木头烧起来的声音，也有人拥抱的声音。阿然觉得梦里的那个人说得真对：真正的开封，要用耳朵去听！#E
en:
Zheng Ran noticed that the crackling of fires in Kaifeng City had vanished, and the scorching, acrid smells had faded. When people walked down the streets, the jingle of the coin pouches in their robes sounded somehow fuller and weightier.
When did it begin...? Right, it was that night, the night someone was singing.
That singing woke her, so she sat by the window to listen.
Someone was roaring in anger, so she leaned out toward the sound, listening even more intently.
The wind picked up, and the rustling leaves brought Ran back to her senses.
Then... what happened then? Then the wanderer arrived! The street vendors' cries grew livelier, and the stench of rotting wood faded. Father came home!
Oh, right! Ran still hasn't told Father that on the night the wanderer brought back the gold leaf, she had a dream. She dreamed of...
#Y[Kaifeng City] Ran had never "seen" Kaifeng City, yet she had heard it. The real Kaifeng held the sounds of flowers blooming, of people weeping, of wood crackling in flames, and of arms closing in embrace. Ran thought the person in her dream was absolutely right: You have to listen to the real Kaifeng with your ears!#E

成大夫，之前你说想要治好阿兰的脸，除了要用到我的皮肉，还需要找到那味名为云生花的药草。

en:
Today, Lan looked into the mirror once more. It has been three years; that sudden disaster has tormented her for three long years.
She used to be a girl who loved to laugh so much. Her smile was as radiant as spring blossoms, as pure as the white snow of winter.
But now, all of that is gone.
I love her smile, and I long to see it again, even if I cannot be the one by her side.
Doctor Cheng, you told me before that to heal Lan's face, apart from taking my own flesh, you needed a medicinal herb called Cloudborne Bloom.
Only by consuming the Cloudborne Bloom could Lan endure the sheer agony of having her skin removed.
Now, I have finally found that flower. Doctor Cheng, this time, I beg you to grant my request.

李白元揉了揉鼻子。“老殷家阿郎走得早，他自己病得又重。”
“听说，他们楚地人买椒做饭，大多是为了死前请什么巫咸神享用，好带自己升天。”张尔普见多识广，自是知道其中的门道。
“所以那位阿兄他……”玛依拉担忧地皱起眉。
“放心吧。”李白元摇摇头，擦了擦灶台上的油花。“老殷向来守信，何况，我还给了他别的东西。”
“来，张罗起来吧。烫菜咧——烫菜咧！”

殷松回到家里，打开布袋，却发现里面除了一包秦椒，还有几袋粟米，一些蔬果，以及……一包小心包好的椒种？

他忘了那一顿饭自己是怎么吃下去的，泪水沁透了粟米饭，上面的花椒被热气蒸得喷香。
他小心翼翼地拿出干涸的花盆，盘算着如何将这椒种好好播下。
摆弄半天，殷松挠挠头。
算了，明天还食盒的时候，问问老李吧。

“李阿兄，就这么把椒种给了他？”玛依拉收拾着碗筷，随口问着。
“一把种子，够他寻个营生了。”李白元帮着幺昭布锤着肩膀。
“就像咱一样。”
“对啊，像咱一样。”

神佛不会亲自下凡拯救苦难，但微末的善意却可驱散严寒。
en:
Zhang Erpu watches Yin Song walk away and sighs quietly. 
Li Baiyuan rubs his nose. "The Yin family lost their son young, and now he's seriously ill himself." 
"I hear people from Chu use Sichuan pepper in cooking mostly to offer to some witch-god before they die, hoping to be taken to heaven." Zhang Erpu, well-traveled, knows these customs. 
"So, that brother he..." Mayila frowns with concern. 
"Don't worry." Li Baiyuan shakes his head, wiping grease from the stove. "Old Yin keeps his word. Besides, I gave him something else." 
"Come on, let's get busy. Hot veggies! Careful!" 

Yin Song returned home and opened the cloth bag. Besides a packet of Sichuan pepper, he found several bags of millet, some vegetables and fruits, and... a carefully wrapped packet of pepper seeds? 

He couldn't remember how he ate that meal. Tears soaked the millet rice, the Sichuan pepper on top steamed fragrantly by the heat. 
He carefully took out a dried flowerpot, pondering how best to plant these seeds. 
After fiddling for a long time, Yin Song scratched his head. 
Forget it. I'll ask Li when I return the food box tomorrow. 

"Brother Li, you just gave him the seeds like that?" Mayila asked casually while clearing bowls. 
"A handful of seeds is enough for him to find a trade." 
"Just like us." 
"Yeah. Just like us." 

Gods and Buddhas don't descend to save the suffering, but small acts of kindness can drive away the cold.

阿回和你在天水集里逛得很尽兴。你听着他像一只快乐的小鸟一样叽叽喳喳说个不停，多希望青史能为他停留一刻——不必征战沙场，不必骨肉分离，不必卷入波诡云谲的朝堂斗争，亦不必为了归唐大业献出自己的一生。此刻他就是阿回，那个勇敢的，开朗的，活泼的，有些小机灵的，装作小大人的，把你当做朋友的阿回。
en:
Under the lantern-lit splendor of Skybrim Market, the people remain lost in an endless celebration. Amid the bustling crowd, you spot Hui, who has sneaked out to play again. He sees you too, waves excitedly, and thanks you for helping him buy a lantern last time. This time, he pats his little pouch and invites you to stroll through the market together. It's hard to turn down such a gracious invitation, but where to next?...
#Y[Buy some traditional sweets.] The vendor invites you to try some samples. Not holding back at all, Hui samples every single kind. Just as you take out some extra coins for the vendor, he smiles and refuses, even pressing two more pieces into your hand.#E
You and Hui have a wonderful time strolling through Skybrim Market. Listening to him chatter away like a cheerful little bird, you can't help but wish the annals of history might pause for him just for a moment, sparing him the blood-soaked battlefields, the separation from his family, the treacherous storms of court intrigue, and the life-long burden of restoring the Tang. In this moment, he is simply Hui, a brave, cheerful, lively, and clever boy who pretends to be a grown-up and treats you as a true friend.

zh:
一柄重枪，成了青切磋伤人的罪证。
她自知留了力。只是那满嘴仰慕，惹人厌烦的登徒子借题发挥，给她找事。
恰那家伙的师父多次论败于张万师，此番借故，硬是闹到了长老们跟前。
一番审度下来，众长老决意判青几日禁足。青正欲认了便罢，然张万师一来，便径自带她离开。还道：
“神亏气弱，病在内里。以淤引气，你该道谢。”
“还有，可多挨些打以活气血，不然……命不长久。”
那师徒二人又惊又疑，又不敢不信，哪还顾得上要灭“三杰”的威风？

甫一出门，便见鸦已垂手而待。两只小雀同跟在师兄身后离开。
青：“师兄，你刚刚说的都是真的？”
张万师：“鸦胡诌给我的。”
鸦有些赧色：“咳咳，反正师兄说什么他们都得掂量掂量……”
en:
That heavy spear ended up as "proof" that Halcyon had injured someone during a spar. She knew she'd held back. The man she clipped was an insufferable creep, all fawning praise on his lips, and he seized on the incident to make trouble.
Worse still, his master had lost to Zhang Wanshi more than once, and now he had an excuse to drag the matter before the elders. After some deliberation, the elders decided to confine Halcyon to quarters for a few days.
Halcyon was ready to accept it, but Zhang Wanshi arrived and simply took her away.
"Your vitality's weak, and the problem's internal," he said. "I was just helping your qi move through the blockage. You should be thanking me."
Then he added, dead serious, "And you should take a few more hits to get your blood moving. Otherwise, you won't live long."
The master and disciple were stunned and suspicious, but they did not dare call his bluff. Whatever talk they had about taking down the "Three Paragons" vanished on the spot.
Outside, Raven was already waiting. The two juniors followed behind their senior brother.
"Senior Brother, were you telling the truth just now?" Halcyon asked.
"Raven fed me that line," Zhang Wanshi said.
Raven coughed, looking a little embarrassed. "Well... when Senior Brother says something, they have to think twice, don't they?"

zh:
凉州父老足下：
  
承赐百衲，惶愧难胜。
然诸君所奉非袈裟，实万民补天之帛；所拜非罗汉，乃河西求生之相。  
夫百衲者，非百零八布，实百八苦厄——抄经僧啮指濡墨，赭渍丹书；铜匠焚膏冶洪钟，青熔玄穹；阵亡儿郎骨殖化雪，白浸寒幡；  归义军缨穗泣血，赤缠残戈。
真佛者，非金刚不坏之躯，乃万姓刳心沥血之相。十载浴血，千里裹尸，凉州归唐路，原是十万八千卷无字血经。
仆本河西一戍卒，敢僭佛衣？惟愿诸君续此百色，共绣河山。
en:
To the honored people of Liangzhou,

I stand humbled by your gift of the patchwork robe, my gratitude eclipsed only by my shame, for I am not worthy.
Know this: the robe you have sewn is no garment for a monk. It is the very fabric of our people's will, stitched together to mend the heavens. The icon you bow to is no distant saint. It is the spirit of Hexi itself, forged in suffering, fighting for life.

You call this a robe of a hundred patches, but I see a hundred and eight chronicles of sorrow.
It is the sorrow of the scribe, who, out of ink, bit his own flesh to sanctify the page with blood.
It is the sorrow of the smith, who, in darkness, melted down his very life to cast the temple bell.
It is the sorrow of our sons, whose bones lie like frost upon the plains, their essence bleaching the banners of the dead.
It is the sorrow of the Guiyi Army, whose crimson tassels weep onto broken spears, a testament to their final sacrifice.

True enlightenment is not found in an unbreakable body. It is seen in the face of a people who have given everything. Ten years of bloodshed, a thousand miles of graves. Liangzhou's long road home to the Tang is a sacred scroll, unwritten, yet penned in the lifeblood of our people.

I began as a simple frontier guard. How can I possibly cloak myself in such sanctity? I ask only this: that you continue this work. Continue to weave your colors, your lives, your sorrows and triumphs together, until you have remade the very map of our homeland.

zh:
凡是见过周蔷的人都不会怀疑，这是一朵只有高门贵胄用真金白银才能浇灌出的绝艳牡丹。
“这样的人，为什么会出现在醉花阴呢？”
很多花间客，甚至不少刚入门的弟子都产生过这样的疑惑。他们都觉得，周蔷自出生便拥有的一切，已令她站在了凡俗终其一生也难以企及的地方。
周蔷不曾回答过这个问题。她不喜欢它，因为这个问题会让自己回忆起那场刻骨铭心的宴会。是的，虽然时至今日，周蔷经历过的宴会何时百数，但她印象最深刻的，却还是八岁时的那一场。

那一年是永隆五年，年幼的周蔷随母亲回家乡福州省亲。亲友们为二人准备了风光的宴席，周蔷向来很喜欢宴会，她喜欢雕龙画凤、金碧辉煌的厅堂，更喜欢意料之外又精妙绝伦的歌舞。而那场宴会，也的确出乎了周蔷或者说所有人的预料，——突然闯入的士兵瞬间便血洗了宅院，那些片刻前还高高在上的亲贵富豪，霎时就变得和盘中装饰精美的牲畜肉菜毫无差别。
是一名醉花阴弟子的偶然相助，才令周蔷母女侥幸脱逃。这两朵温室的鲜花为逃出生天而心中庆幸，孰料真正的噩梦才刚刚开始。眼前的福州已因一场兵变而变了模样，一代王朝几乎是在一夜间便土崩瓦解归于云烟。
普通人很难想象，一个肩不能挑、手不能提，除了身份与美貌以外一无所有的女孩，为了走出福州、回到广陵到底经历了什么。去时的路与来时的，明明距离相等，可女孩却觉得这条路是那样长、那样长…… 长到路上经历的一切都令她终生难忘。
于是当年迈的父亲终于搂住失而复得的女儿，年幼的孩子却早已不会哭了。那场宴会、那条归程向她证明，她曾笃信、依靠的东西，世俗眼中的出身、财富、感情…… 都不可靠。周蔷不愿旧事重演，所以她回忆着宴会上唯一功成身退的醉花阴弟子，自己叩响了醉花阴的大门。

九年后，资质过人的周蔷已是上代掌门最得意的亲传；又九年，樊楼楼主的艳名天下皆知。
这十数年间，这方唱罢那方登场，宴会的宾客、主角、地点变了又变，不变的是十丈软红背后的危机四伏、暗流汹涌。——便如今次的这场群英会，无面人名单之事险之又险，稍有差错便是牵动各方的祸事。可是周蔷也变了，她早已不是那个身在局中、任人鱼肉的小女孩了。——她是足以偷天换日、力挽狂澜的醉花阴门主，是整场宴会的操办者、帷幕后的捉刀人。
en:
Anyone who has ever beheld Zhou Qiang would harbor no doubt: she is a peerless peony, nurtured exclusively by the gold and silver of aristocratic houses.
"Why would such a figure appear in Velvet Shade?"
Many patrons of the pleasure quarters, and even novice disciples, have harbored this question. They all believe that the privileges Zhou Qiang possessed from birth should have placed her upon a pedestal forever beyond the reach of common mortals.
Zhou Qiang has never answered this question. She despises it, for it forces her to recall that unforgettable banquet. Indeed, though she has attended hundreds of feasts to this day, the one etched deepest in her memory remains the banquet from her eighth year.
It was the fifth year of the Yonglong era. The young Zhou Qiang accompanied her mother back to their hometown of Fuzhou to visit relatives. The kin prepared a glorious feast in their honor. Zhou Qiang had always loved banquets; she adored the grand halls carved with dragons and phoenixes, the resplendent decor, and above all, the unexpected and exquisite music and dance. That banquet, however, truly exceeded her expectations and those of everyone present. Soldiers suddenly breached the compound, washing the manor in blood within moments. The noble and wealthy, who had been so imperious just a breath before, were instantly reduced to the likeness of the elaborately garnished meats upon their plates.
It was the fortuitous intervention of a Velvet Shade disciple that allowed Zhou Qiang and her mother to escape by a hairsbreadth. These two hothouse flowers rejoiced at surviving, little knowing that the true nightmare had only just begun. The Fuzhou before them had been entirely transformed by mutiny; an entire dynasty had crumbled into smoke and dust almost overnight.
It is difficult for ordinary people to imagine what a frail girl, possessing nothing but her status and beauty, unable to carry a burden or wield a weapon, had to endure to walk out of Fuzhou and return to Guangling. The road back was the exact same distance as the journey there, yet to the girl, it felt infinitely long. It was so long that everything she experienced along the way became seared into her memory for a lifetime.
Thus, when her aged father finally embraced his lost-and-found daughter, the young child had long forgotten how to cry. That banquet and that perilous return journey had proven to her that the things she once firmly believed in and relied upon, such as status, wealth, and worldly affection, were all unreliable. Unwilling to let history repeat itself, Zhou Qiang recalled the lone Velvet Shade disciple who had successfully retreated from that bloody banquet, and she personally knocked upon the gates of Velvet Shade.
Nine years later, the exceptionally gifted Zhou Qiang had become the most favored personal disciple of the previous sect master. Another nine years passed, and the glamorous reputation of the Mistress of Revelry Hall became known throughout the realm.
Over these decades, powers rose and fell, and the guests, protagonists, and venues of the banquets changed time and again. What remained unchanged was the perilous undercurrent and lurking danger hidden beneath the glamorous vanity fair. Take the current Heroes Assembly for instance; the matter of the Faceless Ones' roster is fraught with extreme peril, where the slightest misstep could spark a disaster entangling all factions. Yet, Zhou Qiang has also changed. She is no longer that helpless little girl trapped in the game, at the mercy of others. She is the Master of Velvet Shade, capable of stealing the sky and turning the tide. She is the orchestrator of the entire banquet, the ghostwriter hidden behind the velvet curtain.

zh:
每到深夜，众人睡去，诸葛哈便会挑灯独坐，摊开厚厚的账簿，记下缺口袋的每一笔开销。
他总是要写很久很久，仿佛有很多很多件事，他也会边写边唠叨，仿佛每件事都值得他挂怀。

——支：银二钱，置窣利红绸缎二十尺
“安仔的神仙索越发旧了，这可是吃饭的家伙事儿，旧了也不说一声。”
“天天出去野，也不知道捎个信儿回来，教人成天惦记着！”
诸葛哈念叨着，余光瞥见了手边的竹编小鸟，不由得长叹一口气。 

——支：银五百文，置波斯药酒数壶
“轻轻这个憨货，眼里面像没有自己一样！丢了钱不吭声，挨了看客骂不吭声，身上见了伤还不吭声！”
“下次、下次再磕了碰了，老子绝对不给他买这么贵的药了！”
诸葛哈嘴上发狠，箱子里却塞满了空药瓶。

——支：银三百文，置糖瓜、蛋奶疙瘩、烤羊腿、烫菜……
“这俩猴儿崽子，嘴比谁都馋，见着吃的就走不动道儿！这点家底儿早晚被吃空。”
“算了算了，正是长身体的时候……哼，我当年要是也这么吃，何至于变成矮矬子！”
诸葛哈气得吹了吹胡子，丝毫没注意帐篷外清脆的铃铛响。

他合上账簿，吹了灯，挑着烟斗，径直向外面走去。
见人已走远，两个小小的身影鬼鬼祟祟地溜进了帐篷。
“小银，我打赌，班主肯定把秘密都记在这里头了。”
“账——小金，这个字该怎么念呀？”
“哎呀什么账啊，这是日记……咦？还真是账簿，没劲透了！”
“小银你说，班主是不是一顶一的小气鬼，买点儿吃的他也记着！”
“嗯……班主是小气鬼，小气得怎么都不给自己买一样东西呢。”
金银铃铛空手走了出来，垂头丧气，连铃铛声都闷闷的。
月光如洗，诸葛哈倚在不远处的树上，几乎与树影融在一起。
只有烟斗里的一点猩红，在黑夜里，随着他的呼吸，一明一灭。
他目送着两个小小的身影钻进了自己的小帐篷，四下终于重归寂静。
“小气鬼？哼……老子乐意。”
en:
Every night, after everyone fell asleep, Zhuge Ha would sit alone by the lamp, spread out the thick account book, and record every expense of the "Pocketrupt Circus". 
He would write for a long, long time, as if there were countless things to record. He would also mutter to himself as he wrote, as if every detail was worth caring about. 

——Expense: 2 qian of silver, purchased 20 chi of Sogdian red silk 
"Anzi's Immortal Rope is getting more and more worn out. This is her livelihood, she doesn't even mention it's old." 
"Running around all day, not even sending a message back. Making people worry about her nonstop!" 
Zhuge Ha muttered, and out of the corner of his eye, he saw the bamboo bird beside him, letting out a long sigh. 

——Expense: 500 copper coins, purchased several pots of Persian medicinal wine 
"That fool Qingqing, he never thinks about himself! He doesn't say a word when he loses money, when he's scolded by the audience, or when he gets hurt!" 
"Next time, next time he gets hurt again, I'll definitely not buy him such expensive medicine!" 
Despite his harsh words, his box was filled with empty medicine bottles. 

——Expense: 300 copper coins, purchased sugar melons, Salted Milk Curds, roasted lamb legs, hot pot dishes... 
"These two little monkeys, they're greedier than anyone else! They can't move when they see food! They'll eat up all our savings sooner or later." 
"Forget it, forget it, they're growing. Hmph, if I'd eaten this well when I was young, I wouldn't have ended up so short and stubby!" 
Zhuge Ha huffed, puffing his beard in anger, not noticing the crisp bell ring outside the tent at all. 

He closed the account book, blew out the lamp, picked up his pipe, and walked straight out. 
Once he was far away, two small figures sneaked into the tent. 
"Xiaoyin, I bet the troupe master wrote all his secrets in here." 
"Account... Xiaojin, how do you read this word?" 
"Ugh, it's not a diary... it's an account book... What a letdown!" 
"Xiaoyin, do you think the troupe master is the biggest miser ever? He even writes down every bit of food he buys!" 
"Hmm... He is a miser. So stingy that he never buys anything for himself." 
Jin and Yin Bells walked out empty-handed, dejected, even their bell rings sounded dull. 
The moonlight was bright and clear. Zhuge Ha leaned against a tree not far away, almost blending into the shadow. 
Only the faint red glow of his pipe flickered in the dark night, lighting up and dimming with his breath. 
He watched the two small figures crawl into their own small tent. Finally, silence returned to the surroundings. 
"A miser? Hmph... I'm happy to be one."
