zh:
谢尧的药篓里，装过灵芝，装过乌头，也装过小草。
他相信药本无毒无良，救人者，良药也，害人者，毒药也。
他一向通透，直到药篓里装了一个小姑娘。
那时他也很小，背不动那个人。
后来他长大了，小姑娘也长大了。放不进小背篓，却放在了他的心上。
病人会因重病疼痛迁怒他，因无治之症而辱骂他，因身陷疾苦而威胁他。
他一向豁达，还是一次又一次地伸出援手。
直到死亡带走他的病人。他才会停下。
可他这次停不下了。
他背着他的药篓走了很多路，走过江湖门派，走去剿灭梦傀。
此后余生，他都在走向自己没有赶回去的“邙山”。
他一向固执，他一次又一次地奔波在路上。
直到死亡带走了他。
en:
Xie Yao's woven basket had carried everything from rare spirit mushrooms to deadly aconite and the humblest blades of grass.
To him, herbs possessed neither malice nor virtue. Whatever cured was medicine, and whatever killed was poison.
He had always seen the world with perfect clarity until the day a little girl ended up in his basket.
He was only a child himself back then, barely strong enough to carry her weight.
As the years wore on, the boy and the girl grew up. She outgrew his little backpack, and so she took root in his heart instead.
Patients blinded by agony would lash out at him, hurl insults over incurable blights, or threaten him in their despair.
He was always forgiving, extending his hands again and again.
He would only stop when death finally came to claim his patients.
But this time, he could not stop.
Shouldering that same medicine basket, he walked countless roads. He wandered through the sprawling jianghu sects and plunged into the desperate wars against the Sleeping Puppets.
For the rest of his days, he was endlessly walking toward Mount Mang, the mountain he had failed to reach in time.
Stubborn to the end, he drove himself forward, chasing an impossible horizon.
Until death finally came for him, too.
Amitabha...
Ji Ye Xuan

"Little Monkey, truth be told, there is nothing so wrong with being unlettered, wouldn't you say?"
...
"Little Monkey, when the disciples come of age this year, what say I make a cap for you as well?"

zh:
绳文、绳武兄弟自幼以皮影为生。兄弟二人一唱一武，渐于皮影之中领悟一套大开大合的武学。

契丹入寇时期。与各路豪侠合为八俊，于清河力阻契丹大军。战事艰苦，兄弟二人忽的被战马撞飞，八俊众兄弟亦被乱军冲散；兄弟二人正要回援时，只见到其他兄弟被敌军包围，寡不敌众而捐躯……

如今，兄弟二人于来生岸边，演练皮影，回念起兄弟结义之时，心魔骤起，忍不住呼喝出“行不得也——哥哥！”
en:
The brothers Sheng Wen & Sheng Wu were raised in the art of shadow puppetry. One sang, the other danced the blade. In time, they forged their own unique martial style from the fluidity of puppet play. 

When the Khitans invaded, they stood alongside with other heroes as the Eight Heroes of Qinghe, defending the region shoulder to shoulder. The battle was brutal. The brothers were suddenly flung aside by a stampede of warhorses, and their comrades scattered in the chaos.
They turned back to help, but all they saw were their sworn brothers surrounded, overwhelmed, and cut down... 

Now, the brothers train their puppet play by the Floral Expanse Beyond, haunted by memories of their oath-bound kin.
Dark thoughts rise unbidden, and one of them cries out,
"Don't go down that path, Brother!"

en:
In the stillness of the courtyard, only the soft sound of falling blossoms and the steady flow of water break the silence.
She's cut off from the world beyond the walls, with only the distant laughter of passersby reaching her ears, like a soft breeze that fades away.
No matter how much her tasks grow, they are always completed eventually. The people she might talk to, however, return on no schedule at all. It's the paper "friends" she folds that keep her company through the endless hours of waiting.
This is Bai Chuyu's most treasured paper "friend."
No one knows why it was left beside the well. Perhaps it was meant for someone else...
Just like a version of "herself" untouched by walls, and quietly admired by others.

阿白和阿黑是一道从栾城跑出来的。
阿白担心，自己白白的脸上，要被恶狠狠的坏人刻上字，就不好看了。
于是，阿白拉上阿黑，一起往外逃，可是逃到哪儿才是个头呢？正当阿白还在思考时，迎面遇见了一群急匆匆的栾城人，他们逃了出来，可仍有亲友关在城里。如今的形势是外面的进不去，里面的人逃不出，音讯隔绝，两处茫茫。
这时阿白站了出来，它一身雪白，在晚上很是显眼。若让它吸引坏人的注意，再由阿黑出手，想要报信或是传递些什么物件，这不就是个好法子吗？
阿白看向阿黑，摇摇尾巴，心想：咱们留在这里，还有些用处，那便不逃了。
en:
Snowy and Shadow ran away from Luancheng together.
Snowy was worried that if those cruel villains branded her white face with ink, she wouldn't be pretty anymore.
So, Snowy took Shadow and fled. But where would they go? While Snowy was still thinking, they ran into a group of frantic people from Luancheng. They had escaped, but their family and friends were still trapped in the city. The situation was such that those outside couldn't get in, and those inside couldn't get out; news was cut off, leaving both sides in despair.
Then Snowy stepped forward. She was pure white and very conspicuous at night. If she drew the villains' attention while Shadow acted, wouldn't that be a perfect way to deliver messages or items?
Snowy looked at Shadow, wagged her tail, and thought: We can be of use here, so let's not run anymore.

青不仅坚定，还有着特殊的直觉（知觉），不日，她或可以御剑之法御衍算之阵。
问青，是否觉得“捞月”是笑谈？自述观点，道与术，缺一不可。传承的精神也好，传承的技术也好，都是重要的。前人有“捞月”心，后人才能有机会“摘月”。
en:
The Chamber of Derivation is crucial, determining the future of the Mohist and even humanity. The choice of who to entrust it to is very important.
Crane shared his views on several people: Zhang Wanshi is a genius, Raven carries too much. The final conclusion is that Halcyon is the right person to manage the Chamber of Derivation. Crane has recommended her to Grandmaster Osprey.
Halcyon is not only steadfast but also has a special intuition (awareness). Soon, she may be able to control the calculation formation with her sword-controlling method.
Crane asks Halcyon if she thinks "reaching for the moon" is a joke. Crane states his own view: the Way and its applications are both indispensable. The spirit of inheritance is just as important as the inherited techniques. With the predecessors' will to "reach for the moon," later generations can have the opportunity to "kiss the moon."

zh: 伏胜钱又称“压胜钱”。“厌胜”一词指“以诅咒厌伏其人”，最早见于《汉书·王莽传》：“是岁八月，莽亲之南郊，铸作威斗。威斗者，以五石铜为之，若北斗，长二尺五寸，欲以厌胜众兵”。《后汉书·清河孝王庆传》也有“因诬言欲作盅道祝诅，以菟为厌胜之术”的记载。厌胜就是方士们用咒语和象征性的物体帮助那些有求于他们的人来诅咒仇人、祈祷鬼神，制服被诅咒者的工具。厌胜钱则是人们据厌胜法的本义，为避邪祈福而制造的形制与流通货币相似的物品，供人佩带赏玩，厌服邪魅，祈求吉祥。
en: Fusheng coins are also called Yasheng coins. The term "yasheng" refers to "using curses to subdue a person," first seen in the Book of Han, Biography of Wang Mang: "In the eighth month of that year, Mang personally went to the southern suburb and cast a Weidou. The Weidou was made of five-mineral copper, resembling the Northern Dipper, two chi five cun long, intended to suppress and overpower all military forces." The Book of Later Han, Biography of Prince Qing of Qinghe also records: "Therefore, they falsely accused him of intending to practice gu sorcery and curses, using rabbits as a yasheng technique." Yasheng refers to the methods used by occultists, employing incantations and symbolic objects to help those who sought their aid curse enemies, pray to spirits and ghosts, and subdue the cursed. Yasheng coins are objects made by people based on the original meaning of the yasheng method, resembling circulating currency in form, created to ward off evil, pray for blessings, worn or kept for enjoyment, to subdue evil spirits and pray for good fortune.

zh:
他从美梦中醒来，身边的被褥早已空无一人，仅余半张毫无温度的字条。
“我还有事情没想清楚，你等等我。”
他坐在驿站的旗帜下，由日出等到日落，日复一日。
前些日子的热闹总令人觉得不踏实。如今她做出离开的决定，他终于相信，遇到她并非梦境。
她最讨厌食言的人。想到这层，他安下心来，毫无疑虑地在原地等她。
昔日躺在手心摩挲的玉器被抛之脑后，他掰着手指头数她需要的东西：要鞣制好的羊皮做成衣裳挡风，要炮制好的甘松来养好胃口……
她不在，房子不过住处，家已不是家。
再等一等。等她的消息来，等她回头看自己。到那时候，他便会毫不犹豫地奔向有她的地方。
en:
He woke from a pleasant dream to an empty bed. Beside him lay half a note, already cold.
"There are still things I have not thought through. Wait for me."
He sat beneath the station banner, waiting from sunrise to sunset, day after day. The liveliness of recent days had always felt unreal. Now that she had chosen to leave, he finally believed that meeting her had not been a dream.
She despised those who broke their word. Thinking of this, he found peace of mind and waited where he was, without doubt.
The jade ornament he once turned over in his palm slipped from his thoughts. Instead, he counted on his fingers the things she would need. Tanned sheepskin to make windproof clothes. Carefully prepared spikenard to settle her stomach.
Without her, a house was only a place to stay. Home was no longer home.
Just wait a little longer. Wait for news from her. Wait for her to look back. When that day came, he would run without hesitation to wherever she was.

原本他将图纸放在了书房的暗格里，结果被三个弟子不慎翻出。最不省心的那个天天问他，什么时候让山里都通了云槎。
可云槎虽易制作，却需要更为坚实的轨道、更迅疾的流水与之匹配。如今的山中，自师兄不再问机关事，已无人能翻制流水轨。
他只好将图纸藏进了石室，只是看了又看……最后决定把这图纸折成纸鹊。
只是临挂上去时，他又犹豫了。于是把纸鹊拆开，写下一封长信，复又叠好。
挂好后，鸦看着上方盘旋的纸鹊架，又笑了。不知是依他预料，由师兄先找到这个秘密；还是被这些小纸鹊里的哪个孩子先发现呢？

zh:
胡厘：要下雨了。
董夫子：是啊，要下雨了。我曾听闻，狐身于巢便知风起，鼠居于洞可晓雨至，想来阁下不是狐便是鼠了。
胡厘：你知道我？
董夫子：不知道，但我在等你，等你来杀我。
胡厘：你不怕死？
董夫子：不，我怕死，但我还有比死更怕的事。先生也是如此，不是么？
胡厘：哦？那你怕什么？
董夫子：先生可知，董某虽修儒，但亦曾学过百家。
胡厘：为什么？
董夫子：因为我想找一条大道，一条能够让天下真正太平的大道。
董夫子：我曾学法，然始皇以法治六合，执棰拊以鞭笞天下，威虽振四海，万民却不曾得意。
董夫子：后来我便去研道，然汉初以黄老之术治天下，纵民若马，不施教化，豪强也不曾敛翼。
董夫子：我亦曾习墨，然墨者兼爱非攻，禁绝人伦，舍己利人，这天下又有几人可为？
胡厘：所以你觉得百家之中，唯有儒家才是真正的大道？
董夫子：儒家，也不是。
胡厘：那，你寻找的道究竟是什么？
董夫子：我做过一场梦，梦到了两千年后的世界。
董夫子：那里以儒作脊，立千秋风骨；以墨为锋，佑天下苍生；以法定尺，衡万物方圆。诸子百家尽皆归流，天下万民无不归心，无饥馑之忧，更无离乱之苦。
胡厘：你要融汇百家！不怕被儒门唾弃？
董夫子：刚刚先生问我怕什么，现在我可以回答你。我怕，这只是一场梦。
董夫子：朝菌不知朔晦，蟪蛄不识春秋，不见高山，不觉地平，既见沧海，难为细流。
董夫子：十年可谋一时兴衰，百年可谋王朝更替，千年可谋文脉赓续。先生，你我身处这万古洪流，何不纵目千载，谋那万年之势？
胡厘：你想要怎么做？
董夫子：欲平天下，需以王道统百家，而此举必当与墨家兼爱争锋。
董夫子：所以，董某厚颜，想代天下向墨者借岁千载。此后两千年，千年在儒，千年归墨，如此，天下大同矣。
……………………
胡厘：你当如何借？
董夫子：请墨者赴死。
en:
Hu Li: It is going to rain.
Master Dong: Yes, it is going to rain. I have heard that a fox knows the wind from its den, and a mouse knows the rain from its hole. I suppose you must be either a fox or a mouse.
Hu Li: You know me?
Master Dong: No. But I have been waiting for you... waiting for you to come and kill me.
Hu Li: Are you not afraid of death?
Master Dong: No, I am afraid of death. But there is something I fear far more than death itself. I believe you feel the same, do you not?
Hu Li: Oh? Then what is it you fear?
Master Dong: You should know, though I am a scholar of Confucianism, I have also studied the Hundred Schools of Thought.
Hu Li: Why?
Master Dong: Because I wanted to find a Great Way, a path that could bring true and lasting peace to the world.
Master Dong: I studied Legalism. Yet, the First Emperor used harsh laws to rule the six directions, cracking the whip across the realm. His majesty shook the four seas, but the people never found joy.
Master Dong: Then I studied Daoism. In the early Han Dynasty, they ruled through the ways of Huang-Lao, letting the people run free like unbridled horses without guidance, but the powerful and wealthy never restrained their greed.
Master Dong: I also studied Mohism. But the Mohists preach universal love and non-aggression; they suppress human desires and sacrifice themselves for the benefit of others. How many in this world can truly achieve that?
Hu Li: So you believe that among the Hundred Schools, only Confucianism is the Great Way?
Master Dong: Confucianism? No, it is not.
Hu Li: Then what exactly is this Way you are searching for?
Master Dong: I had a dream. I dreamed of a world two thousand years from now.
Master Dong: In that world, Confucianism serves as the spine, establishing eternal moral fortitude; Mohism serves as the blade, protecting the lives of the common people; Legalism serves as the ruler, balancing the boundaries of all things. The Hundred Schools merge into one stream, and the hearts of all people are united. There is no fear of famine, and no suffering of war and separation.
Hu Li: You want to merge the Hundred Schools! Are you not afraid of being spat upon by your own Confucian peers?
Master Dong: Just now, you asked me what I fear. Now I can answer you. I fear that this is merely a dream.
Master Dong: The morning mushroom knows not the turning of the moon; the summer cicada knows not the passing of the seasons. One who has not seen the high mountains cannot comprehend the flat plains; one who has gazed upon the vast ocean can hardly be captivated by a trickling stream.
Master Dong: A decade can plan for temporary prosperity; a century can plan for the rise and fall of a dynasty; a millennium can plan for the continuation of a culture. My friend, you and I stand in the eternal flood of time. Why not cast our gaze across a thousand years, and plan for an era that spans ten thousand?
Hu Li: How do you intend to do this?
Master Dong: To bring peace to the world, the Royal Way must unify the Hundred Schools. But this act will inevitably clash with the Mohist ideal of universal love.
Master Dong: Therefore, I brazenly seek to borrow a thousand years from the Mohists on behalf of the world. For the next two thousand years, the first millennium shall belong to Confucianism, and the second shall return to Mohism. Thus, the world shall reach the Great Harmony.
...
Hu Li: And how do you intend to borrow it?
Master Dong: By asking the Mohists to die.

zh:
游侠，见字如面。
前些时日，老朽随府尹大人巡查蒙学，见学堂里的娃娃们一个个正襟危坐，埋首书卷，连我等走近了都未曾察觉。
老朽心下好奇，是何等妙文，能让这些上蹿下跳的娃娃们如此专心？一问才知，他们手中所读，竟是你前些时日所赠。
老朽又问，这些书好在何处？娃娃们七嘴八舌，老朽这才知道，原来你竟为每个孩子都择了不同的书，实在是费心了。而听闻老朽与你相熟，他们都央着我，定要代他们向你道声谢。
只是，真要问他们想说什么，这群小家伙却面露羞赧，讷讷而止了。最后，老朽想了个法子，让他们把想说的话都诉诸笔端，一并封在信里了。至于写了什么，老朽绝未偷看！
对了，娃娃们还托我转交几幅画作，说是读了书卷后的有感而发。他们都说，游侠你是他们见过最有眼光的人，定能欣赏他们的大作。
哈哈，看来往后若再有与孩子们打交道的差事，找游侠准是没错了。

en:
Dear Wanderer,

The other day, I accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the village school. The children sat straight at their desks, noses buried in scrolls, so absorbed they didn't even notice us draw near.
Curious what could hold their attention so completely, I asked. Turns out, they were reading the very books you gifted them not long ago.
I inquired further: what made these books so special? The little ones burst into chatter, and that's when I learned you had chosen a different book for each child. What thoughtfulness.
When they heard I knew you, they begged me to pass along their thanks.
But when I asked what they wanted to say, shyness took over, and words failed them. So I suggested they write it down instead. Their letters are enclosed. And no, I did not peek!
Oh, and they also asked me to send you a few drawings. Inspired, they said, by your books. They all agreed you're the most discerning person they've ever met, and that you'd surely appreciate their masterpieces.
Seems to me, whenever there's a task involving children, you're the one to call.

《傲林匹敌车赛赛制宣传页》

文津馆历城台演武馆颁
【车赛源流】
行车之礼，肇于周室。天子诸侯，以车战为荣，三人一乘，左持弓、右执矛、中御马，谓之“全车”。齐鲁乃周之近国，此礼绵延千载，未曾断绝。

至本朝，文津馆林险生先生于历城台以车拒敌，一夫当先，百姓从之，遂成佳话。自此，车赛不再囿于庙堂，而归于乡野。三年一度，四方来会，名曰“傲林匹敌”——傲者，志也；林者，众也；匹敌者，以车会友也。

四海之客，不论门派、不论出身、不论男女，凡能驾车、愿参赛者，皆可报名。单人、二人、三人皆可。

临时组队：素不相识亦可成队，赛前抽签配对，缘分使然。
固定搭档：往年同车之人，可继续同车，无需重新磨合。
临阵换将：若进入决赛，亦可临阵换将。
每场比赛，胜方积三分，败方积一分。
不设平局。若双方同时抵达终点，加赛一轮，先过线者胜。
魁首之队，有惊天地泣鬼神之大奖相赠。
en:
Apex Chariot Contest Guide

Issued by the Inkbound Order Licheng Terrace Martial Hall
[Origins]
Chariot tradition began with the Zhou. Each "complete chariot" carried three riders: an archer on the left, a spearman on the right, and a driver in the center. This custom has endured in Qi and Lu for a thousand years.

In the present age, Inkbound Order Master Lin Xiansheng defended Licheng Terrace by chariot, inspiring the people to join him. Apex Chariot Contest then spread from the courts to the countryside. Held every three years, the Apex Chariot Contest welcomes competitors from across the land. Its name honors ambition, the gathered crowds, and friendship through rivalry.

Anyone may enter, regardless of sect, background, or gender. Teams may have one to three members.

Matched Teams: Enter alone and be paired by lot.
Regular Partners: Former teammates may race together again.
Substitutions: Finalists may change members before the race.
A win earns 3 points; a loss earns 1.
There are no draws. Ties are settled by an extra round.
The champions will receive an earth-shaking grand prize.

zh:
情之惑人，在其热切。
情之长久，在其诺成。
就像这双鞋，从想做，到做好，乃至送出，间隔了近十年。
因为诺可轻许，但诺成一事，须人有情，天有意。
天意让他们重逢，又在争吵中袒露最深的秘密，最后得以并肩而行。

于是，有了这双鞋子。
这世上有情人，终成眷属。
即使是在黄泉，也必定如此。

夏之日，冬之夜。百岁之后，归于其居。
en:
Love captivates through its heat. Love endures through promises kept.
These shoes are no different. From the wish to make them, to the making, to the giving, nearly a decade passed.
Promises come easily, but keeping them takes both a willing heart and a willing world. Fate brought them back together, a quarrel stripped away every last secret, and at the end of it all, they walked the same road.
And so these shoes came to be.
Those who love will find their way to each other in this world. Even in the realm of the dead, that much will hold.
In summer's long days and winter's long nights, after a hundred years, we come home to one another.

zh:
仗着自己身量尚小，弄潮儿躲过看守，到了奴隶地窖。
汉人奴隶见了弄潮儿手上的剑，伸手要挡，全身铁链哗啦啦地响。
剑贴在了奴隶的颈间。几乎是同时，弄潮儿身后生出高大黑影，银枪抵住了他后颈。三人谁都没有动。
“我来救人。”弄潮儿剑尖一挑，铁链应声而断。黑影低笑两声，收回长枪，刺破了另一人的枷锁。两道利器的光芒在地窖游走，带来久违的自由。
行侠仗义的两人一同攀上屋顶。对方扔来的壶中酒，把弄潮儿辣得龇牙咧嘴。他一挑银枪，将剩下的半壶洒向夜空，止住了弄潮儿问他名字的冲动。
他们没有姓名，因为他们共用一个名字，共照一副肝胆。
en:
Relying on his still-small stature, Young Yichao slipped past the guards and reached the slave cellar.
A Han slave, seeing the sword in Young Yichao's hand, reached out to block it, his chains clanking loudly.
The blade pressed against the slave's neck. Almost simultaneously, a tall shadow rose behind Young Yichao, a silver spear aimed at the back of his neck. None of the three moved.
"I'm here to rescue you." Young Yichao flicked his blade, and the iron chain snapped. 
The shadow chuckled, withdrew his spear, and pierced another man's shackles. 
Two gleaming weapons moved through the cellar, bringing long-awaited freedom.
The two righteous warriors climbed onto the roof together. Wine from a jug the stranger tossed made Young Yichao grimace at its bite. With a flick of his spear, the stranger scattered the remaining half toward the night sky, halting Young Yichao's impulse to ask his name.
They had no names, for they shared a single identity, illuminated by the same courage and loyalty.

游侠，多亏了你的建议，我昨日休沐好好睡了一觉，还做了个奇怪的梦！我一定要说与你听。
梦里我的火箭终于研制出来了！还因此获得了一个山中的奇怪奖项，叫什么若背尔奖！这个奖好像厉害得很，每年只颁发给长老们评出来最优秀的论文。我也不知道我怎么就拿了奖。
梦里头巨子、长老们，还有好多师弟师妹站在台下给我鼓掌，哦，还有游侠你！
巨子还说要授我封号，只是我还没听到封号名，就醒了。
想来这个梦是想告诉我，要更加努力才行。明日就不休沐了，我得多看，多背，多研究。
en:
Wanderer, thanks to your advice, I actually took a proper day off yesterday and got some good sleep. And I had the strangest dream. I have to tell you about it.
In the dream, I finally managed to invent my flaming arrow! And because of it, I even won some odd prize in the mountains, something called the No-bell Prize. It seemed like a very prestigious award, given once a year to the finest paper chosen by the Elders. I've no idea how I ended up winning it.
In the dream, the Grandmasters, the Elders, and a whole crowd of juniors were all standing below, clapping for me. You were there too, Wanderer.
The Grandmaster even said he was going to bestow a title on me, but before I could hear what it was, I woke up.
I suppose the dream was telling me I need to work even harder. No more days off starting tomorrow. I need to read more, memorize more, and do more research.

zh:
农人们扛着锄头、抱着娃娃，争相挤上书院门前叫嚷。
封龙书院的弟子们早已见惯不惊，该背书的背书，该画图的画图。
凑近了听，来的并非慕名求学之人，而是寻来这儿讨人的百姓。
什么八十岁的老母亲每到午后便失了踪影，什么那个整日晃悠的老头把人家郎君给拐走了，什么那人对他家姑娘胡说些“书读不透家财要破”的怪话……

大白天到处晃悠，嘴上没个把门，还疑似“拐”跑了不少人……这样危险的人物，他们封龙书院——
还真有一位。
有弟子想起，那人在她师父跟前，如何把这出山教书的差事说得天花乱坠，“骗”得她和几个同门齐齐跟来了此处，帮乡人抡了几个月的锄头。可收成的时候，他却愣是不收乡人们的粮。问起来，他只是把锅里最后几粒米捞给她，自己喝着米汤，神秘兮兮地说：“等着吧，这是在打窝呢。”哼，出力的又不是他！
有弟子记得，那人有一日套上那件从孤云讹来的袍子，捧着一本讹来的经书，逢人便要试验一遍那书上的看相之法。最后他自觉学有所成，去外头找人练手，劝得那为富不仁之辈花钱消灾，劝得那抛儿弃女之徒抱头痛哭。回来把这身行头一脱，摇头说动嘴皮子还是太累，不如回来打瞌睡。
还有跟得久些的弟子，想到了更远的往事——那人如何从文津馆那“借”来了一批书，又如何向那王姓的将军“请”来了建书院的人。以为书院建起来了就万事大吉，真正的苦日子还在后头呢。不受束脩，那他们就得自个儿种菜；不事权贵，那他们就得去田头自己找学生……
几人无奈相视，领了这一大帮人，熟门熟路地寻到了那条山后的小溪。

“院主——”
“嘘！”
只见那人手持鱼竿，头也没回。他的身旁，被“拐”来的男女老少也人手一竿，神色肃穆地盯着水面。
“上钩了！”
一个孩子惊喜地喊道，身旁几人帮他提起竿子，果真是一条肥大的鲢鳙。
“这是先生说的，上下同欲者胜吧！”“不对不对，我看是锲而不舍，金石可镂。”
钓鱼者们七嘴八舌地讨论起来，那后头来的弟子却看不下去了。
“可不是金石可镂嘛。让它们吃饱了饭，又下了这么多饵，这别家的鱼儿，可不都一个个上钩了嘛！”
被“拐”来的乡人们见了家人，意犹未尽地同他们说起了今日的收获。不只是人人手中的一篓子鱼，还有那饵料里的道理，打窝的门道，书中说过的，先贤讲过的……还有许许多多他们从没见过、听过的学问，他们明日还得来学呢！
那人这才回首，笑而不语。
先打窝，后下饵，这钓鱼啊，门道深着呢。
山缓溪浅，他鹤公钓不上来个周文王，但能钓起来几个向学的好苗子，钓起来一乡人的好日子。
当然，等鱼儿长大要很久，等好日子来要更久。但钓鱼嘛，最重要的是有耐心。
昔年姜太公钓鱼，不也是绸缪了大半辈子，这才钓起来个八百年盛世吗？
受得住风与霜，才守得住好地方。
而后，任鱼儿游向江湖广邈，天下启智，便由此始。
en:
Farmers came crowding to the gates of Dragonbend Academy, hoes slung over their shoulders and babies in their arms, all shouting at once.

The disciples of Dragonbend Academy were long used to scenes like this. Those reciting kept reciting, and those drawing kept drawing.
Listen a little closer, though, and it became clear these were not hopeful students come in search of learning. They were villagers who had come to get their people back.

One complained that his eighty-year-old mother went missing every afternoon. Another said that shambling old man had lured away her husband. Someone else said he had been filling her daughter's head with nonsense like, "If you don't study properly, your family fortune will fall apart."
Roaming around in broad daylight, talking without any filter, and possibly having "carried off" half the village... for a dangerous figure like that, Dragonbend Academy really did have one.

One disciple remembered how he had sweet-talked her master into letting them come down from the mountain to teach, making it all sound so grand that she and several of her fellow disciples had followed him here without a second thought, only to spend months out in the fields swinging hoes for the villagers.
And when harvest finally came, he flatly refused to take any grain from them.
When she asked why, he simply fished the last few grains of rice out of the pot into her bowl, drank the thin rice broth himself, and said with an air of mystery, "Just wait. I'm chumming the water."
Easy for him to say. He wasn't the one doing all the work.

Another disciple remembered the day he put on that robe he had conned out of Lone Cloud, tucked a scripture he had conned out of someone under his arm, and went around trying out the face-reading techniques from the book on everyone he met.
By the end of it, he thought he'd gotten pretty good, so he went out to practice on real people. He talked one rich brute into spending money to ward off disaster, and talked one heartless man who had abandoned his children into breaking down in tears.
Then he came back, took the whole outfit off, shook his head, and said talking people into things was too tiring. Better to come back and nap.

Those who had been with him longer remembered even earlier days, how he had "borrowed" a batch of books from Inkbound Order, and how he had "invited" a certain General Wang to send people to build the academy.
They had thought that once the academy was built, things would get easier. If anything, that was when the hard days really began.
If they would not take tuition, then they had to grow their own vegetables.
If they would not curry favor with the powerful, then they had to go out into the fields and find students themselves.

The disciples exchanged resigned looks, then led the whole crowd along a familiar path to the little stream behind the mountain.
"Master Crane..."
"Shh."
The man sat there with a fishing rod in hand without even turning around. Beside him sat the very villagers he had supposedly "carried off," men and women, old and young, each with a rod of their own, all staring solemnly at the water.

"I got one!"
A child cried out in delight. The people around him hurried to help lift the rod, and up came a fat silver carp.

"So this is what the teacher meant by 'When people pull together, they win'!"
"No, no, this is more like 'With enough persistence, even metal and stone can be carved through'!"
The fishers all started arguing at once, but the disciples who had come up behind them could not hold it in anymore.
"Carved through stone, sure. You fed them full and threw in this much bait. Of course every fish in the stream came running."

The villagers who had been "carried off" were still full of enthusiasm when they saw their families again, eagerly telling them about everything they had gained that day.
It was not just the baskets of fish in their hands. It was the ideas behind the bait, the know-how of chumming the water, the things the books had said, the teachings the sages had left behind... and all kinds of knowledge they had never seen or heard before.
They still had to come back tomorrow and learn more.
Only then did the man turn around, smiling without a word.

First you chum the water, then you set the bait. There was a lot more to fishing than most people thought.
In these gentle hills and shallow streams, Crane was not going to fish up another King Wen of Zhou.
But he could still reel in a few good young minds eager to learn, and with them, a better life for the whole village.

Of course, fish take a long time to grow, and good days take even longer to arrive.
But that was the thing about fishing. What mattered most was patience.

Back then, didn't Jiang Ziya spend most of his life preparing before he finally hooked eight hundred years of flourishing rule?
Only those who can endure wind and frost can hold on to a good place.
And after that, let the fish swim out into the wide world of rivers and lakes.
From here, learning would begin to spread beneath the sky.

zh:
天一楼者，天下第一藏书之楼也。入门但见书橱连云，缥帙满架，自先秦竹简至本朝新椠，无所不备。经史子集，经纬纵横；南北舆图，东西方志，皆列于其间。更有珍本孤册，或为名家手录，或为前朝秘藏，世人难得一见者，亦尽收于此。
楼中书目，分门别类，井然有序。凡登楼者，初入之际，莫不瞠目。一眼望去，卷帙浩渺，如入书海。此非一楼之藏，乃天下文章之所归也！
四方之士，闻天一楼之名，无不向往。有负笈千里而来者，有辞官专程而至者，有白发老儒终日抄录于其间者，亦有年少学子捧卷忘食、不觉日暮者。楼中肃静，唯闻翻书之声，窸窸窣窣，如春蚕食叶。每逢晴日，日光从西窗斜入，光影斑驳，落于宣纸之上，尘埃浮浮，满室生香。
其中藏书之富，非言语所能尽述。“天下可读之书，十之七八，尽在此楼。”此言虽有过，然观者莫不颔首。天一楼非独藏也，实乃天下好学之人所共仰者也。书藏于此，文脉不绝，后之览者，亦当怀此敬心而来。
en:
Tianyi Tower is the foremost library under heaven. Upon entering, one sees bookshelves stretching to the clouds, scrolls filling every rack. From bamboo slips of the pre-Qin era to newly carved editions of the current dynasty, nothing is missing. The Ancient Classics span every field, woven together in intricate order; maps of the north and south, records of east and west, all arranged within. Rare and singular volumes—some copied by famous scholars' own hands, some secret treasures of past dynasties, seldom seen by the world—are all gathered here as well.
The tower's catalog is meticulously organized by category. All who climb its stairs, upon first entering, cannot help but stare in awe. At a single glance, the sea of scrolls seems boundless, as if stepping into an ocean of books. This is not the collection of one tower alone, it is where all the writings of the world converge!
Scholars from every corner, hearing the name of Tianyi Tower, cannot help but long to visit. Some travel a thousand miles with their satchels; some resign their posts just to come; white-haired scholars spend their days copying texts within its halls, while young students clutch their books, forgetting to eat, unaware that dusk has fallen. The tower remains hushed, save for the rustle of turning pages, like silkworms nibbling spring leaves. On sunny days, light slants through the western windows, casting dappled shadows upon the Xuan paper, dust drifting in the air, filling the room with a quiet fragrance.
The richness of its collection defies description. "Seven or eight out of every ten books worth reading in this world can be found within this tower." Though this may be an exaggeration, no visitor fails to nod in agreement. Tianyi Tower is not merely a repository, it is a place revered by all who love learning throughout the land. As long as its books remain, the cultural lineage endures, and those who come after shall visit it with the same reverence.

zh: 车夕夕曾经是爱下棋的。小时候，每到酉时三刻，他都会蹲在门口，等待头顶的天空被染成金色，娘扯着嗓子喊：“车夕夕，叫你爹回来吃饭了。”他便跑向不死树，不死树下传来叮叮当当的响声，这是爹吃的子落进棋盒的声音。爹总赢。“马走日，象飞田，这是下棋的规矩。做人的规矩，可比这难多了。”这是爹赢棋后最爱说的一句话，这句话，他记了很多年。
en: Che Xixi once loved playing chess. As a child, every evening around sunset, he'd sit by the doorway, waiting for the sky to turn golden. His mother's voice would ring out, "Che Xixi, call your father—dinner's ready!" And he'd dash to the Immortal Tree, where the familiar clatter of chess pieces falling into the box told him his father was near. His father always won. "Knights move in an L, elephants fly diagonally—those are the chess rules. But the rules for living? They're far, far harder," his father would say after each victory. Those words stayed with Che Xixi for years.

zh: 古香炉名，汉代最流行的熏香器具。其造型为圆形铜盘底座，中有铜柄承接炉身，高低可调。炉身半圆形，炉盖为重叠山峰造型，山中有羽人、走兽等形象，呈尖锥体。炉内焚香时，烟气飘忽而出，盘旋缭绕，仿若海中仙山博山，因此得名。
en: An ancient incense burner, the most popular incense tool in the Han Dynasty. Its shape featured a circular bronze plate base with a copper handle in the middle to support the furnace body, which could be adjusted for height. The furnace body was semicircular, and the lid was shaped like overlapping mountain peaks, with figures such as feathered immortals and beasts inside, forming a cone. When incense was burned inside, smoke drifted out, curling around like Boshan, a mythical immortal mountain in the sea, hence the name Boshan Incense Burner.

江湖上有句话，叫：离人一饮不羡神仙。中原武林各路豪侠尽皆喜爱此饮，神仙渡亦是因此饮闻名。只是众人大多只品尝出饮中三分滋味，却从未了解离人泪中，离人二字何为离人。
有的人说，这是霸陵桥上送别亲朋的诗意。也有的人说，这是明月徘徊，相思远游的爱人。
但只有神仙渡中那些同洛神做过交易的人知道，离人泪，离的从来都是他们自己。从此超脱人世，与那过往种种，永诀别离。
en:
There's an old saying in the martial world: One sip of the Parting Tears, and even immortals hold no allure. Heroes from every corner of the Central Plains cherish this drink, and Heaven's Pier is famed for it. Yet most only taste a hint of its flavor, never grasping the true meaning behind "Parting Tears", nor what it means to be the one who parts. 
Some say the name speaks of sorrowful partings at Baling Bridge. Others believe it echoes the longing of lovers separated beneath the wandering moon. 
But only those in Heaven's Pier who've bargained with the Water Lady know the truth: the one who parts is always themselves. From that moment on, they leave the mortal world behind, and all they once held dear.

zh:
禁庭深处，教养宫娥为公主梳起云鬟，插上一支精致的步摇。
一步一摇，琅琅作响。宫娥叮嘱她，行必缓，步必平，不可让步摇发出声音。
公主就这样带着步摇，一步一步从寝宫出发，来到了遥远的凉州。
对她来说，步摇代表着公主的身份，也时时刻刻提醒自己担负的使命。

后来，她在一场宴会上，遇到了像葡萄一样莹润可爱的少女。她拉着公主的手，将步摇的垂珠唤作铃铛。
少女带着手串起舞，快乐得像一只小鸟。公主温柔的眼眸里，映着少女烂漫的微笑。
她希望少女的快乐可以像舞步一样永不停歇。

无人的寂夜，公主在玉池的小屋里，对着天上的月亮。
她也模仿起少女的舞步，耳边的步摇也欢快地飞扬。
原来带着步摇也可以起舞。
真希望以后还有机会见到那位少女，她也要学会那支快乐的舞。
en:
Deep in the palace, maids styled the princess's hair, adorning it with an exquisite step-shaker. 
One step, one sway, a clear, ringing sound. They reminded her: walk slowly, step evenly, never let the step-shaker clatter. 
Thus, wearing it, the princess walked step by step from her chambers to distant Liangzhou. 
To her, the step-shaker meant her identity, a constant reminder of her mission. 

Later, at a banquet, she met a girl sweet as grapes. She took the princess's hand, calling the step-shaker's pearls "bells." 
The girl danced with her bracelet, joyful as a bird. The princess's gentle eyes reflected her radiant smile. 
She wished the girl's happiness could dance on forever. 

In a silent night, the princess faced the moon in her jade pond chamber. 
She imitated the girl's dance, the step-shaker at her ear swaying happily. 
So one could dance with a step-shaker after all. 
How she wished to see that girl again—she wanted to learn that joyful dance too.

Heaven's Pier now has two great specialties: one is the fragrant drink named Parting Tears, and the other is a Pear Blossom Grove whose blooms fall like snow. When the Drunken Immortal Month arrives, this place becomes a splendid scene on earth—truly a delight to behold.

无果。

同光三年，十月初十
外出寻豹乳，三子托与稚童。
归来时见三子容光焕发。汝天才乎？定要与其亲近一番。

同光三年，十月十一
闻稚童名万师，世代治水，于机关之术颇为痴迷。
幸甚，如此良才岂能不收为弟子？

同光三年，十月十二
与吾徒竞机关术，胜之，将其收入门下。
虽胜之不武，然美质良材，湮没于尘，岂不惜哉！此恶吾受之。

同光三年，十月十五
得闲。我以九节之法，制一鱼竿，去其锐锋，甚是趁手。
唯吾徒辅喂三子之时，眼神颇为幽怨。

同光三年，十月十六
万师甚苦，心中有愧，今日定钓肥鱼一条为其补身。
孰料一杆入水，竟又得一子……吾徒，待归山便好了。
en:
1st Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
The floodwaters have begun to recede. Seeing Feng Nengqi's uncommon gifts, I thought I might take on a disciple after all. Yet the brat dares call my martial skill mediocre?
Very well. He may keep his fish.
2nd Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
My belly was empty, so I went to the river to fish. Before even half a quarter hour had passed, something had taken the hook.
Had that brat been here, I would have shown him what I caught... a baby?
3rd Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
How does one feed an infant? Mohist Hill never taught such things.
Would fish broth do?
4th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
With one child in each arm, I can no longer fish.
I can only follow the river upstream. Perhaps I may find their parents.

5th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
Reached a deserted village. Found someone about to drown his child in the river, and managed to talk him out of it.
That night, I heard an infant crying outside the house. Its parents had already taken their own lives. Has the world truly fallen so far?

7th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
The three little ones were starving. With no other choice, I went to ask a woman for milk. I was rewarded with a beating.
To no use.

8th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
Reached Heavenfall. Asked a village women for milk again. Was beaten again.
Still nothing. I am nearly beside myself.

9th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
Still nothing. Beaten yet again. Then I suddenly heard a child's voice ask, "Why not use animal milk?"
It struck me like thunder. A revelation from Heaven.

10th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
Went out in search of leopard's milk, leaving the three children in that child's care.
When I returned, the little three looked bright and full of life. Is he some kind of prodigy? I must get to know him properly.

11th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
Learned that the child is called Wanshi. His family has managed the waters for generations, and he is utterly obsessed with mechanisms.
Excellent. How could I fail to take such talent as a disciple?

12th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
Matched my skill in mechanisms against his and defeated him, thus taking him into my school.
The victory may not have been entirely honorable, but to let such fine material vanish into the dust would be a terrible waste. Let him hate me for it.

15th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
At last, a little leisure. Using the method of nine joints, I made a fishing rod and blunted away its sharp edge. It sits very well in the hand.
Only my disciple, when helping feed the three children, looks rather aggrieved.

16th Day of the Tenth Month, third year of Tongguang
Wanshi has had a hard time of it. I feel somewhat ashamed, so today I resolved to catch a fat fish and nourish him properly.
Who would have thought that the moment the line touched water, I would catch yet another child... Disciple, once we return to the mountain, things will surely be better.

街坊们便笑：“人抓不着贼，猫抓得着耗子，这不比捕头强？” 
一来二去，“赛捕头”就叫开了。 
后来黎师爷在衙门功劳簿上添了一笔：“赛捕头，本月缉盗四十三只，无漏网。”

en:
Detectail is a stray cat that Constable Xing Dalang took in and brought to the county office. While Constable Xing cannot catch a single thief, Detectail catches a rat every single day.

The neighbors soon began to joke, "The constable cannot catch a thief, yet the cat catches rats with ease. Isn't this cat better than our constable?" Over time, the name "Detectail" caught on.

Later, Officer Li added an entry to the county office's merit ledger: "Detectail: apprehended forty-three thieves this month, with none slipping the net."

Looking at the empty space beneath his own name, Constable Xing could only sigh.

zh:

锦绣是原本的质地，旧是过往历经的岁月。
父亲把这双鞋送出的时候，在鞋尖上缀上了两颗夜明珠。
那是权臣给这位江湖侠客的见面礼。
惊涛掌未曾收过这么重的礼，左思右想，最后缀在了给女儿的新鞋上。
但兰澳扯掉了明珠，将那华贵的珠宝丢了出去，珠子咕噜噜滚出客栈油腻腻的过道，依然不改它的明光。
无论是糊里糊涂收下礼物的父亲，还是不明所以但是很不喜欢的女儿，
那时候他们都不知道，上位者所有的馈赠，都会让你付出昂贵的代价。
en:
A pair of Worn Brocade Shoes. 

The brocade recalls what they were made to be, and the wear tells the story of all the years they've traveled through. 
When the father gifted these shoes, he attached two night pearls to the toes— 
gifts from a powerful noble to this Wandering Hero. 

Palm Strike Master had never received such a lavish present before. After much thought, he fastened the pearls to a new pair intended for his daughter. 
But Lan Ao tore them away, tossing the precious jewels to the dusty floor, where they rolled across the greasy inn hallway, still shining with unyielding light. 
Neither the bewildered father who accepted the gift, nor the daughter who rejected it, 
understood then that such favors from the mighty always came with a hidden price.

zh:
【学而第一】

子曰：“学而时习之，不亦悦乎？有朋自远方来，不亦乐乎？人不知而不愠，不亦君子乎？”
有子曰：“其为人也孝悌，而好犯上者，鲜矣。 不好犯上，而好作乱者，未之有也。君子务本，本立而道生。孝悌也者，其仁之本与？”
子曰：“巧言令色，鲜矣仁。”
曾子曰：“吾日三省吾身，为人谋而不忠乎？与朋友交言而不信乎？传不习乎？”
子曰：“导千乘之国，敬事而信，节用而爱人，使民以时。”
子曰：“弟子入则孝，出则悌，谨而信，泛爱众，而亲仁，行有余力，则以学文。”
子夏曰：“贤贤易色。 事父母，能竭其力；事君，能致其身；与朋友交，言而有信。虽曰未学，吾必谓之学矣。”
子曰：“君子不重则不威，学则不固。主忠信，无友不如己者，过则勿惮改。”
曾子曰：“慎终追远，民德归厚矣。”
子禽问于子贡曰：“夫子至于是邦也，必闻其政。求之与？抑与之与？”子贡曰：“夫子温、良、恭、俭、让以得之。夫子之求也，其诸异乎人求之与？”
子曰：“父在，观其志；父没，观其行。三年无改于父之道，可谓孝矣。”
有子曰：“礼之用，和为贵。先王之道，斯为美，小大由之，有所不行，知和而和，不以礼节之，亦不可行也。”
有子曰：“信近于义，言可复也。恭近于礼，远耻辱也。因不失其亲，亦可宗也。”
子曰：“君子食无求饱，居无求安，敏于事而慎于言，就有道而正焉，可谓好学也已矣。”
子贡曰：“贫而无谄，富而无骄，何如？”子曰：“可也，未若贫而乐道，富而好礼者也。”子贡曰：“诗云：如切如磋，如琢如磨，其斯之谓与？”子曰：“赐也，始可与言诗已矣，告诸往而知来者也。”
子曰：“不患人之不己知，患己不知人也。”
en:
[Chapter 1: Learning]

The Master said, "Is it not pleasant to learn with a constant perseverance and application? Is it not pleasant to have friends coming from distant quarters? Is one not a person of complete virtue, who feels no discomposure though people may take no note of one?"
The philosopher You said, "They are few who, being filial and congenial, are fond of offending against their superiors. There have been none, who, not liking to offend against their superiors, have been fond of stirring up confusion. The superior person bends one's attention to what is radical. That being established, all practical courses naturally grow up. Filial piety and congenial submission—are they not the root of all benevolent actions?"
The Master said, "Fine words and an insinuating appearance are seldom associated with true virtue."
The philosopher Zeng said, "I daily examine myself on three points: whether, in transacting business for others, I may have been not faithful; whether, in intercourse with friends, I may have been not sincere; whether I may have not mastered and practised the instructions of my teacher."
The Master said, "To rule a country of a thousand chariots, there must be reverent attention to business, and sincerity; economy in expenditure, and love for people; and the employment of the people at the proper seasons."
The Master said, "A youth, when at home, should be filial, and, abroad, respectful to one's elders. One should be earnest and truthful. One should overflow in love to all, and cultivate the friendship of the good. When one has time and opportunity, after the performance of these things, one should employ them in polite studies."
Zixia said, "If one withdraws one's mind from the love of beauty and applies it as sincerely to the love of the virtuous; if, in serving one's parents, one can exert one's utmost strength; if, in serving one's prince, one can devote one's life; if, in one's dealings with friends, one's words are sincere: although people may say that one has not learned, I will certainly say that one has."
The Master said, "If the scholar be not grave, one will not call forth any veneration, and one's learning will not be solid. Hold faithfulness and sincerity as first principles. Have no friends not equal to yourself. When you have faults, do not fear to abandon them."
The philosopher Zeng said, "Let there be a careful attention to perform the funeral rites to parents, and let them be followed when long gone with the ceremonies of sacrifice; then the virtue of the people will resume its proper excellence."
Ziqin asked Zigong, saying, "When our master comes to any country, he does not fail to learn all about its government. Does he ask his information? or is it given to him?" Zigong said, "Our master is benign, upright, courteous, temperate, and complaisant, and thus he gets his information. The master's mode of asking information—is it not different from that of other people?"
The Master said, "While one's father is alive, look at the bent of one's will; when one's father is dead, look at one's conduct. If for three years one does not alter from the way of one's father, one may be called filial."
The philosopher You said, "In practising the rules of propriety, a natural ease is to be prized. In the ways prescribed by the ancient kings, this is the excellent quality, and in things small and great we follow them. Yet it is not to be observed in all cases. If one, knowing how such ease should be prized, manifests it, without regulating it by the rules of propriety, this likewise is not to be done."
The philosopher You said, "When agreements are made according to what is right, what is spoken can be made good. When respect is shown according to what is proper, one keeps far from shame and disgrace. When the parties upon whom one leans are proper persons to be intimate with, one can make them one's guides and masters."
The Master said, "One who aims to be a person of complete virtue, in one's food does not seek to gratify one's appetite, nor in one's dwelling-place does one seek the appliances of ease; one is earnest in what one is doing, and careful in one's speech; one frequents the company of people of principle that one may be rectified: such a person may be said indeed to love to learn."
Zigong said, "What do you pronounce concerning the poor person who yet does not flatter, and the rich person who is not proud?" The Master replied, "They will do; but they are not equal to one, who, though poor, is yet cheerful, and to one, who, though rich, loves the rules of propriety." Zigong replied, "It is said in the Book of Poetry, 'As you cut and then file, as you carve and then polish.' The meaning is the same, I apprehend, as that which you have just expressed." The Master said, "With one like Ci, I can begin to talk about the Odes. I told him one point, and he knew its proper sequence."
The Master said, "I will not be afflicted at people's not knowing me; I will be afflicted that I do not know people."

【阳货第十七】

阳货欲见孔子，孔子不见，归孔子豚。孔子时其亡也，而往拜之，遇诸涂。谓孔子曰：“来，予与尔言。”曰：“怀其宝而迷其邦，可谓仁乎？”曰：“不可。”“好从事而亟失时，可谓智乎？”曰：“不可！”“日月逝矣，岁不我与。”孔子曰：“诺，吾将仕矣。”
子曰：“性相近也，习相远也。”
子曰：“唯上智与下愚不移。”
子之武城，闻弦歌之声，夫子莞尔而笑，曰：“割鸡焉用牛刀？”子游对曰：“昔者偃也闻诸夫子曰：‘君子学道则爱人，小人学道则易使。’”子曰：“二三子，偃之言是也，前言戏之耳。”
公山弗扰以费畔，召，子欲往。子路不说，曰：“末之也已，何必公山氏之之也？”子曰：“夫召我者而岂徒哉？如有用我者，吾其为东周乎！”
子张问仁于孔子，孔子曰：“能行五者于天下为仁矣。”请问之，曰：“恭、宽、信、敏、惠。恭则不侮，宽则得众，信则人任焉，敏则有功，惠则足以使人。”
佛肸召，子欲往。子路曰：“昔者由也闻诸夫子曰：‘亲于其身为不善者，君子不入也。’佛肸以中牟畔，子之往也，如之何？”子曰：“然，有是言也。不曰坚乎，磨而不磷；不曰白乎，涅而不缁。吾岂匏瓜也哉？焉能系而不食？”
子曰：“由也，女闻六言六蔽矣乎？”对曰：“未也。”“居！吾语女。好仁不好学，其蔽也愚；好知不好学，其蔽也荡；好信不好学，其蔽也贼；好直不好学，其蔽也绞；好勇不好学，其蔽也乱；好刚不好学，其蔽也狂。”
子曰：“小子何莫学夫《诗》？《诗》可以兴，可以观，可以群，可以怨。迩之事父，远之事君，多识于鸟兽草木之名。”
子谓伯鱼曰：“女为《周南》、《召南》矣乎？人而不为《周南》、《召南》，其犹正墙面而立也与！”
子曰：“礼云礼云，玉帛云乎哉？乐云乐云，钟鼓云乎哉？”
子曰：“色厉而内荏，譬诸小人，其犹穿窬之盗也与？”
子曰：“乡愿，德之贼也。”
子曰：“道听而涂说，德之弃也。”
子曰：“鄙夫可与事君也与哉？其未得之也，患得之；既得之，患失之。苟患失之，无所不至矣。”
子曰：“古者民有三疾，今也或是之亡也。古之狂也肆，今之狂也荡；古之矜也廉，今之矜也忿戾；古之愚也直，今之愚也诈而已矣。”
子曰：“巧言令色，鲜矣仁。”

en:
【Book 17: Yang Huo】

Yang Huo wished to see Confucius, but Confucius would not see him. He then sent Confucius a present of a pig. Confucius, having chosen a time when Yang Huo was not at home, went to pay his respects for the gift. He met him, however, on the way. Yang Huo said to Confucius, "Come, let me speak with you." He then asked, "Can he be called benevolent who keeps his jewel in his bosom, and leaves his country to confusion?" Confucius replied, "No." "Can he be called wise, who is anxious to be engaged in public employment, and yet is constantly losing the opportunity of being so?" Confucius again said, "No." "The days and months are passing away; the years do not wait for us." Confucius said, "Right; I will go into office."
The Master said, "By nature, men are nearly alike; by practice, they get to be wide apart."
The Master said, "There are only the wise of the highest class, and the stupid of the lowest class, who cannot be changed."
The Master having come to Wu-cheng, heard there the sound of stringed instruments and singing. Well pleased and smiling, he said, "Why use an ox knife to kill a fowl?" Zi-you replied, "Formerly, Master, I heard you say, 'When the man of high station is well instructed, he loves men; when the man of low station is well instructed, he is easily ruled.'" The Master said, "My disciples, Yan's words are right. What I said was only in sport."
Gongshan Fu-rao, when he was holding Fei, and in an attitude of rebellion, invited the Master to visit him, who was rather inclined to go. Zi-lu was displeased, and said, "Indeed, you cannot go! Why must you think of going to see Gongshan?" The Master said, "Can it be without some reason that he has invited me? If any one employ me, may I not make an eastern Zhou?"
Zi-zhang asked Confucius about perfect virtue. Confucius said, "To be able to practice five things everywhere under heaven constitutes perfect virtue." He begged to ask what they were, and was told, "Gravity, generosity of soul, sincerity, earnestness, and kindness. If you are grave, you will not be treated with disrespect. If you are generous, you will win all. If you are sincere, people will repose trust in you. If you are earnest, you will accomplish much. If you are kind, this will enable you to employ the services of others."
Bi Xi invited the Master to visit him, who was inclined to go. Zi-lu said, "Master, formerly I have heard you say, 'When a man in his own person is guilty of doing evil, a superior man will not associate with him.' Bi Xi is in rebellion, holding possession of Zhongmou; if you go to him, what shall be said?" The Master said, "Yes, I did use these words. But is it not said, that, if a thing be really hard, it may be ground without being made thin? Is it not said, that, if a thing be really white, it may be steeped in a dark fluid without being made black? Am I a bitter gourd? How can I be hung up out of the way of being eaten?"
The Master said, "You, have you heard the six words to which are attached six becloudings?" You replied, "I have not." "Sit down, and I will tell them to you. There is the love of being benevolent without the love of learning; the beclouding here leads to a foolish simplicity. There is the love of knowing without the love of learning; the beclouding here leads to dissipation of mind. There is the love of being sincere without the love of learning; the beclouding here leads to an injurious disregard of consequences. There is the love of straightforwardness without the love of learning; the beclouding here leads to rudeness. There is the love of boldness without the love of learning; the beclouding here leads to insubordination. There is the love of firmness without the love of learning; the beclouding here leads to extravagant conduct."
The Master said, "My children, why do you not study the Book of Poetry? The Odes serve to stimulate the mind. They may be used for purposes of self-contemplation. They teach the art of sociability. They show how to regulate feelings of resentment. From them you learn the more immediate duty of serving one's father, and the remoter one of serving one's prince. From them we become largely acquainted with the names of birds, beasts, and plants."
The Master said to Bo-yu, "Do you give yourself to the Zhou Nan and the Shao Nan? The man who has not studied the Zhou Nan and the Shao Nan is like one who stands with his face right against a wall. Is he not so?"
The Master said, "'It is according to the rules of propriety,' they say. 'It is according to the rules of propriety,' they say. Are gems and silk all that is meant by propriety? 'It is music,' they say. 'It is music,' they say. Are bells and drums all that is meant by music?"
The Master said, "He who puts on an appearance of stern firmness, while inwardly he is weak, is like one of the small, mean people; yea, is he not like the thief who breaks through, or climbs over, a wall?"
The Master said, "Your good, careful people of the villages are the thieves of virtue."
The Master said, "To tell, as we go along, what we have heard on the way, is to cast away our virtue."
The Master said, "There are those mean creatures! How impossible it is along with them to serve one's prince! While they have not got their aims, their anxiety is how to get them. When they have got them, their anxiety is lest they should lose them. When they are anxious lest such things should be lost, there is nothing to which they will not proceed."
The Master said, "Anciently, men had three failings, which now perhaps are not to be found. The high-mindedness of antiquity showed itself in a disregard of small things; the high-mindedness of the present day shows itself in wild license. The stern dignity of antiquity showed itself in grave reserve; the stern dignity of the present day shows itself in quarrelsome perverseness. The stupidity of antiquity showed itself in straightforwardness; the stupidity of the present day shows itself in sheer deceit."
The Master said, "Fine words and an insinuating appearance are seldom associated with true virtue."

zh:
马屏山出发时，草上的露水还没干。
路旁有个塌了的草棚。他看了一眼，原本脚步没停。走出三步，还是折回来，从包袱里抽出铁棍和麻绳。
或许是他想起父亲修东厢房窗户的样子，虽止不住那群孩子的啼哭声，但记忆中阳光斜射，父亲的背影如此宽厚温暖。
棚柱立起来时，有个老人朝他作揖，一听是去封龙书院的，立马说那儿的弟子真好，真好！
他护紧身上的包袱，扭头不答——他可不是什么封龙弟子，他带了那么多东西来，是为了杀鹤！
先用麻绳勒晕，再用铁棍打死。与杀父之仇相比，这已算仁慈。
眼下两样物件都留在此地，那就改用拳好了，更爽快！

行至半程，太阳正午。
汗从鬓角流下来，滑进嘴角，是咸的。他想起那些孩子们的眼泪。
父亲总说，别过去，你和他们不一样。他们没有爹娘，等给他们找到爹娘，自然就不哭了。
父亲是寻人高手，很快就能为他们找见爹娘。每送走一个孩子，他都有一粒糖吃。父亲说，团圆，就是这种滋味。虽然那时常与哭声作伴，可他的的确确有过那样一个甜蜜的童年。这样好的父亲，鹤怎敢说他是恶人？
是鹤，让他和那些孩子一样了。
鹤夺走了他的父亲、他的童年，留给他的东西，不过屈指可数：几册墨家典籍、一套武学心法、一对养父母、无数从梦中惊醒的夜晚……还有一颗复仇心。
前面的桥怎么断了？榫头断口的粉屑，簌簌地落。
马屏山打开包袱，取出那人当年留下的机巧图谱。翻到第三页，是修桥之法。
很快，桥修好了。他踩上去试了试，稳。
但是这本图谱，就留在原地吧，免得留下话柄，说他承了恶人的情。

雾从山涧漫上来，已是夜深。
马屏山的呼吸开始重了，才不是因为累。
只因眼前情况危急，这块岩石太重，被压住的樵夫已昏了过去。若再不施救，必死无疑。
今天真倒霉。
他蹲下来，摊开包袱，看着里面最后的东西，只剩一套袖箭。移石要杠杆，正骨需夹板，他也学过。现只好连那箭匣都拆了去，一分为二，变作夹板。
绑夹板时，他看见樵夫手中的茧，忽地想起一些从没在意的事。
父亲的手，也有过这样的茧——可父亲是先生，所以家里才会有那么多可怜孩子。但先生的手，又怎会有握刀的茧……不会，不是的……家里那么多来了又去的孩子，不过是因为他们无家可归……他的父亲不是拐子、不是人牙子！
从前左邻右里的议论声在马屏山的脑中再度嚷起，险些连这猎猎作响的山风都盖不住。
可那些离家的孩子以后是否再也不哭，他确实不清楚。
樵夫意识渐明时，马屏山站起身。
此刻的他，已一无所有了。

雾淡了。
抬头望，封龙书院就在不远处。
这条复仇路，在他的心里已反复走了十年。
马屏山最后看了一眼来路，山道弯弯曲曲，蒙着薄雾，像一道试图愈合又挣开的疤。
他忽然想起书中的话，“世间黑白，不在观色，而在观心。”
他回过头，只向前去。
en:
When Ma Pingshan set out, the dew on the grass was still there.

By the roadside stood a collapsed thatched shack. He glanced at it and kept walking.
After three steps, he stopped, turned back, and pulled an iron rod and a length of hemp rope from his bundle.

Maybe it reminded him of the way his father used to mend the window in the east room. The crying of those children never stopped, but in his memory the sunlight slanted in, and his father's back looked broad and warm.
By the time he had propped the posts back up, an old man was bowing to him in thanks. The moment he heard Ma Pingshan was headed for Dragonbend Academy, he started praising its disciples, saying what good people they were, what good people they were.
Ma Pingshan tightened his hold on the bundle at his side and turned away without a word.

He was no disciple of Dragonbend.
He had brought all this with him for one reason: to kill Crane.

First, use the rope to choke him senseless. Then use the iron rod to finish him off.
Compared with the debt of a murdered father, that was mercy enough.

Now both items had been left behind here, so he would use his fists instead.
That might be even better.

By the time he was halfway there, the sun was high overhead.
Sweat ran from his temples to the corner of his mouth. It tasted salty.
It made him think of those children's tears.

His father had always said, "Don't go near them. You're not the same as they are. They don't have fathers or mothers. Once I help them find their parents, they won't cry anymore."
His father had been good at finding people. It never took him long to track down a child's parents.
And every time he sent one child away, Ma Pingshan got a piece of candy.
"Reunion tastes like this," his father used to say.
Even with crying all around him, he really had once had a sweet childhood.

How could Crane dare call a father like that an evil man?
It was Crane who had made him just like those children.
Crane had taken his father and his childhood from him, and left him only a few things: a few Mohist texts, a martial manual, a pair of foster parents, countless nights jolting awake from dreams... and a heart bent on revenge.

Why was the bridge ahead broken?
Powder from the snapped mortise joint sifted down.
Ma Pingshan opened his bundle and took out the book of mechanical diagrams that man had left behind all those years ago.
He flipped to the third page. Bridge repair.

Before long, the bridge was fixed. He stepped on it to test it.
Solid.
But he left the book where it was.
That way, no one could say he had accepted a favor from a villain.

Mist rose from the mountain ravine. By then it was deep into the night.
Ma Pingshan's breathing grew heavy, and not because he was tired.
The situation in front of him was urgent. A woodcutter had been pinned under a rock so heavy he could not move, and he was already unconscious. If no one saved him now, he would die.
What rotten luck.

Ma Pingshan crouched down and spread open his bundle.
Only one thing was left inside now: a set of sleeve arrows.
Moving the rock would need a lever. Setting the bone would need splints. He had learned both.
So he took apart even the arrow case, split it in two, and used the pieces as splints.

As he tied them in place, he noticed the calluses on the woodcutter's hands, and suddenly remembered things he had never paid attention to before.
His father had had calluses like these too.
But his father was a teacher. That was why there had always been so many pitiful children in their home.

Then how could a teacher's hands have the calluses of someone who gripped a blade?
No... that couldn't be right...
All those children who came and went were only there because they had nowhere else to go...
His father was not a kidnapper. He was not a child trafficker.
The gossip of old neighbors started clamoring in his head again, almost loud enough to drown out the mountain wind.
But whether those children ever stopped crying after they were taken away, he truly did not know.

By the time the woodcutter began to come to, Ma Pingshan rose to his feet.
At that moment, he had nothing left.
The mist had started to thin.

Looking up, he saw Dragonbend Academy not far ahead.
In his heart, he had walked this road of revenge over and over again for ten years.
Ma Pingshan gave the road behind him one last look.
The mountain path twisted through the thin mist like a scar, one that seemed to be trying to heal even as it pulled itself open again.

A line from a book suddenly came back to him:
"In this world, black and white are not judged by what the eye sees, but by what the heart knows."

He turned back and walked on.
Zì Xián

Dear Wanderer,

How are you? I write with glad tidings. Thanks to your help, I've set up my stall at the Wheatwind Bazaar in Kaifeng Suburbs-South. When I left home, I never dreamed such a day…

But the weather's been cruel this year, drought and flood by turns. The harvest would likely suffer… May the land prove worthy.

他一眼就能算清，一把凳子需木材几何，一座桥需石材几何，一艘天下无双的五牙大舰，又需建材几何。匠人按他说的材料数量，造成一物能做到分毫都不浪费。
胡算盘在金明池的后方，算人力、算物力、算财力，没算到一场大火，烧光了百工多年的辛劳。
唉，无妨，无妨……胡算盘扫过沿着水流漂出来的碎木、残渣、只剩半个的齿轮。
哎、哎！胡算盘赶紧拍拍围观的将士。快捞、快捞！这还能做成——
#Y【司南】——做成指路司南绰绰有余，行商可喜欢着呢！#E
en:
From the old dynasty to Kaifeng today, from the villages to the Imperial Artisan Court and Masterwood Hamlet, everyone praised Accountant Hu as a truly masterful human abacus.
With one glance, he could tell exactly how much timber a stool would need, how much stone a bridge would take, and how much material it would cost to build a peerless Quintadent Warship. By following his exact calculations, the artisans could craft an object without wasting a single sliver.
Working behind the scenes at Jinming Pool, Accountant Hu had counted labor, supplies, and funds, yet he had not counted on a fire that would reduce years of efforts to ashes.
"Alas, let it be..." Accountant Hu's eyes swept over the broken wood drifting with the current, the scattered wreckage, and a half-broken gear.
"Hey, hey!" Accountant Hu hurriedly patted the soldiers watching nearby. "Quick, fish it out! This can still be made into...
#Y[a compass] It's more than enough to be made into a guiding compass. Traveling merchants will absolutely love it!"#E

其一  看门狗

其三  卖命钱
卖命钱，白花花，
拿了银钱好归家。
爹说去去就回来，
娘把铜钱缝衣下。
我一口，娘一口，
鱼粥喝完等灯花，
花灭不见爹回家。
en:
The First: The Watchdog
A dog sits by the tavern gate,
Silent to men, but howls at gold's weight.
When copper coin comes, its tail wags free,
When gold arrives, it crawls on its knee.
They say this beast was once a man,
Who traded his conscience for a silver span.
Gold and silver rot the heart within,
Now a mangy dog, groveling in sin.

The Second: The Person in the Coffin
The Mad Man kills with naught but blade,
Boasts to all of the trade he's made.
Heads roll today, he laughs the morrow,
Blood as wine, and lives as straw to borrow.
The Dragon King of the shoal lifts but a hand,
And living men drift coffined from the land.

The Third: Blood Money
Blood money, gleaming white,
Take the silver, go home tonight.
Father said he'd soon return,
Mother stitched the coin, her hands did churn.
A bite for me, a bite for her,
Fish porridge gone, still no sight—
Father never came home that night.

6.唯有抱着批判之思，方能进步。

en:
To all Mohist City disciples: Welcome!
To keep your studies and life here running smoothly and safely, please follow these rules after class:

1. If you hear whispering from the Hanging House, don't respond or engage.
2. If you don't understand an elder's advice right away, take three days to ponder it before asking again.
3. Mohist City doesn't have any "Smart Newsie" communication devices. If anyone tries to sell you one, do not buy it.
4. When studying late by candlelight, be careful not to doze off and accidentally knock over the flame.
5. There is nothing wrong with the Elders' hair. If you spot stray tresses or wigs anywhere, do not touch them under any circumstances.
6. Keep a questioning mind; that's the key to true progress.

Stick to these rules, and you'll sail confidently through your studies and enjoy a fulfilling journey here!

王芬失去女儿的那一天，是个明媚的春日。
她去庄稼田里收了半天稻谷，回来时一路盘算着，要给女儿做顿好吃的。
她那漂亮的女儿啊，是方圆几里村子里，出落得最好的一个。她感到骄傲，又感到愧疚。她想把最好的一切都给她。可她那懂事的，乖巧的女儿啊，总是什么都不要，什么也不求。
问她，她就说，只想跟娘亲，一直一直在一起。
好吧。王芬认真思考了几日后，心里头想着，她的女儿，乖巧又懂事，去了外头，兴许会受委屈。如果她想，她就一直一直留在自己身边也无妨。

可她回到家后，却找不见女儿了。她丈夫的两个哥哥低着头不说话，她那懦弱的丈夫也不说话。
她感到不安，冲出家门。而隔壁的刘奶奶抹着眼泪告诉她。
卖了，被卖了啊。
卖去哪了？
不知道。
已经过去了半日，马车的车轱辘印消失在山野中，方向无从找寻。
王芬沉默了半晌，回屋换了双鞋子，奔进了山林里……

她那漂亮的，懂事的，乖巧的女儿啊……她找了她一年又一年，一年又一年。
鞋子早就破了，有路过的好心人送了她一双新的。但新的又破了……一双又一双，她还是走在路上。
就这样，不知道过去了多少年，也不知道自己眼下到了何方。
王芬唱着那首女儿最喜欢的歌谣，拉着每一个过路的人，反反复复的问。
我有一个顶漂亮的女儿，你见过她吗？
en:
The day Wang Fen lost her daughter dawned bright with spring sunshine.
She'd spent half the day harvesting rice in the fields, planning all the way home what delicious meal she'd cook for the girl.
Her beautiful daughter, the loveliest girl in all the surrounding villages. Pride swelled in Wang Fen's chest, followed by guilt. She wanted to give the child every good thing in this world. Yet that thoughtful, sweet-natured girl never asked for anything. When asked, she'd say, "I just want to stay with Mother forever."
After days of consideration, Wang Fen decided: Perhaps it's better this way. The world beyond their home might wound such a gentle soul. If her daughter wished to remain by her side forever, so be it.

But when she returned, the girl was gone. Her husband's two brothers hung their heads in silence, her spineless husband wouldn't meet her eyes.
A chill running down her spine, Wang Fen dashed outside. Grannie Liu next door wiped her tears and told her. 
"She was sold. They sold her."
"Where?"
"No one knows."
Half a day had already passed. The wagon tracks had vanished into the wilderness, leaving no trail to follow.
Wang Fen stood motionless for a long moment. Then she turned, changed her shoes, and ran into the mountains...

Her beautiful, sensible, sweet daughter... she searched year after year, decade after decade.
Her shoes wore through. Kind strangers gave her new pairs. Those, too, wore through... Pair after pair, still she walked.
Years blurred into one, her feet carrying her nowhere and everywhere.
Singing the lullaby her daughter loved, Wang Fen stopped every passerby, asking the same question, over and over:
"I have a beautiful daughter. Have you seen her?"
Shanyuan Jun

en: When Chestnut was but two months old, the cat cafe owner picked it up from the streets, a small sodden ball of fur, its head like a furry chestnut burr. Once the owner fed it, it clung fast to him ever after. Even when the shop later filled with a crowd of guests, Chestnut would only lie sprawled before its owner, idly batting at its own tail out of boredom. For reasons unknown, Chestnut would not touch fish nor meat, only plain rice. One guest, refusing to believe it, brought over a bowl of watershield fish soup to tempt it. Chestnut took one look, dipped a paw into it, and pressed it square onto the owner's robe. The guest laughed, saying what a strange thing it was, born with the hide of a cat bred to catch fish and mice, yet loving only grains. The owner merely said it was just as well, less trouble that way, though in his heart he felt a deep tenderness for it, guessing that in harder days gone by, Chestnut had known only scraps and leftovers, and so had come to believe that plain rice was the finest thing in all the world.

本届「论剑赛」参赛限制装备最高为86阶，参与比赛的游侠务必保留好86阶【装备】，在比赛中选手的部分战斗属性进行调平（角色和武学等级为90级，心法为6重，奇术为5重9段，装备叠音最高生效四十五重，解锁当前赛季所有通用型止戈天赋），战斗规则沿用论剑玩法规则。

海选初赛开放时间内报名参赛的游侠需要自行前往论剑赛海选界面参与匹配，完成10场海选比赛，胜利4场即可晋级海选复赛。

海选复赛开放时间内，晋级复赛的游侠需要自行前往论剑赛海选界面参与匹配，完成14场海选比赛，排名前64名的游侠晋级下一阶段比赛。

小组循环赛比赛开始前15分钟参赛选手可进入准备场景，赛制为单循环积分赛，采用三局两胜制。
【1】匹配机制：系统将于14:00开始自动为各战队匹配未对阵过的对手，
【2】匹配流程：每次返回准备场景后，系统会持续进行新一轮匹配，由于仅匹配未交战的对手，可能出现等待时间较长的情况，请耐心等待。
【3】单循环赛制：需与小组内所有选手完成一轮对阵，小组赛将在所有参赛选手完成相互对阵后结束。
审核时间结束后各小组第一名晋级八强胜者组、第二名晋级八强败者组，奖励在审核期结束后领取。

排名规则（优先级）：胜场总数 > 胜场平均用时（计算平均值时，仅计入非轮空的有效胜场数据）。
en:
Players must abide by the Where Winds Meet General Tournament Rules. See the [General Tournament Rules] section on the official Where Winds Meet Tournament Center website. 

The max Gear Tier for this "1v1 Arena Tournament" is Tier 86. Wanderers must keep their Tier 86 [Gear]. Combat attributes will be balanced during the match (Character and Martial Arts Level 90, Inner Ways Tier 6, Mystic Skill Tier 5 Rank 9, Gear Enhancement max 45 stacks, all current season general Arena Talents unlocked). Combat rules follow the 1v1 Arena rules. 

Wanderers registered during the Initial Qualifiers period must proceed to the 1v1 Arena Tournament Qualifiers interface to match. Complete 10 qualifying matches; 4 wins are required to advance to the Secondary Qualifiers. 

During the Secondary Qualifiers, advancing Wanderers must proceed to the 1v1 Arena Tournament Qualifiers interface to match. Complete 14 qualifying matches. The top 64 Wanderers advance to the next stage. 

Participating players can enter the preparation scene 15 minutes before the Group Round Robin match starts. The format is a Single Round Robin tournament, using a Best of 3 format. 
[1] Matchmaking: The system will automatically match players against opponents they haven't fought yet starting at 14:00. 
[2] Process: After returning to the preparation scene, the system will continue to match for the next round. Wait times may be longer as it only matches opponents not yet fought. Please wait patiently. 
[3] Round Robin: Players must complete a match against every other player in the group. The Group Stage ends when all participating players have fought each other. 
After the review time ends, the 1st place of each group advances to the Top 8 Winners Bracket, and the 2nd place advances to the Top 8 Losers Bracket. Rewards are claimed after the review period. 

Ranking Rules (Priority): Total Wins > Avg. Time in Wins (Calculated using only valid winning matches, excluding byes).

zh:
暮色染透天际，不知觉间，已来到了夜晚。
阿景与阿达紧跟张叔，穿街过巷，拐进了雀神争霸赛场。赛场金玉流光，晃得人睁不开眼。阿达衣角不慎扫过石貔貅，竟被咬住半截铜钱。
瓦当间忽然滚落铜钱声，只见张叔手握横刀，“哐啷”砸在青砖上。
张叔口齿不清：“钱……钱……吐出来！……把钱都吐出来！”
两人吓得浑身一颤，阿景攥紧袖，暗自嘀咕：张叔是唱的哪一出？
几个戴金戴银的账房围拢过来。张叔却视若无睹，眼神凌厉如刀：
“你们两个小子，别废话，赶紧去！”
二人目光交汇，心中暗自坚定，这次无论如何，此次绝不能再被这古怪老头白白驱使。他们鼓起勇气，壮起胆子。
阿景握了握已被汗浸湿的衣袖，挺身而出：“从前软弱的我们已经死了！现在站在这里的……”
话未说完，便见府尹缓步走来。他见三人形迹诡异，便上前询问情况。随即，少年人原本打算拒绝的“白工”，便变成了“军令”。
“好吧……现在站在这里的……是更软弱的我们……”阿达哭丧着脸，腰间硬塞的红蛋硌得生疼。
无奈，二人投入了争霸赛中……
经过一番斗智斗勇，他们终于赢得了丰厚的筹码。正当他们兴冲冲地将筹码交给张叔时，张叔却善手一挥，“……钱……分下去……分下去……叫那些奴户来……分下去……”
奴户？哪来的奴户？二人一脸茫然，面面相觑。
而张叔只是满意地点了点头，转身离去，留下二人在风中凌乱。
en:
Dusk washed over the sky, and before they knew it, night had fallen. Jing and Da followed Uncle Zhang closely through the streets and alleys, finally turning into the Mahjong God Challenge arena. The arena glittered with gold and jade, so dazzling it was hard to keep one's eyes open. Da's sleeve accidentally brushed against a stone pixiu, which promptly clamped onto a half-exposed copper coin.
Suddenly, the clatter of rolling coins came from the eaves. They saw Uncle Zhang, Heng Blade in hand, slam it down on the blue bricks with a clang.
Uncle Zhang slurred, "The coin... spit it out! Spit all the money out!"
The two trembled with fear. Jing clenched his sleeve, muttering to himself, "What is Uncle Zhang up to now?"
Several bejeweled accountants gathered around, but Uncle Zhang paid them no heed, his gaze as sharp as a blade. "You two! Stop dawdling and get a move on!"
Their eyes met, a silent resolution forming between them: this time, no matter what, they would not be ordered around by this strange old man for nothing. They mustered their courage.
Jing gripped his sweat-dampened sleeve and stepped forward. "The weaklings we once were are dead! The ones standing here now—"
Before he could finish, the Prefect strolled toward them. Noticing the three acting strangely, he approached to ask what was happening. In an instant, the "voluntary labor" the youths had intended to refuse became a "military order."
"Alright... the ones standing here now... are even weaker than before..." Da said with a pained expression, the eggs stuffed at his waist digging into him.
Helpless, the two threw themselves into the challenge. After a battle of wits and courage, they won a hefty pile of chips. Just as they excitedly handed the chips to Uncle Zhang, he waved his hand magnanimously. "...The money... distribute it... distribute it... call the slaves over... and distribute it..."
Slaves? What slaves? The two looked at each other, utterly confused.
Uncle Zhang simply nodded with satisfaction, turned, and left, leaving them bewildered in the wind.

清音此生，命如蜉蝣，寄身烟花之地，从未奢求真心。
然长街一瞥，陋室欢谈，山盟在耳，犹自难忘。
君言共赴天涯，妾未有半分迟疑，赴君之约。
若钱财万贯可换真心一片，吾不所惜也。
若漂泊江湖可得比翼万里，吾不所怨也。
若清苦一世能得相守终生，吾不所惧也。
长堤苦等三日，未见君至，想来邱郎已有他念。
今日种种虽为错付，然终无所悔。
#Y惟愿此生不见，心中勿念！#E
en:
I, Qing Yin, have lived a humble life, fleeting like a whisper lost in the night. Dwelling in the shadows of the pleasure quarters, I've never dared to hope for true devotion.
Yet that glance on the street, our laughter in that shabby little room, and the vows you whispered—I still cannot forget them. 
You spoke of roaming the world together, and not for a second did I hesitate—I was ready to follow you anywhere. 
If endless wealth could buy but a grain of a true heart, I'd spend every penny without regret.
If a restless life in the jianghu meant a lifetime by your side, I would have welcomed every hardship ahead.
But I waited three days by the river, and you never showed up. It seems your heart had turned elsewhere long before.
Though I gave my trust to the wrong man, I do not regret having loved. 
#YMay our paths never cross again, and may I forget you in this lifetime!#E

zh: 驴肉火烧制作技艺是河北省传统饮食文化之一，2012年被列为省级非物质文化遗产名录。该技艺包含火烧面点制作与驴肉烹制两大核心工艺，相传唐代漕运工人曾以驴肉和面饼作为便携干粮，后经过发展至清代，因御厨传承形成完整技艺体系，现以保定、河间两地为主要传承区域。河间驴肉火烧和保定驴肉火烧最直观的区别在于保定的驴肉火烧是圆形，而河间的驴肉火烧是长方形。

推荐上传单人表演视频，识别效果更佳；
推荐使用画面稳定，且没有人物与镜头切换的视频；
推荐使用人物服装颜色与背景保持明显区分的视频；
在生成表情时，推荐使用全程人脸位于画面内且正对镜头，五官露出清晰的视频；
在生成动作时，推荐使用人物全身清晰可见的视频；
推荐拍摄环境为明亮空旷的区域，昏暗或阴影处可能效果不佳；
上传的视频时长不超过15秒，超时的内容可能丢失处理结果；
推荐分辨率大于720P，人脸在画面中占比高于10%；
目前支持.mp4/.mov/.mkv/.avi格式的视频。
上传一段视频片段或图片，我们的 AI 会从中提取您选择的一项元素——动作、表情或运镜——用于生成一段游戏内的动画或表情动作。
我们会对您的视频片段或图片进行加密，并且在动画或表情动作生成后 7 天，您的原始视频片段或图片会被自动删除。这个时间刚好足够我们在您反馈问题时，修复可能出现的罕见故障。您上传的视频片段或图片不会用于 AI 模型训练。
en:
Video Upload Requirements
1. Use solo performance videos with stable framing
2. Avoid character or camera cuts
3. Ensure clothing contrasts with the background
4. Keep video under 15 seconds
5. Use 720P+ resolution (face should occupy 10%+ of frame)
6. Supported formats: mp4/mov/mkv/avi
For Emotes: Face must stay in frame, facing the camera with clear features
For Poses: Full body must be clearly visible
Environment: Shoot in bright, open areas (avoid shadows)
Privacy: Videos are encrypted and auto-deleted after 7 days. Not used for AI training.

乾祐元年水至此：

三则，水在此稍低田淹；

六则，水在此稍高田淹；
七则，水在此极高田俱淹。
竭不至足，盛不没肩。不知饥馑，时无荒年。

歪扭的刻字：寻水则至此，已为绝路。今生既无缘，来生旦见君。来生愿以此钗为盟……
en:
Barely legible carvings 

Water reached this height during 948 CE: 
First, if the water reaches here, then the field is safe. 
Second, if the water reaches here, then the really low fields are flooded. 
Third, if the water reaches here, then the low fields are also flooded. 
Fourth, if the water reaches here, then the lower-mid fields are also flooded. 
Fifth, if the water reaches here, then the upper-mid fields are also flooded. 
Sixth, if the water reaches here, then the high fields are also flooded. 
Seventh, if the water reaches here, then the really high fields are also flooded. 
The water should not be below the feet during dry years, and should not be above the shoulders during a flood. Then the people shall know no hunger and there will be no bad years.

zh:
六月初五
今日试飞，风自西南而来，风势甚猛。途遇逆风阻挠，颇为不利，致使飞行器未能升空。心中颇感沮丧，然仍决心改良之，再度挑战蓝天。

六月十五
今日试飞，风向偏东，然飞行器犹未能如愿飞翔。虽心中愧疚，然对此器仍怀有信心，将继续修正，期待改日再战蓝天。

六月二十五
今日试飞，中途大雨，仍未能实现飞翔之愿，使我心中倍感失望。但我将随神女步伐，继续改良，誓要让我同此器翱翔苍穹。

七月初五
今日试飞，风势平和，起飞平稳，无奈很快遭树木拦腰，导致多处挫伤，看来要休整一阵子了。望神女在上，保佑错误是成功的必经之路。

七月二十五
再度面对失败，心中满是无奈。

八月初五
今日，我进行了一次大胆的尝试！我忍痛将飞行器拆解，重新拼接了许多零部件，希望能够提升其飞行性能。尝试飞行时，果真似乎有了明显的改善！初步展现出了飞翔的迹象，虽仍未能持续在空中飞行……最终我与一断线纸鸢同时坠于地面之上，但初尝飞行之乐，实在感动！

八月十日
上次落下的腿伤久久未愈，正苦闷于不知何日能重新起飞，幸得路遇一好心人悬壶相救。定是神女显灵，助我飞天之梦！

八月十五
驾改良后的飞行器再度尝试飞行，然而结果依旧与前几次无异。这次的失败，不仅使我双腿骨折，更令我陷入了深深的挣扎之中。可飞行之梦想，岂能说放就放……
en:
5th day of the Sixth Month
During today's test flight, the headwind was so fierce that I couldn't even get it off the ground. Though frustrating, I'll keep working on it.

15th day of the Sixth Month
I tried again with an east wind, but still no luck. Yet I believe in this machine. I have to keep refining. Next time, maybe.

25th day of the Sixth Month
Heavy rain cut today's test short before I could even launch. Disappointed, but I'll keep improving this craft. One day, it will carry me across the sky.

5th day of the Seventh Month
Smooth takeoff today with light winds. Then I hit a tree. Looks like repairs will take a while. Let these failures be the stones that pave the road to success.

25th day of the Seventh Month
I failed again, feeling hopeless and exhausted.

5th day of the Eighth Month
I tore the craft apart and rebuilt it piece by piece. And it worked! In the end, I tumbled to the earth alongside a snapped kite. But that first taste of flight... it was pure magic.

10th day of the Eighth Month
I'm still recovering from the crash. My leg is not healed yet. A kind stranger helped me today. Surely the Goddess is watching, guiding my dream of flight!

15th day of the Eighth Month
I tried again with the rebuilt craft. Same result. What was worse, I even broke my leg this time. I'm in despair. But how can I give up on the dream of flight now?

“方才那个高了些，那小短腿踮着脚也够不着吧？”
“那个淡了……再补一个！”
嘟嘟囔囔的，天不收又往回走了。
几百米的山路，篓里只躺着几株灵芝，日头却已顺着他的脊背，暖融融地爬到了肩头。
en:
Unfated Tian never stopped complaining about the children following him. Still, his hands were kinder than his mouth.
He carved trail marks into the rock as he walked. A few steps, one mark. A few more, another.
"That last one's too high. Those little legs won't reach it."
"And that one is fading. Better cut it deeper."
Grumbling to himself, he turned back again.
By the time he was done, he'd barely gathered a few lingzhi. The sun, meanwhile, had already climbed from the middle of his back to his shoulders.

无患崖的穷奇师间流传着一则怪谈，说是有只小狗白日见不到，夜里生龙活虎。
而山民们也奇怪，这小狗仅吃白日一顿，体型却日益壮硕。
想必此狗，不是凡狗。
一日傍晚，两方一个早了，一个迟了，竟同时端着饭盆走来。就在两边面面相觑之时，却见小狗先奔向穷奇师摇了摇尾巴，又跑回山民处打了个滚。在左边的盆吃一口，右边的盆舔一嘴。
不白来，都不白来，两边送的，狗都爱吃。
自那以后，怪谈小狗就变成了小狗饭盆。
en:
A strange tale circulated among the Qiongqi Artificers of Brighthale Cliff about a little dog that was nowhere to be seen during the day but became lively and vigorous at night.
The mountain folk also wondered why the dog only ate one meal during the day yet grew sturdier by the day.
Surely, this was no ordinary dog.
One evening, two groups, one early, one late, walked up with food bowls at the same time. While they stared at each other in surprise, the dog first ran to the Qiongqi Artificer and wagged its tail, then ran back to the mountain folk and rolled over. It took a bite from the left bowl and a lick from the right.
Neither came in vain; the dog loved everything they brought.
Since then, the "Ghost Dog" became "Bowlly."

秦川有一种老狐狸，想要变成人，就得偷吃人的精气。它不咬别处，专吃人的脚趾头。
有个靠跑商发家的张老爷，晚上总要唤两个暖脚婢伺候。半夜，床底下有动静，他装睡偷看却发现，从床底下钻出来一只狗那么大的狐狸，眼睛通红，像人一样站起来，枯树枝似的爪子掀开他被子，捧起他左脚就咬小趾头，而两个暖脚婢却睡死过去。
张老爷疼得要命，却浑身僵硬，喊不出也动不了。只见狐狸咬得带劲，喉咙里发出怪声，牙上还带着血光。咬完，狐狸眼里的红光淡了点，居然像人一样咧嘴一笑，然后钻回床底不见了。
张老爷能动后一看，小指头差点咬断，血肉模糊。怪的是，伤好后那小指头变得像石头一样又冷又硬，没知觉了。而事后那两个暖脚婢却毫不知情。
en:
There is a breed of ancient fox in Qinchuan that must steal the vital essence of humans to take on a human form. It bites nowhere else. Just the toes.
Master Zhang, a merchant who made his fortune on the road, always kept two bed-warming maids to serve him at night. At midnight, hearing a rustle beneath his bed, he feigned sleep and peeked. From under the bed crawled a fox as large as a hound. Its eyes glowing a blood-red hue, it stood on its hind legs like a man. With claws like withered branches, it pulled back his quilt, lifted his left foot, and began gnawing on his little toe. Strangely, the two maids slept on like the dead.
The pain was excruciating, yet Zhang's body went completely rigid; he could neither scream nor move. He could only watch the fox chew vigorously, emitting eerie rasps from its throat, its teeth glinting with blood. After the feast, the red glow in its eyes dimmed. It flashed a hideous, human-like grin before diving back under the bed and vanishing.
When Zhang finally regained his movement, he found his little toe nearly severed into a bloody pulp. The strange thing was, after the wound healed, that toe became as cold and hard as stone, completely devoid of feeling. As for the two maids, they remained entirely oblivious to the night's horrors.
