——正文——

（先吹曲破，把色断送）

（末泥扮窦谔上，云）冤屈！

（末泥唱）夏日炎炎汗煮汤，只为艺业不敢荒。谁料中暑石上卧，扁毛畜生欺我在。若在平时三招胜，怎奈热毒胜刀枪……

（副净扮大鹅上，逐之。末泥奔走，跌科。副净立石上，笑云）什么梨园子弟，连我鹅爷爷都打不过！

（外扮师父内喊，云）窦谔啊，功夫还不到家，再加练八个时辰罢。

（末泥起，羞愤科）

（末泥唱）非我不能打，实是中暑头脑晕、手脚软！苍天在上，怎将我这苦艺人作耍？厚土为凭，怎的也把良善来作践？

（末泥云）我窦谔立誓——

（末泥唱）但教我消得此怨，叫那大鹅三年大汗、汗浸白练，更要六月飞雪，方解我恼！

（末泥云）剧名——《斗鹅冤》！

（下）

——杂扮一段——

（副末上，云）后来？那鹅被客人点了铁锅炖，已吃了。正是：铁锅炖了横行物，中暑冤消一笑无。

（并下）
en:
There was a Masked Troupe Disciple named Dou E, who trained diligently through the dog days of summer. Having finished his practice, with sweat pouring down like rain, he grew dizzy from the heat and lay down upon a stone to rest a while. Suddenly a great goose came pecking at him; though Dou E could ordinarily have bested it with ease, being overcome by the heat, he was defeated and fled. His master, witnessing this, ordered him to train eight additional hours as punishment. And so Dou E composed this drama to cry out his injustice.

- Main Text -

(First, the overture is played; the Scene-Setter announces the prologue.)

(Actor in the leading male role enters as Dou E, and speaks) Injustice most foul!

(Leading male sings) The blazing summer sun boils my sweat like broth, yet dare I not neglect my craft. Who could have known that lying dizzied upon a stone, I'd be bullied by a feather-brained beast! Were it any ordinary day, three strokes would see it beaten, but alas, the poison of the heat proved mightier than blade or spear...

(Actor in the comedic villain role enters as the Goose, chasing him. The leading male runs and takes a comedic fall. The comedic villain stands on the rock, laughing and speaking:) Some Masked Troupe Disciple you are, unable even to best a mere Goose!

(Actor in the supporting role as the Master shouts from offstage, speaking:) Dou E! Your skill is not yet refined enough. Rain eight more hours!

(Leading male gets up, acting ashamed and furious)

(Leading male sings) Unless this grievance of mine be redressed, let that great goose sweat through three years of summers till its white feathers are soaked through, and let snow fall in the sixth month besides. Only then shall my anger be appeased!

(Leading male speaks) The title of this drama: The Goose's Grievance!

(Exit)

- A Comic Interlude -

(Actor in the narrator role enters and speaks) And afterward? Why, that goose was ordered stewed in an iron pot by a guest, and has already been eaten. Indeed, as the saying goes: the unruly creature was stewed in an iron pot, and with a laugh, the grievance of the heatstroke was dissolved entirely.

zh:
和尚家贫，幼入囫囵庙学佛，六岁时诵经，忽发疑问：既有佛经，世间缘何不见佛陀？师父震怒，罚和尚闭门思过。月余间，和尚苦苦思过，愈思愈不解，疑问从此而生，愈生愈多。若有佛陀，佛陀是否真有神通？佛陀所著佛法，是否真能令人解脱？师父常说修戒定慧，此真能戒除烦恼？和尚虽百思不得其解，但真理愈问愈明，何不多问一二？和尚一生所求，不过寻得佛法之真谛，若不提问一二，何知真理如何？多思多问，自然能了悟佛法真妙，不思不问，恐怕常限偏狭之中。故汇总归纳和尚多年来对佛法的三千疑问，以示佛家弟子，若观者能由此了悟，则为和尚之幸，亦为观者之幸，观者即为众生，此即为众生之幸，能以和尚一问普度众生，便不枉和尚苦思冥想，笔录此卷，善哉、善哉。
……
佛法有云，大千世界，一千“小世界”为一小千世界，一千“小千世界”为一中千世界，一千“中千世界”为一大千世界，故称“三千大千世界”。此三千非彼三千，佛祖有云，一尘含数刹，是为此理，三非数学之三，而是动生之三，和尚之三千疑问亦如三千大千世界，一千个小疑问为一小千问，一千小千问为一中千问，一千中千问为一大千问，故称“佛法三千问”。
……
释迦牟尼佛、金刚不坏佛、宝光佛、龙尊王佛、精进军佛、精进喜佛、宝火佛、宝月光佛、现无愚佛、宝月佛、无垢佛、离垢佛、勇施佛、清净佛、清净施佛、婆留那佛、水天佛、坚德佛、旃檀功德佛、无量掬光佛、光德佛、无忧德佛、那罗延佛、功德华佛、莲华光游戏神通佛、财功德佛、德念佛、善名称功德如来、红炎幢王如来、善游步功德如来、斗战胜如来、善游步如来、周匝庄严功德如来、宝华游步如来、宝莲华善住娑罗树王如来、锭光佛、光远佛、月光佛、旃檀光佛、善山王佛、须弥天冠佛、须弥等曜佛、月色佛、正念佛、离垢佛、无著佛、龙天佛、夜光佛、安明顶佛、不动地佛、琉璃妙华佛、琉璃金色佛、金藏佛、焰光佛、焰根佛、地动佛、月像佛、日音佛、解脱华佛、庄严光明佛、海觉神通佛、水光佛、大香佛、离尘垢佛、舍厌意佛、宝焰佛、妙顶佛、勇立佛、功德持慧佛、蔽日月光佛、日月琉璃光佛、无上琉璃光佛、最上首佛、菩提华佛、月明佛、日光佛、华色王佛、水月光佛、除痴暝佛、度盖行佛、净信佛、善宿佛、威神佛、法慧佛、鸾音佛、师子音佛、龙音佛、处世佛，此为八十八佛，那么问题来了，和尚百思不得其解，为什么是八十八佛，不是八十七佛，也不是八十九佛，八十八这个数字是为了吉利么？此为第一大千问。
《长阿含经》为什么叫长《阿含经》？既有长《阿含经》，是否当有短《阿含经》？又是否当有不长不短《阿含经》？《大悲咒》为什么叫大《悲咒》？既有大《悲咒》，是否当有小《悲咒》？又是否当有不大不小《普通悲咒》？有‘八吉祥’‘六吉祥’‘八菩萨’‘六菩萨’，究竟是六还是八，又或者还有‘四吉祥’‘四菩萨’乃至更多？佛经中各经各律各论，究竟是何人命名，又是何人解读？命名是否有根据，解读又是否正确无误？和尚不解，此为第二大千问。
小乘佛教有多小，大乘佛教有多大，既有大、小二乘佛教，是否当有不大不小中乘佛教？小乘佛教在先，为何反而为小，大乘佛教在后，为何反而为大？大乘佛教真的比小乘佛教高明么，小乘佛教又低在何处？既然众生平等，佛家亦当如此，为何还分大小高低？佛家内部缘何又有上座部、大众部，又有十八部、二十部，更有空宗、有宗，乃至华严宗、法相宗、律宗、禅宗、密宗，林林总总，何为正统？和尚不解，此为第三大千问。
……
三大千问之外，和尚亦有各中千问、小千问、小问，成千上万，不计其数，和尚随行随问，生也有涯，问却无穷，故另起一卷，笔录和尚修行途中诸般中千问、小千问及小问。此卷书页有余，且暂录数问，与观者同思同悟同享。
……
苦谛说人有八苦，生、老、病、死、爱别离、怨憎会、求不得、五蕴炽盛，若有人生而不老便死，又当何论？
若有人生而不病便死，又当何论？
若有人不生便死，又当何论？
若有人无所爱之物，如何爱别离？
若有人无所憎之物，如何怨憎会？
若有人应有尽有，如何求不得？
若有人天生痴呆，无知无识，又体格健硕，如何五蕴集聚在身？
……
佛家有四谛，又有三谛圆融，为何只融三谛，另一谛当如何处置？
所融三谛为哪三谛，不融的那一谛又为何不融？
难道是任选三谛圆融，任弃一谛不融？
……
（似乎是迫于纸页有限，后面的字越写越小，几如蝇头，全然看不清了）
en:
Born into an impoverished family, I studied Buddhism at Hulun Temple. While chanting sutras at six, I doubted: If the sutras exist, why is no Buddha seen in the world? The master, enraged, confined me to reflection. For months, I pondered, only for doubts to multiply. If the Buddha exists, does he possess divine power? Can his teachings liberate the people? The master speaks of discipline, meditation, and wisdom. Do these truly end sufferings? Puzzled still, I believed that truth reveals itself through questioning. If I do not ask, how will I know? To seek the essence of the Dharma, I must inquire. Thus, I compile my three thousand doubts, hoping they may enlighten others. If so, it would be my fortune and theirs too. For if even one being awakens through my questions, then my labor is not in vain....

The Dharma teaches that in the vast cosmos, a thousand small worlds form a small chiliocosm, a thousand small chiliocosms form a medium chiliocosm, and a thousand medium chiliocosms form a great chiliocosm, hence the name "three thousand great chiliocosms." But this three thousand is not that three thousand. The Buddha once said, "A single speck of dust contains countless realms," illustrating this truth. Three here is not a numerical value but a dynamic, generative three. Similarly, my three thousand doubts are like the three thousand great chiliocosms: A thousand small queries form a small chilio-query; A thousand small chilio-queries form a medium chilio-query; A thousand medium chilio-queries form a great chilio-query. Thus, they are called "Three Thousand Queries of Dharma."...

The sutras speak of eighty-eight buddhas: Śākyamuni, Vajra-Indestructible, Jeweled Light, Dragon-Sovereign, Vigorous Striver, Joyous Striver, Jeweled Flame, Jeweled Moonlight, Non-Folly Manifest, Moonlight, Stainless, Free-from-Stain, Courageous Giver, Pure, Pure Giver, Varuṇa, Water-Celestial, Steadfast Virtue, Sandalwood-Merit, Boundless Light-Grasper, Luminous Virtue, Sorrowless Virtue, Nārāyaṇa, Merit-Blossom, Lotus-Light Playful Miracle, Wealth-Merit, Virtue-Remembrance, Well-Renowned Merit Tathāgata, Blazing Banner King Tathāgata, Well-Treading Merit Tathāgata, Victorious in Battle Tathāgata, Well-Treading Tathāgata, Universally Adorned Merit Tathāgata, Jeweled Blossom Treading Tathāgata, Jeweled Lotus Firmly Abiding Śāla King Tathāgata, Dīpaṃkara, Far-Shining Light, Moonlight, Sandalwood Radiance, Virtuous Mountain King, Sumeru-Crowned, Sumeru-Equal Splendor, Moon-Form, Right Mindfulness, Stain-Free, Non-Attachment, Dragon-Celestial, Night Radiance, Peaceful Summit, Immovable Ground, Lapis Lazuli Wonder-Blossom, Lapis Lazuli Golden, Golden Treasury, Flame Light, Flame Root, Earth-Shaker, Moon-Image, Sun-Sound, Liberation Blossom, Majestic Light, Ocean-Wake Miracle, Water Light, Great Fragrance, Free-from-Dust, Disgust-Abandoning Mind, Jeweled Flame, Wondrous Summit, Courageous Stand, Merit-Holding Wisdom, Eclipse of Sun and Moon, Sun-Moon Lapis Lazuli Light, Supreme Lapis Lazuli Light, Foremost Leader, Bodhi Blossom, Moon Brightness, Sunlight, Blossom-Color King, Water-Moonlight, Delusion-Dispelling, Cover-Crossing, Pure Faith, Virtuous Abode, Majestic Power, Dharma-Wisdom, Phoenix-Voice, Lion-Voice, Dragon-Voice, World-Dwelling. But why eighty-eight? Not eighty-seven or eighty-nine? Is the number chosen for auspiciousness? This is the First Great Thousandfold Queries.Why is the Dīrgha Āgama called the Long Āgama? If there is a Long Āgama, should there not be a Short Āgama? And perhaps a Medium-Length Āgama? Why is the Great Compassion Mantra "great"? If there is a Great Compassion Mantra, should there not be a Small Compassion Mantra? Or an Average Compassion Mantra? There are the Eight Auspicious Signs and the Six Auspicious Signs, the Eight Bodhisattvas and the Six Bodhisattvas. Why six or eight? Are there also Four Auspicious Signs or Four Bodhisattvas? Who named these texts? Who interpreted them? Are the names justified? Are the interpretations flawless? This is the Second Great Thousandfold Queries.
How small is Hinayana ("Lesser Vehicle")? How great is Mahayana ("Greater Vehicle")? If there are two, should there not be a Middle Vehicle? Hinayana came first. Why is it "lesser"? Mahayana came later. Why is it "greater"? Is Mahayana truly superior? If all beings are equal, why rank teachings? Why are there Theravāda and Mahāsāṃghika, eighteen or twenty schools, Mādhyamika and Yogācāra, Huayan, Faxiang, Vinaya, Chan, Esoteric, so many divisions? Which is orthodox? This is the Third Great Thousandfold Queries....

Beyond these, I have countless lesser queries: middle-thousandfold, small-thousandfold, and minor. Life is short, but doubt is endless. So I write another book to record all these queries of different types as I practice Buddhism. The book only records several queries, and I invite readers to ponder together....Eight sufferings include birth, aging, sickness, death, parting from loved ones, meeting the hated, unfulfilled desires, the skandhas' torment. But what of one who is born, does not age, and dies?
Or one born without sickness, then dying?
Or one who dies without being born?
If one loves nothing, how can they suffer parting?
If one hates nothing, how can they suffer meeting?
If one lacks nothing, how can they suffer unfulfilled desires?
If one is born witless yet robust, how do the skandhas torment them?...

Buddhism speaks of Four Noble Truths, yet also of "Three Truths in Perfect Harmony." Why harmonize only three? What of the fourth?
Which three are harmonized? Why exclude the fourth?
Or is it arbitrary? Any three, discarding one?... (The writing grows smaller, cramped, until it fades into illegibility.)
Heh, nothing that fancy.

突然，在一旁看了许久的妙妙喵猫步轻巧地跳到它们面前，舔了舔爪子，开了尊口：“本喵有一妙计。喵认识一位游侠，热心、厉害又仗义。何不把宝贝交与游侠保管？”
大聪明心下一喜，诶？这就对了，那大侠顶顶厉害，把宝贝交给大侠，这样就再也不用担心宝贝的安危了。
众狗听得尾巴直摇，兴奋地大呼“喵哇，妙哇！”
得快点行动才行！这宝贝一天不给大侠，大聪明就一天也不得安宁。
它赶紧把宝贝都埋了起来。自己则日夜守在显眼处，只盼游侠快快来，早日把宝贝交给游侠。
en:
Big Smart, Jingle from Kaifeng Prefecture, and Big Ears from the Forsaken Quarter are having a meeting. Jingle brings news: Skilled thieves in black robes in the city can steal treasures in the blink of an eye.
As they say, better a thief steal than a thief scheme. Big Smart figures those black robes will eventually target his treasure, his cloth tiger.
But after woofing at each other for ages, glancing back and forth, none of them has any good ideas.
Suddenly, Meow Meow, who has been watching nearby, pads over lightly. She licks her paw and deigns to speak: "I have a brilliant plan. I know a wanderer who is kind, capable, and loyal. Why not entrust your treasures to him?"
Big Smart's heart leaps. Yes! That's it! Give him the treasures, and never worry again!
All the dogs wag their tails excitedly, barking, "Meow-velous! Purr-fect!"
They must act fast. Until the wanderer has his treasure, Big Smart cannot rest easy.
He quickly buries everything, then stands guard in plain sight day and night, hoping the wanderer will come soon.

从昔年的前朝，到今日的开封，从山野到百工坊到梓匠居，人人都夸，胡算盘真是个好算盘。
他一眼就能算清，一把凳子需木材几何，一座桥需石材几何，一艘天下无双的五牙大舰，又需建材几何。匠人按他说的材料数量，造成一物能做到分毫都不浪费。
胡算盘在金明池的后方，算人力、算物力、算财力，没算到一场大火，烧光了百工多年的辛劳。
唉，无妨，无妨……胡算盘扫过沿着水流漂出来的碎木、残渣、只剩半个的齿轮。
哎、哎！胡算盘赶紧拍拍围观的将士。快捞、快捞！这还能做成——
⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛
en:
From the old dynasty to Kaifeng today, from the villages to the Imperial Artisan Court and Masterwood Hamlet, everyone praised Accountant Hu as a truly masterful human abacus.
With one glance, he could tell exactly how much timber a stool would need, how much stone a bridge would take, and how much material it would cost to build a peerless Quintadent Warship. By following his exact calculations, the artisans could craft an object without wasting a single sliver.
Working behind the scenes at Jinming Pool, Accountant Hu had counted labor, supplies, and funds, yet he had not counted on a fire that would reduce years of efforts to ashes.
"Alas, let it be..." Accountant Hu's eyes swept over the broken wood drifting with the current, the scattered wreckage, and a half-broken gear.
"Hey, hey!" Accountant Hu hurriedly patted the soldiers watching nearby. "Quick, fish it out! This can still be made into..."

zh: 汉刘向采自古圣贤之迹，辑为母仪、贤明、仁智、贞节等七篇，以著妇人懿行，乃中国第一部专记女子事迹之传记。《汉书·艺文志》列于诸子略儒家类；至《隋书·经籍志》始移入史部。其书非独矜持节烈，亦多记才女、辩士，足令后世知妇人亦能以智勇立言建功，垂范千古。
en: Liu Xiang of the Han dynasty gathered accounts from the deeds of ancient sages and worthies, compiling them into seven chapters: on Maternal Virtue, Worthy Enlightenment, Benevolent Wisdom, Chaste Fidelity, and more, so as to set down the admirable conduct of women. It stands as the first biographical work in China devoted entirely to the deeds of women. The Book of Han: Treatise on Literature placed it among the Confucian texts in the section on various schools of thought; it was not until the Book of Sui: Treatise on Classics that it was moved into the section on history. The work does not concern itself solely with chastity and moral steadfastness. It records in great number women of talent and eloquence, making clear to later ages that women too could establish their words and accomplish deeds through wisdom and courage, leaving a model for all generations to come.

玄元教徒之间，不互示面貌，但邓一灯却能一眼认出带他玩的几个兄弟。
只要叫一声兄弟，几个人就会围在一块。或是聊些趣事，或是切磋技艺，总之比看大门有趣多了。
几人围坐，有一人突发奇想。若是脱了这一身玄元教服，大家出去行走江湖，岂不快哉？
另一人赶忙捂了他的嘴。教内规矩森严，离教者离药，必死无疑。怎么就这么大喇喇说出来？
又一人点点头。这种事情，得从长计议。
邓一灯看着面前几个兄弟，想起自己从前混江湖的时光，好似过了好多年岁。
邓一灯轻轻拍了下大腿，说也算我一个。
从那日起，不知何时，他们的小圈子就会少一人。
邓一灯知道这是什么信号。
仅剩的两个兄弟拍拍他的肩头，让邓一灯好好替他们值班，他们再试一次。
邓一灯又做回了看大门的活计。他偷懒、打盹、玩石子，就是不肯挪开一下脚步。
他要等兄弟回来。
en:
Xuanyuan disciples never showed their true faces, but Deng Yideng could recognize these few at a glance.
All it took was a call of "brother," and they'd gather. Sometimes they swapped stories, sometimes they traded a few moves, anything was better than rotting at the gate.
Once, sitting together, one of them suddenly blurted out an idea: what if they ditched the cult robes and went roaming the Jianghu together? Wouldn't that be freedom?
Another clamped a hand over his mouth at once. Rules were ironclad here. To leave meant cutting off the antidote. Certain death. You don't just blurt that out.
A third nodded slowly. If such a thing were ever to happen, it would take careful planning.
Deng Yideng looked at the brothers before him and, all at once, memories of his old drifting days came flooding back. It felt like a lifetime ago.
He slapped his thigh, "Count me in."
After that, he wasn't sure when it started, but every so often, someone would be missing from their group.
Deng Yideng knew exactly what that meant.
In the end, the last two clapped him on the shoulder, told him to keep watch, and said they'd try again.
Deng Yideng returned to his post at the gate. He slacked off, dozed, and skipped stones, but he refused to budge a single step.
He's waiting for his brothers to come home.

The only certainty was the occasional text, books, and paintings during the Heroes Assembly, while the relationship between the Shimmer and the Velvet Shade, how they communicated, and the Shimmer's whereabouts remained mysteries.

zh:
【序卦】

有天地，然后万物生焉。
盈天地之间者唯万物，故受之以屯。屯者，盈也。屯者，物之始生也。
物生必蒙，故受之以蒙。蒙者，蒙也，物之稚也。
物稚不可不养也，故受之以需。需者，饮食之道也。
饮食必有讼，故受之以讼。
讼必有众起，故受之以师。师者，众也。
众必有所比，故受之以比。比者，比也。
比必有所畜，故受之以小畜。
物畜然后有礼，故受之以履。
履而泰然后安，故受之以泰。泰者，通也。
物不可以终通，故受之以否。
物不可以终否，故受之以同人。
与人同者，物必归焉，故受之以大有。
有大者不可以盈，故受之以谦。
有大而能谦必豫，故受之以豫。
豫必有随，故受之以随。
以喜随人者必有事，故受之以蛊。蛊者，事也。
有事而后可大，故受之以临。临者，大也。
物大然后可观，故受之以观。
可观而后有所合，故受之以噬嗑。嗑者，合也。
物不可以苟合而已，故受之以贲。贲者，饰也。
致饰然后亨则尽矣，故受之以剥。剥者，剥也。
物不可以终尽剥，穷上反下，故受之以复。
复则不妄矣，故受之以无妄。
有无妄，然后可畜，故受之以大畜。
物畜然后可养，故受之以颐。颐者，养也。
不养则不可动，故受之以大过。
物不可以终过，故受之以坎。坎者，陷也。
陷必有所丽，故受之以离。离者，丽也。
……
en:
【Sequence of Hexagrams】

When there were Heaven and Earth, then all things were produced.
What fills Heaven and Earth is only all things, hence it is followed by Zhun. Zhun means fullness. Zhun is the beginning of the birth of all things.
When things are born, they must be in a state of ignorance, hence it is followed by Meng. Meng means ignorance, the infancy of things.
When things are in infancy, they must be nurtured, hence it is followed by Xu. Xu is the way of food and drink.
With food and drink there must be disputes, hence it is followed by Song.
With disputes there must be the rise of multitudes, hence it is followed by Shi. Shi means multitudes.
Multitudes must have something to which they adhere, hence it is followed by Bi. Bi means adherence.
With adherence there must be accumulation, hence it is followed by Xiao Xu.
When things are accumulated, then there is propriety, hence it is followed by Lü.
When one treads and becomes prosperous, then there is peace, hence it is followed by Tai. Tai means smoothness and success.
Things cannot remain forever in smoothness, hence it is followed by Pi.
Things cannot remain forever in obstruction, hence it is followed by Tong Ren.
When one is in harmony with others, things must return to him, hence it is followed by Da You.
One who possesses much cannot afford to be arrogant, hence it is followed by Qian.
One who possesses much and can be humble must be joyful, hence it is followed by Yu.
With joy there must be followers, hence it is followed by Sui.
One who follows others with delight must have affairs, hence it is followed by Gu. Gu means affairs.
When there are affairs, then one can become great, hence it is followed by Lin. Lin means greatness.
When things are great, then they can be observed, hence it is followed by Guan.
When they can be observed, then there is union, hence it is followed by Shi He. He means union.
Things cannot be united merely carelessly, hence it is followed by Bi. Bi means adornment.
When adornment is carried to the utmost, then prosperity comes to an end, hence it is followed by Bo. Bo means stripping away.
Things cannot be stripped away to the very end; when the top is exhausted, it returns to the bottom, hence it is followed by Fu.
With return, there is no delusion, hence it is followed by Wu Wang.
When there is no delusion, then one can accumulate, hence it is followed by Da Xu.
When things are accumulated, then they can be nourished, hence it is followed by Yi. Yi means nourishment.
Without nourishment, one cannot act, hence it is followed by Da Guo.
Things cannot remain forever in excess, hence it is followed by Kan. Kan means a pit or peril.
When one is in peril, he must have something to cling to, hence it is followed by Li. Li means attachment.
……

zh:
【微子第十八】

微子去之，箕子为之奴，比干谏而死。孔子曰：“殷有三仁焉。”
柳下惠为士师，三黜。人曰：“子未可以去乎？”曰：“直道而事人，焉往而不三黜？枉道而事人，何必去父母之邦？”
齐景公待孔子曰：“若季氏，则吾不能。”以季、孟之间待之，曰：“吾老矣，不能用也。”孔子行。
齐人归女乐，季桓子受之，三日不朝，孔子行。
楚狂接舆歌而过孔子曰：“凤兮凤兮，何德之衰？往者不可谏，来者犹可追。已而已而，今之从政者殆而！”孔子下，欲与之言，趋而辟之，不得与之言。
长沮、桀溺耦而耕，孔子过之，使子路问津焉。长沮曰：“夫执舆者为谁？”子路曰：“为孔丘。”曰：“是鲁孔丘与？”曰：“是也。”曰：“是知津矣。”问于桀溺，桀溺曰：“子为谁？”曰：“为仲由。”曰：“是鲁孔丘之徒与？”对曰：“然。”曰：“滔滔者天下皆是也，而谁以易之？且而与其从辟人之士也，岂若从辟世之士？”耰而不辍。子路行以告，夫子怃然曰：“鸟兽不可与同群，吾非斯人之徒与而谁与？天下有道，丘不与易也。”
子路从而后，遇丈人，以杖荷蓧。子路问曰：“子见夫子乎？”丈人曰：“四体不勤，五谷不分，孰为夫子？”植其杖而芸，子路拱而立。止子路宿，杀鸡为黍而食之，见其二子焉。明日，子路行以告，子曰：“隐者也。”使子路反见之，至则行矣。子路曰：“不仕无义。长幼之节不可废也，君臣之义如之何其废之？欲洁其身而乱大伦。君子之仕也，行其义也，道之不行已知之矣。”

en:
【Weizi 18】

When Weizi left, Jizi became a slave, and Bigan remonstrated and died. Confucius said, "In the Yin dynasty, there were three men of virtue."
Liuxia Hui served as a judge and was dismissed three times. Someone said, "Can you not leave?" He replied, "If I serve men by the straight path, where can I go and not be dismissed three times? If I serve men by crooked ways, why should I leave the land of my parents?"
Duke Jing of Qi, in his treatment of Confucius, said, "I cannot treat him as I treat the head of the Ji family." He treated him between the Ji and Meng families, and said, "I am old; I cannot use him." Confucius then left.
The people of Qi sent female musicians, and Ji Huanzi accepted them. For three days, no court was held. Confucius then left.
The madman of Chu, Jieyu, passed by Confucius, singing, "O phoenix, phoenix, how has your virtue declined! What is past cannot be mended, but the future may yet be pursued. Give it up, give it up! Those who engage in government today are in danger." Confucius alighted and wished to speak with him, but the madman hastened away and avoided him, so that Confucius could not speak with him.
Changju and Jieni were ploughing together. Confucius passed by them and sent Zilu to ask about the ford. Changju said, "Who is that holding the reins?" Zilu said, "It is Kong Qiu." He said, "Is it Kong Qiu of Lu?" Zilu said, "It is." He said, "He knows the ford." Zilu asked Jieni. Jieni said, "Who are you?" Zilu said, "I am Zhong You." He said, "Are you a disciple of Kong Qiu of Lu?" Zilu replied, "Yes." He said, "The world is all rushing along like a flood, and who can change it? Moreover, rather than follow one who avoids men, is it not better to follow those who avoid the world?" And he went on with his ploughing without stopping. Zilu went and reported this to the Master. The Master was disappointed and said, "We cannot associate with birds and beasts. If I do not associate with these people, with whom shall I associate? If the Way prevailed in the world, I would not need to change it."
Zilu, following the Master, fell behind and met an old man carrying a staff on his shoulder. Zilu asked him, "Have you seen my Master?" The old man said, "Your four limbs are unaccustomed to toil; you cannot distinguish the five grains. Who is your Master?" Planting his staff in the ground, he weeded. Zilu stood with his hands folded. The old man kept Zilu for the night, killed a chicken, prepared millet, and fed him, and also introduced his two sons. The next day, Zilu went on his way and reported this. The Master said, "He is a recluse." He sent Zilu back to see him, but when he arrived, the old man had gone. Zilu said, "Not to take office is not righteous. The relationship between old and young cannot be neglected. How then can the relationship between ruler and minister be neglected? Wishing to keep his person pure, he subverts the great relationships. The superior man takes office to do his duty. As to the failure of the Way, he knows that beforehand."
...

At the cliff's base, scattered remnants of bamboo traps and delicate paper kites whisper of a time when children's laughter once filled the air.
But those days have faded. Now, misfortune looms over this place, and the joyful echoes of play have fallen silent.
In a world riven by endless strife and unrest, where can we find the Haven we once longed for? All that remains is a gasp and a sigh.

一个库吏将他从生意里赚来的钱，全留在了这里。

他好惊惧，今日才窥见叔父做的真生意。
竟是将所有的军资，变卖作钱财入了自个儿的府邸。
今时倒走的所有东西，来日都要换了这大营里将士的性命。
他好叹悔，为了一星半点儿的前程，把自己的半条命搭在这里。
泄了密，自己人会杀了他，仇视的人更会杀了他。
而今钥匙已失，叔父震怒，他害怕，害怕自己的死期将至。
他觉着，他还有一丝的良知，
那些所有腌臜换来的钱，他一分也不敢花。
不管是谁，求求你，拿走这些钱，别害他的命。
en:
A warehouse clerk left all the money he made from his business right here.

He is terrified; only today did he see his uncle's true business.
Every bit of military funding was sold and turned into wealth for his own mansion.
Everything sold off today will be paid for tomorrow with the lives of the soldiers in this camp.
He is filled with regret, having gambled half his life here for a sliver of a future.
If he leaks the secret, his own people will kill him; if he is caught by the enemy, they will kill him too.
Now that the key is lost, his uncle is furious. He is afraid—afraid that his end is near.
He feels he still has a spark of conscience left.
He hasn't dared to spend a single cent of that filthy money.
Whoever you are, please, take this money and leave. Just don't let it take his life.

zh:
《说文解字》有云：“驳，马色不纯。从马，爻声。”契丹铁蹄中杂而不纯者，为乌驳。
《辽史·食货志》有云：“契丹旧俗，其富以马，其强以兵。纵马於野，弛兵於民。有事而战，彍骑介夫，卯命辰集。马逐水草，人仰湩酪，挽强射生，以给日用，糗粮刍茭，道在是矣。以是制胜，所向无前。”契丹为游牧民族，素有逐水草而牧马之习俗，自辽国建立，六院之下专设马群司，掌彰愍宫马群牧养蕃息之事。契丹战马素以耐劳善忍、勇猛稳健著称，故名“契丹铁蹄”。
契丹铁蹄体格较小，肢粗而短，蹄小而圆，蹄质坚实，不易裂缝，步伐敏捷，即便于崎岖山路亦如履平地。性沉稳，耐粗饲，易增膘，寿命长，可负重乘骑，为契丹辽国最常见的马种。
en:
The Shuowen Jiezi explains: "The character bo means a horse of impure color." Among the famed Khitan Iron Hooves, those with such a mixed, dark coat were known as Wubo.
According to the History of Liao: "In old Khitan custom, wealth lay in horses and strength in arms." As nomads, the Khitan roamed with their herds, raising horses along rivers and pastures. When war came, armored cavalry would assemble at dawn at the emperor's command. Their horses, raised on wild pastures and sustained by nature, were famed for endurance, strength, and composure, earning them the name "Khitan Iron Hooves." With the founding of the Liao Dynasty, a dedicated Horse Herd Office was established to manage the imperial herds.
The Khitan Iron Hoof is compact, with short, sturdy limbs and small, round hooves that rarely crack. Nimble and sure-footed, it navigates rugged mountain terrain as if it were level ground. Calm in nature, tolerant of rough feed, and long-lived, this versatile horse could carry both rider and load, making it the most common and essential steed of the Liao Dynasty.

旁观者无不艳羡，争相竞买，更有人高呼：“万金求一碗，可乎？”
神秘男子留下一言：“我名老金，无需万金；明日出摊，到时便知！”
我报将于明日，全程追踪“老金出摊”盛况，敬请期待，不见不散！

Rumor has it that General Murong Yuan once devoted himself to crafting "ice devices," aiming to use the ingenuity of Mohist mechanics to relieve the heat for thousands of troops.
Today, we specifically visited Jinming Pool for these "ice devices," only to stumble upon a naval drill. Under the blazing sun, waves of heat rolled in, and three people fainted one after another!
Chaos ensued—could it be that our army’s strength is on par with that of the Giant Goose?
Suddenly, the Mysterious Man appeared, bringing several bowls of ice treats and feeding them to the fallen. The three immediately sprang back to life, full of vigor, and even ran three laps around the pool, their stamina surpassing their previous state!
Onlookers watched enviously, clamoring to buy, with some even shouting, "Ten thousand gold for a bowl, would that suffice?"
The Mysterious Man left with a single remark: "My name is Old Jin, no need for ten thousand gold; I’ll set up shop tomorrow—you’ll see then!"
Our publication will cover the grand event of "Old Jin’s Stall Opening" live tomorrow. Stay tuned, and don’t miss it!
Now that's a rare sight...

en:
Celestial Spring Station was first established during Emperor Wu of Han's western campaigns and destroyed in the years when war raged across the Western Realms.
The final station master upheld his duty for a lifetime, never abandoning his mission even as all contact faded into silence.
Fortune smiled when he crossed the boundless sands and reached his homeland's border. Yet fate frowned when he was captured and exiled—becoming a bound barbarian, enduring injustice.
All the hardship, all the wandering—transformed now into a well of sorrow, a crown of thorns piercing his very soul.
He returns once more to the endless desert, searching for traces of his fallen comrades.
But what greets him is only the biting wind, the steadfast poplars, and the silent fortress standing guard in solitude.
The courier became an ark of tree, drifting through the cold, desolate, eternal night.
Forever lost in the sea of sand, the vessel seeks the distant flutter of long-lost banners.

Then, the elder's gaze fell upon the map in the General's hands. The candlelight seemed to wash away their titles, leaving only two men bound by a single purpose.
By the time Elder He awakened, the General's company had already departed, leaving only the map behind.
The General has his wall to guard, and Horsehelm Village has its own. Neither has ever abandoned their post.

zh:
醉仙月的客房永远热热闹闹。小二为往来客人斟上离人泪，听五湖四海的侠客操着不同的口音讲着各地的见闻。但当他们饮尽杯中酒时，所有的语言都变成满足的喟叹。你突然想到，上次刀哥来不羡仙后，还没有坐在这里，喝上一壶你亲自斟满的酒。
有那样一把好刀的人，唯有世间的好酒才可相配。若是要去见刀哥，你定要准备一壶……
#Y满江红。河西狂澜的满江红，会不会就是刀哥喝下的第一口酒。那样烈的酒，浸透了刀哥的骨头，才让他的刀都带着酒气吧。#E
你提着酒壶来到刀哥坟前，替他去了碑上的落叶。你记得在瓷窑初见时他的嘲讽，也记得在破庙中他的坦诚。你们说好一起要去江湖，去看看外面的世界。可他却像闯入你生活里的一场风暴，轰轰烈烈为你揭开了江湖的一角，然后便消散世间。是的，消散，如日光下的雪，似流水中的盐，无从搜寻。唯有一身怅然，尽付壶中酒。
en:
The Drunken Immortal Month is always bustling with life. The waiter pours Parting Tears for wanderers from all corners of the world, who are trading stories of their travels in varying accents. When they drain their cups, all words soften into contented sighs. You think of Blade's last visit and the cup you never poured for him.
A man with such a fine blade deserves only the finest wine in the world. If you are going to see Blade, you must prepare a pot of...
#YRiver All Red. Could the River All Red of Raging Tides in Hexi be the very first wine Blade ever drank? Only a wine that fierce, soaking into his very bones, could make even his blade carry the scent of alcohol.#E
You bring a wine pot to Blade's grave and brush the fallen leaves from his tombstone. You remember his sneer when you first met at the porcelain kiln, and his blunt honesty in the ruined temple. You had agreed to venture into the jianghu together, to see the world outside. Yet he burst into your life like a fierce storm, dramatically tearing back a corner of the jianghu for you, only to vanish from this earth. Yes, he vanished, like snow under sunlight or salt in flowing water, nowhere to be found, leaving you with nothing but a deep sorrow, all poured into the wine in your pot.

zh:
*一段荒腔走板的歌声* 
嘿，老头儿！对对，就你。你知道去长安往哪儿走吗？我不是臭屁小孩，我叫安琉璃。我去长安找我爹。我爹……是个诗人！我娘是这么说的。你知道“长安大道横九天，青牛白马七香车”吗？那就是我爹写的！……你笑什么，臭老头。我看着写的挺好的。……哦，我不是寻亲。我娘不在乎什么名分啊家室那些个东西，说那是破烂儿。我也这么觉得！我是去找他学法术。对对，他会变戏法，有神通的！他在长安开了个胡饼铺子，安氏胡饼，你听说过吗？老字号了！ 
你这老头怎么问这么多，你……该不会是人贩子吧？啊？你也会神通？就你这样，骗谁呢，我可不是普通的小孩。好吧好吧，那我们拉钩，我说完身世，你就得给我看看你的神通。我是从把戏团跑出来的。嗨，没事儿，把戏团嘛，破烂地方，我妈也经常跑。但是没地儿去嘛，跑几天还是得回来。我今年都七岁了，也能跑了！ 
你……你真会神通啊……天呐……师父在上，受徒儿一拜！ 
师父你姓什么？廉？廉师父！师父我帮你牵骆驼！我来拿行李……唔，那我帮你背琵琶吧！师父你还会弹琵琶呀，那你会唱歌吗？……陇头流水……流回长安的歌？哦，我不去长安了，我有师父教我！师父师父，你的法术都是从哪儿学的呀？……神通册子？有这样的册子吗？……那我不说话了。我话不多的。唔唔。 
*一段荒腔走板的歌声* 
哟吼！哈哈佬！我回来了。哦，我去找我师父了。三娘的病一直不好，总不能不管她。我师父说她是……相思病。真是怪病……也不知道该怎么治。 
都说了我师父不是骗子。我看你才像个骗子。今天我师父又教我认字了，教的是我的神通名字，说叫游戏神通。嗯……“戏名自在，如师子在鹿中自在无畏，故名为戏”……你笑屁！我认字又不多，能记住这句已经够了不起了！算了，跟你这种俗人说不到一起去。走走走，别烦我。 
……三娘？三娘也是。为了那什么婚宴啊，名分啊，家室啊要死要活的。没意思的紧。要我说，都没我的游戏神通有意思！
en:
A tuneless song  
Hey, old man! Yeah, you. Do you know which way to go to Chang'an? I'm not some brat, my name is An Liuli. I'm going to Chang'an to find my dad. My dad… is a poet! That's what my mom says. Do you know "Chang'an's great avenues span the nine heavens, green oxen, white horses, and seven-scented carriages"? That was written by my dad! … What are you laughing at, you smelly old man? I think it's pretty well written. … Oh, I'm not looking for family recognition. My mom doesn't care about things like status or family ties, she says those are rubbish. I think so too! I'm going to learn magic from him. Yeah, he can perform tricks, he has divine powers! He runs a foreign pancake shop in Chang'an, An's Pancakes. Have you heard of it? An old established brand!  
Why are you asking so many questions, old man?… You aren't a kidnapper, are you? Huh? You have divine powers too? Someone like you, who are you trying to fool? I'm no ordinary kid. Alright, fine, let's pinky swear. After I tell you my background, you have to show me your powers. I ran away from a troupe. Eh, it's nothing, just a troupe, a dumpy place. My mom runs away often too. But there's nowhere else to go, so after a few days she always comes back. I'm seven years old now, I can run away too!  
You... You really have divine powers... Oh my god... Master, please accept your disciple's bow!  
Master, what's your surname? Lian? Master Lian! Master, I'll lead your camel for you! I'll carry your luggage… Hmm, then let me carry your pipa! Master, you can play the pipa too? Then can you sing? … The flowing water at Longtou… a song that flows back to Chang'an? Oh, I'm not going to Chang'an anymore. I have a master to teach me! Master, master, where did you learn all your magic? … A book of divine powers? There's such a book? … Then I won't talk. I don't talk much. Mmm, mmm.  
A tuneless song  
Yo-ho! Haha guy! I'm back. Oh, I went to find my master. Sanniang's illness hasn't gotten better. I can't just ignore her. My master said she has... lovesickness. What a strange illness... I don't know how to cure it.  
I told you, my master isn't a fraud. You're the one who looks like a fraud. Today my master taught me to read again, taught me the name of my divine power, called Divine Power of Play. Hmm… "The play is named 'Leisure', like a lion among deer, fearless and at ease, thus called 'play'…" What are you laughing at, you jerk? I don't know many characters, being able to remember this line is impressive enough! Forget it, no point talking to a vulgar person like you. Go away, go away, don't bother me.  
… Sanniang? Sanniang is the same. Fussing over weddings, status, family ties… so pointless. If you ask me, none of it is as interesting as my Divine Power of Play!
Yao Feng Xiaosheng
Xi Yan Hui

他说等我们成年后，他就来向我求亲，真是个傻子。

那信他看懂没，我要是同意，#Y子时#E屋子里的灯就亮起来……他应该明白吧。

他成日关心我家的灯做什么，难不成之后还会不亮了？
真是傻子，哼——

他这几日呆头呆脑的，准备求亲就求亲，还以为瞒得过我。

en:
He said that once we're grown, he'd propose—what a silly guy.
Who would want to spend their life with someone that clueless? But—
I told him if he's serious about it, I might actually consider it.
And that idiot even asked me how I'd say yes. Like, how is a girl supposed to make that clear? So ridiculous.
I said in the letter, if I agreed, the lights in the house would come on at the #YHour of Zi#E... He should've caught on.

Why is he always so fixated on whether the lights at my place are on or off? Does he think they won't turn on one day?
What a fool. Hmph.

Lately, he's been acting all clueless, thinking he can keep his proposal a secret from me. No chance.
I've got to buy some lamp oil... but I'll have to sneak out at night to get it.
Otherwise, it'll just look like I'm the desperate one.

冀州：既载壶口，治梁及岐。既修太原， 至于岳阳；覃怀厎绩，至于衡漳。厥土惟白壤， 厥赋惟上上错，厥田惟中中。恒、卫既従，大 陆既作。岛夷皮服，夹右碣石入于河。济河惟
济河惟兖州。九河既道，雷夏既泽，澭、 沮会同。桑土既蚕，是降丘宅土。厥土黑坟， 厥草惟繇，厥木惟条。厥田惟中下，厥赋贞， 作十有三载乃同。厥贡漆丝，厥篚织文。浮于 济、漯，达于河。
海岱惟青州。嵎夷既略，潍、淄其道。厥 土白坟，海滨广斥。厥田惟上下，厥赋中上。 厥贡盐絺，海物惟错。岱畎丝、枲、铅、松、 怪石。菜夷作牧。厥篚檿丝。浮于汶，达于济。
海、岱及淮惟徐州。淮、沂其乂，蒙、羽 其艺，大野既猪，东原厎平。厥土赤埴坟，草木渐包。厥田惟上中，厥赋中中。厥贡惟土五 色，羽畎夏翟，峄阳孤桐，泗滨浮磬，淮夷蠙 珠暨鱼。厥篚玄纤、缟。浮于淮、泗，达于河。
淮海惟扬州。彭蠡既猪，阳鸟攸居。三江既 入，震泽厎定。筱簜既敷，厥草惟夭，厥木惟乔。 厥土惟涂泥。厥田唯下下，厥赋下上，上错。厥 贡惟金三品，瑶、琨筱、簜、齿、革、羽、毛惟 木。岛夷卉服。厥篚织贝，厥包桔柚，锡贡。沿 于江、海，达于淮、泗。
荆及衡阳惟荆州。江、汉朝宗于海，九江孔 殷，沱、潜既道，云土、梦作乂。厥土惟涂泥， 厥田惟下中，厥赋上下。厥贡羽、毛、齿、革惟 金三品，杶、干、栝、柏，砺、砥、砮、丹惟菌 簵、楛，三邦底贡厥名。包匦菁茅，厥篚玄纁玑 组，九江纳锡大龟。浮于江、沱、潜、汉，逾于 洛，至于南河。
荆河惟豫州。伊、洛、瀍、涧既入于河，荥 波既猪。导菏泽，被孟猪。厥土惟壤，下土坟垆。 厥田惟中上，厥赋错上中。厥贡漆、枲，絺、纻， 厥篚纤、纩，锡贡磬错。浮于洛，达于河。
华阳、黑水惟梁州。岷、嶓既艺，沱、潜既 道。蔡、蒙旅平，和夷厎绩。厥土青黎，厥田惟 下上，厥赋下中，三错。厥贡璆、铁、银、镂、 砮磬、熊、罴、狐、狸、织皮，西倾因桓是来， 浮于潜，逾于沔，入于渭，乱于河。
黑水、西河惟雍州。弱水既西，泾属渭汭， 漆沮既従，沣水攸同。荆、岐既旅，终南、惇物， 至于鸟鼠。原隰厎绩，至于猪野。三危既宅，三 苗丕叙。厥土惟黄壤，厥田惟上上，厥赋中下。 厥贡惟球、琳、琅玕。浮于积石，至于龙门、西 河，会于渭汭。织皮昆仑、析支、渠搜，西戎即 叙。
导岍及岐，至于荆山，逾于河；壶口、雷首 至于太岳；厎柱、析城至于王屋；太行、恒山至 于碣石，入于海。
西倾、朱圉、鸟鼠至于太华；熊耳、外方、 桐柏至于陪尾。
导嶓冢，至于荆山；内方，至于大别。
岷山之阳，至于衡山，过九江，至于敷浅原。
导弱水，至于合黎，馀波入于流沙。
导黑水，至于三危，入于南海。
导河、积石，至于龙门；南至于华阴，东至 于厎柱，又东至于孟津，东过洛汭，至于大伾； 北过降水，至于大陆；又北，播为九河，同为逆 河，入于海。
嶓冢导漾，东流为汉，又东，为沧浪之水， 过三澨，至于大别，南入于江。东，汇泽为彭蠡， 东，为北江，入于海。
岷山导江，东别为沱，又东至于澧；过九江， 至于东陵，东迆北，会于汇；东为不江，入于海。
导沇水，东流为济，入于河，溢为荥；东出 于陶丘北，又东至于菏，又东北，会于汶，又北， 东入于海。
导淮自桐柏，东会于泗、沂，东入于海。
导渭自鸟鼠同穴，东会于沣，又东会于泾， 又东过漆沮，入于河。
导洛自熊耳，东北，会于涧、瀍；又东，会于伊，又东北，入于河。
九州攸同，四隩既宅，九山刊旅，九川涤源， 九泽既陂，四海会同。六府孔修，庶土交正，厎慎财赋，咸则三壤成赋。中邦锡土、姓，祗台德先，不距朕行。
五百里甸服：百里赋纳总，二百里纳铚，三 百里纳秸服，四百里粟，五百里米。
五百里侯服：百里采，二百里男邦，三百里诸侯。
五百里绥服：三百里揆文教，二百里奋武卫。
五百里要服：三百里夷，二百里蔡。
五百里荒服：三百里蛮，二百里流。
东渐于海，西被于流沙，朔南暨声教讫于四海。禹锡玄圭，告厥成功。
en:
【Book of Xia · Tribute of Yu】

Yu divided the nine provinces, followed the mountains to dredge the rivers, and assessed the land to levy tributes. Yu spread the soil, followed the mountains to cut down trees, and established the high mountains and great rivers.
Jizhou: After completing the work at Hukou, he managed Liang and Qi. After restoring Taiyuan, he reached the southern foot of Mount Yue; Tanhuai achieved success, reaching the Heng and Zhang rivers. The soil there was white and fertile, the tribute was of the highest grade with some variation, and the fields were of the middle-middle grade. The Heng and Wei rivers were brought under control, and the Dalu lowlands were cultivated. The island barbarians brought skins and furs as tribute, and they entered the Yellow River via the right side of Jieshi Mountain. The Ji and Yellow Rivers were...
The Ji and Yellow Rivers defined Yanzhou. The nine rivers were channeled, Leixia became a marsh, and the Yong and Ju rivers converged. The mulberry lands were suitable for sericulture, so the people descended from the hills to dwell on the plains. The soil there was black and fertile, the grass was lush, and the trees were tall. The fields were of the middle-lower grade, and the tribute was fixed, taking thirteen years to match the standard. The tribute consisted of lacquer and silk, and the baskets contained patterned fabrics. They traveled by water via the Ji and Luo rivers to reach the Yellow River.
The sea and Mount Dai defined Qingzhou. The Yuyi region was settled, and the Wei and Zi rivers were channeled. The soil there was white and fertile, with vast salty marshes along the coast. The fields were of the upper-lower grade, and the tribute was of the middle-upper grade. The tribute consisted of salt, fine hemp cloth, and various sea products. The Dai valley produced silk, hemp, lead, pine, and strange stones. The Laiyi people practiced animal husbandry. The baskets contained wild silk. They traveled by water via the Wen River to reach the Ji River.
The sea, Mount Dai, and the Huai River defined Xuzhou. The Huai and Yi rivers were harnessed, and the Meng and Yu mountains were cultivated. Daye was made into a marsh, and Dongyuan was leveled. The soil there was red, clayey, and fertile, and the vegetation gradually flourished. The fields were of the upper-middle grade, and the tribute was of the middle-middle grade. The tribute consisted of the five-colored soils, the pheasants from the Yu valley, the solitary tung trees from the southern side of Yi Mountain, the floating stones from the Si River shore, and the pearls and fish from the Huaiyi people. The baskets contained dark and white silks. They traveled by water via the Huai and Si rivers to reach the Yellow River.
The Huai and the sea defined Yangzhou. Pengli was made into a marsh, and the wild geese found their abode there. The three rivers entered the sea, and Zhenze was stabilized. Bamboo shoots and bamboo spread widely, the grass was luxuriant, and the trees were tall. The soil there was muddy. The fields were of the lowest grade, and the tribute was of the lower-upper grade with some variation. The tribute consisted of the three grades of metals, jade, stones, bamboo, ivory, hides, feathers, and fur, as well as timber. The island barbarians wore grass clothing. The baskets contained woven shells, and they presented wrapped oranges and pomelos as special tributes. They traveled along the Yangtze and the sea to reach the Huai and Si rivers.
Jing and the southern side of Mount Heng defined Jingzhou. The Yangtze and Han rivers flowed toward the sea, the nine rivers were properly channeled, and the Tuo and Qian rivers were managed. The Yun and Meng lowlands were cultivated. The soil there was muddy, the fields were of the lower-middle grade, and the tribute was of the upper-lower grade. The tribute consisted of feathers, fur, ivory, hides, and the three grades of metals, along with the trees of Chu, Gan, Gua, and Bai, as well as whetstones, grindstones, arrowheads, and cinnabar, and the bamboo of Jun, Lu, and Hu. The three states offered their famous products. They presented wrapped bundles of Jingmao grass, and the baskets contained dark and light red silks with strings of pearls. The nine rivers offered large tortoises as tribute. They traveled by water via the Yangtze, Tuo, Qian, and Han rivers, then crossed overland to the Luo River, and finally reached the southern Yellow River.
The Jing and Yellow Rivers defined Yuzhou. The Yi, Luo, Chan, and Jian rivers all flowed into the Yellow River, and Xingbo was made into a marsh. The Heze marsh was channeled and connected to Mengzhu. The soil there was fertile, with clayey soil in the lower layers. The fields were of the middle-upper grade, and the tribute was of the upper-middle grade with some variation. The tribute consisted of lacquer, hemp, fine hemp cloth, and ramie cloth. The baskets contained fine silk and floss, and they presented chime stones as special tribute. They traveled by water via the Luo River to reach the Yellow River.
The southern side of Mount Hua and the Black Water defined Liangzhou. The Min and Bo mountains were cultivated, and the Tuo and Qian rivers were channeled. The Cai and Meng mountains were pacified, and the Heyi people achieved success. The soil there was greenish and fertile, the fields were of the lower-upper grade, and the tribute was of the lower-middle grade with three variations. The tribute consisted of jade, iron, silver, engraved metals, arrowhead stones, chime stones, bears, brown bears, foxes, wildcats, and woven furs. The Xiqing people came via the Huan River. They traveled by water via the Qian River, crossed overland to the Mian River, entered the Wei River, and then crossed the Yellow River.
The Black Water and the Western Yellow River defined Yongzhou. The Weak Water flowed westward, the Jing River joined the Wei River, the Qi and Ju rivers were brought under control, and the Feng River converged. The Jing and Qi mountains were pacified, from Zhongnan and Dunwu to the Niaoshu Mountains. The plains and lowlands achieved success, reaching Zhuye. Sanwei was settled, and the Sanmiao people were properly ordered. The soil there was yellow and fertile, the fields were of the highest grade, and the tribute was of the middle-lower grade. The tribute consisted of jade, stones, and gems. They traveled by water from Jishi to Longmen and the Western Yellow River, converging at the confluence of the Wei River. The woven furs came from Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou, and the Western Rong people were brought into order.
He channeled the Qian and Qi mountains to Mount Jing, crossing the Yellow River; from Hukou and Leishou to Taiyue; from Dizhu and Xicheng to Wangwu; and from Taihang and Hengshan to Jieshi, entering the sea.
From Xiqing, Zhuyu, and Niaoshu to Taihua; from Xiong'er, Waifang, and Tongbai to Peiwei.
He channeled the Bozhong Mountain to Mount Jing; and from Neifang to Dabie.
From the southern side of Mount Min to Mount Heng, passing through the nine rivers to Fuqianyuan.
He channeled the Weak Water to Heli, with its remaining waters flowing into the shifting sands.
He channeled the Black Water to Sanwei, flowing into the Southern Sea.
He channeled the Yellow River from Jishi to Longmen; southward to Huayin, eastward to Dizhu, further east to Mengjin, then east past the confluence of the Luo River to Dapi; northward past Jiangshui to Dalu; further north, it divided into nine rivers, which converged into the Ni River and entered the sea.
From Bozhong he channeled the Yang River, which flowed eastward as the Han River, and further east became the waters of Canglang. It passed through Sanshi to Dabie, then flowed southward into the Yangtze. Eastward, it converged into the Pengli marsh, and further east became the Northern River, entering the sea.
From Mount Min he channeled the Yangtze, which branched eastward as the Tuo River, and further east reached the Li River. It passed through the nine rivers to Dongling, then flowed eastward and northward, converging at the Hui. Eastward it became the Bei River, entering the sea.
He channeled the Yan River, which flowed eastward as the Ji River, entered the Yellow River, and overflowed as the Xing marsh. It emerged eastward from the north of Taoqiu, further east reached the He River, then flowed northeastward to converge with the Wen River, and further north, flowed eastward into the sea.
He channeled the Huai River from Tongbai, flowing eastward to converge with the Si and Yi rivers, and then eastward into the sea.
He channeled the Wei River from the Niaoshu Mountains, flowing eastward to converge with the Feng River, further east to converge with the Jing River, and further east past the Qi and Ju rivers, entering the Yellow River.
He channeled the Luo River from Xiong'er, flowing northeastward to converge with the Jian and Chan rivers; further east, it converged with the Yi River, and further northeast, entered the Yellow River.
The nine provinces were unified, the four corners were settled, the nine mountains were cleared and opened, the nine rivers were dredged at their sources, the nine marshes were diked, and all within the four seas were brought together. The six treasuries were properly managed, all lands were correctly assessed, and tributes were carefully levied, all based on the three grades of soil. The central states were granted lands and surnames, with virtue as the foremost principle, and none dared to defy his decrees.
Five hundred li formed the Dianfu (royal domain): within a hundred li, the tribute was paid in grain stalks; within two hundred li, in harvested grain; within three hundred li, in straw; within four hundred li, in husked grain; and within five hundred li, in polished grain.
Five hundred li formed the Houfu (noble domain): within a hundred li, officials were appointed; within two hundred li, petty states were established; and within three hundred li, feudal lords held sway.
Five hundred li formed the Suifu (pacification domain): within three hundred li, cultural education was promoted; and within two hundred li, martial defense was strengthened.
Five hundred li formed the Yaofu (alliance domain): within three hundred li, the Yi people lived; and within two hundred li, the Cai people lived.
Five hundred li formed the Huangfu (wilderness domain): within three hundred li, the Man people lived; and within two hundred li, the Liu people lived.
Eastward it reached the sea, westward it extended to the shifting sands, and his influence and teachings spread to the four seas. Yu was granted the dark jade scepter, proclaiming the completion of his great work.

en: "Zang" refers to the Heart's capacity to store the spirit. When the heart is still, the spirit remains at rest. But if injured by the seven emotions, the heart grows restless, and the spirit becomes agitated and unsettled. Hence, weeping from joy or sorrow reveals that the spirit can no longer govern emotion. Appearing possessed, as if by spiritual influence, means the heart has lost its clarity. This is what we now call madness and disorientation.

zh:
世上有没有眼睛的人，有没有良心的人，你说心和眼睛哪个更重要，很多人都说，心最重要。
但没有良心的人却活得这么好，而没有眼睛的人却不行。
这不公平。
话本子里不是这样写的，话本子里写的是大侠惩奸除恶，写的是皇帝爱民如子，写的是坏人都会受到惩罚，写的是好人都会团圆。
所以阿然不明白。

阿然不明白，为什么孙叔叔会搬走，不明白为什么会有一家又一家的招牌被砸下，不明白为什么刘奶奶的脸上都是眼泪，不明白为什么外边这么吵闹，任小平抱着娘哭得比以往任何一天更加大声，不明白为什么爹去买了荷花酥，走了这么久都不再回来。
她不喜欢这个结局，没有人喜欢这个结局，一个没有人喜欢的结局，为什么要存在？

她不明白，为什么她说这些道理的时候，原本别人总笑，她气呼呼地去问，他们又总说：阿然说得没错，现在他们总是不说话。
难道没错的东西，会被笑话吗？或者只能不回答吗？
她不明白，为什么她说金叶子侠客故事的时候，原本别人是笑的，自从爹爹不见之后，却总有人听她说这个故事，却不说话了。
难道她爹爹走了，他们就不爱听这个故事了吗？

这些是话本子里没有写过的东西。
不应该是这样的，孙叔叔不应该搬走，店里应该永远有热气腾腾的饭菜，后厨温暖的火焰应该时时燃起，刘奶奶的脸上不应该湿漉漉的，任小平虽然很不懂事，却也不应该难过到哭得这样大声，家门前的河水应该永远流动，而爹爹应该永远不离开她。
en:
In this world, there are those without eyes, and those without conscience. Tell me, which matters more, the heart or the eyes? Most would say the heart.
 But those without conscience thrive, while those without eyes suffer.
 This isn't fair.
 Storybooks don't write it this way. They tell of heroes punishing villains, emperors loving their people, bad men getting their due, good souls reuniting.
 So Ran couldn't understand.

 She couldn't understand why Uncle Sun moved away, why shop signs were smashed one after another, why Grannie Liu's face was wet with tears, why the streets roared with chaos, why Ren Xiaoping sobbed into his mother's arms louder than ever, why her father had gone to buy lotus pastries and never returned...
 She doesn't like this ending. Nobody likes this ending. Why should an ending nobody likes exist?

 She couldn't understand why when she says these truths, people who used to laugh now stay silent. When she angrily asks, they always say: "Ran isn't wrong." But now they just stayed silent.
 Can right things be mocked? Or must they go unanswered?
 She couldn't understand why people once laughed at her Gold Leaf Swordsman stories, but after her father vanished, they'd listen in silence.
 Did her father's disappearance make them stop loving this story?

 These are things the storybooks never wrote about.
 This wasn't how it should be. Uncle Sun shouldn't have left. The shop should always teem with hot meals. The kitchen fire should never die. Grannie Liu's cheeks shouldn't glisten with tears. Ren Xiaoping, for all his mischief, shouldn't wail like his heart was breaking. The river by her door should flow forever, and her father should have never walked away.
What's wrong?

zh:
游侠亲启： 
冬寒，敬惟 
江湖好景容易过，不知觉间，燕云已陪伴诸位游侠走到寒冬将尽。承蒙诸君支持，比春天更早到来的，是燕云已迎来#8c58231500万游侠#E的消息。 
自公测开启以来，我们一直密切关注着各位游侠的反馈，希望能够完善江湖的每一个角落，为多端的游侠们提供更好的体验。能够取得今日的成绩，皆仰仗各位游侠的支持和包容。十六巷全员感念于此，特为游侠奉上#4d734d谢礼一份#E，以表心意。 
诸位的支持是对我们最好的鞭策，我们将永远铭记，是诸位游侠与《燕云十六声》共同构筑了今日的江湖。前路漫漫，燕云将不忘初心，永远站在各位游侠身边，让江湖的故事长久传颂。 
新春将至，祝愿各位游侠新岁吉祥，万事胜意。浩瀚江湖，山河锦绣，愿并辔共赏，岁岁同看。
en:
To the Esteemed Youxia-er: 
In the chill of winter, we greet you. 
The splendid vistas of Jianghu pass swiftly, and before we knew it, Yanyun has journeyed with you through the depths of winter. Thanks to your unwavering support, even before spring arrives, we celebrate the milestone of #8c58231500 million Youxia-er#E joining our ranks. 
Since the Open Beta began, we have diligently heeded your feedback, striving to refine every corner of Jianghu and enhance the experience for all adventurers across platforms. Today's achievements are a testament to your support and patience. In gratitude, the Sixteen Lanes present you with a #4d734dToken of Appreciation#E. 
Your encouragement inspires us to greater heights. We will forever cherish how you and "Yanyun Sixteen Lanes" have shaped today's Jianghu. The road ahead is long, but Yanyun remains steadfast by your side, committed to preserving the legends of Jianghu for generations. 
As the New Year approaches, we wish you prosperity and joy. May we ride side by side through the boundless beauty of Jianghu, sharing its wonders year after year.

【梅花】

王维
屋上春鸠鸣，村边杏花白。
持斧伐远扬，荷锄觇泉脉。

en:
【Hundred Flowers - I】


【Plum Blossom】


Three Miscellaneous Poems - The Second

Wang Wei

You, coming from my old hometown,

Should know all that has happened there.

The day you go, before the silken window,

Has the winter-plum blossomed yet?


Early Plum Blossoms

Liu Zongyuan

Early plum blossoms bloom on tall trees,

Reflecting the blue sky of Chu.

The north wind blows their fragrance at night,

Heavy frost nourishes their dawn-white hue.

I wish to send them ten thousand miles away,

But vast mountains and rivers stand in the way.

These cold blossoms will wither and fall,

What can console the distant traveler at all?


【Peach Blossom】


Peach Blossoms in the Great Forest Temple

Bai Juyi

In the mortal world, all flowers fade in April's day,

In the mountain temple, peach blossoms just come into play.

I often regret spring's departure leaves no trace to find,

Not knowing it has turned and come to this place in kind.


Inscribed on the Southern Village Wall of the Capital

Cui Hu

On this day last year, within this very door,

A face and peach blossoms mirrored each other's red glow.

The face is nowhere to be found anymore,

Only the peach blossoms still smile in the spring breeze's flow.


【Apricot Blossom】


Springtime in the Countryside

Wang Wei

On the roof, spring turtledoves coo,

By the village, apricot blossoms are white.

Axe in hand, I cut the long branches,

Hoe on shoulder, I check the spring's source in sight.

Returning swallows know their old nest,

Old folks look at the new calendar's test.

Facing the wine, I suddenly cannot drink,

Melancholy for the traveler on the brink.


Revisiting the Apricot Garden

Bai Juyi

Suddenly recalling those fragrant times of frequent drunken delight,

I seek again the place of intoxication, pacing back and forth in plight.

Apricot blossoms bear fruit after the deep spring has passed,

Who understands this sentimental soul, coming alone at last?


【Pear Blossom】


Pear Blossoms

Qian Qi

Gorgeous and serene as if caged by the moon,

Their cold fragrance does not chase the wind's tune.

Peach blossoms merely shine upon the ground,

In the end, laughed at for their bewitching red, unsound.


Pear Blossoms by the Left Palace Gate

Qiu Wei

Their cold beauty wholly surpasses snow,

Their lingering scent suddenly enters the clothes' flow.

Oh spring breeze, do not settle down,

Blow them towards the jade steps, let them be known.
Compose yourself. Is this how you were taught?

en:
Once a shining city on the water's skin— 
Now a stinking swamp, a graveyard steeped in sin! 
All because— 
Some devil-brained rogue struck at the sky, 
A scorpion-hearted woman let her mercy die, 
A wretch with bones that rot within, 
And crowds of fiends with knives that grin— 
Till walls gave way 
And fire had its day, and Death rode in, hungry for his prey. 
Now only this dead lake heaves each night, 
Wailing to shake the earth with spite. 

Facing Qinchuan, back to the bay— 
There rides the villain, wild in his sway. 
One boot kicks heaven's gates apart, blood on his hands, fear in his heart. 
Arrows from the court fly fast, 
The underworld sharpens its blades at last. 
Water locked down, roads shut tight, gates barred in fright— 
All waiting for the traitor to come, 
To answer for what he's done, 

So justice can rise and drums may drum, 
And feasts return with pipe and strum. 
A pale face, a cold-blooded mind, 
A girl who whirls like a sprite unkind. 
Quiet eyes that trade in lies, soft hands spinning silken ties. 
Poison stakes in peach trees stand, a laughing chill through every man. 
Hatred roars, then snuffs her flame— 
Through ghostly gates she goes, no name. 

Great waves crash hard upon the shore—Where lie the heroes from before? 
Some strode proud through palace light. Some bent low, boots kissed outright. 
In the end, all fall the same—two stiff legs, a mound, no fame. 
Let heaven shake, let earth upend— 
A kindness paid, a grudge to end; blood for debt and head for friend. 
Sun sinks low, the city's gone. 
The golden peach—where will it dawn? 
Still swinging in the windy air, half a dream in mist out there.

zh:
“东阙到了。”
女人说完话转身离去时，衣袖带起的风使得桌上烛火剧烈摇晃起来，南烛公子忙用衣袖护住那烛火。耳边脚步声响起，接着，一只布满茧的手从另一边帮他一起护住了那支烛。
“江南一别，许久不见。”那手的主人开了口。
他抬起头，看到的并不是金衣桀骜的公子，而是一位布衣的姑娘，眉目虽是一如往前，气质却已经截然不同。
”你的变化实在太大。”南烛公子忍不住道。
东阙笑了笑，坐到南烛的对面：“啊呀，也没那么大吧。”
那一夜，东阙从唐钱收缴策谈起，谈到九流门、谈到河伯，谈到石守信等人，谈到常平使……南烛安静听着，手指一下下敲着桌案，犹如在打着牙板……直到那支蜡烛即将烧到尽头。
“你要的不多，我可以给你，只是……”南烛的目光停留在那最后的烛火上，“……帮我护一护烛火。”
“好。”
东阙望向北方，风低声呜咽着从手指间穿过。
“今日的风还不大。”
en:
"The Ember of East has arrived." 
As the woman finished speaking and turned to leave, the wind stirred by her sleeve violently shook the candle flame on the table. Shimmer of South hurriedly used his own sleeve to shield it. The sound of footsteps reached his ears, then a calloused hand came from the other side to help him protect the candle. 
"It's been a long time since we parted in Jiangnan," the owner of the hand spoke. 
He looked up and saw not the arrogant young master in golden robes, but a woman in plain clothes. Though her features were as before, her demeanor was completely different. 
"You've changed so much," Shimmer of South couldn't help but say. 
The Ember of East smiled, sitting down opposite Shimmer of South. "Ah, well, it's not that much, is it?" 
That night, The Ember of East spoke starting from the Tang coin confiscation policy, moving on to the Nine Mortal Ways, River Deity, Shi Shouxin and others, the Master of Grain... Shimmer of South listened quietly, his fingers tapping the table rhythmically, as if keeping time with clappers... until the candle was about to burn out. 
"What you ask is not much, I can give it to you, just..." Shimmer of South's gaze lingered on the last of the flame, "...help me protect this candlelight." 
"Okay." 
The Ember of East looked northward. The wind whimpered softly as it passed through her fingers. 
"The wind isn't too strong today."

Namo Amitabha.
To Fellow Disciples:

Our Sect Master, in recent meditation, spoke thus: "Our order bears the karma of slaughter to ascent sentient beings to the Pure Land; this itself is suffering. Yet those who willingly board this Vessel of Mercy to intercede and shoulder their Karma possess the firmest resolve and the bravest hearts."
To honor such resolve, the Sect Master decrees a change to our rules, effective immediately:
All Midnight Blades ascetics who triumph over the "Sufferer" shall not only take their place and inherit their karmic burden, #Ybut also receive a "Seven Sorrows Token," exchangeable for Jianghu reputation#E, a mark of their great courage in sharing the weight of sin.
This applies even among the Sufferers themselves. The strong grow stronger; the capable do more. So they may bear more sin for all sentient beings.
Upon the Path of Carnage, there is no fellowship among disciples. But there is a shared will to endure hellfire and cross the bitter sea of life and death together.

zh:
又到了一日的子时。
无颜趴在暗房的地上，侧耳听了一会儿。她确信这是个逃跑的好时机。客人已经散场，看守的人也都已经睡下。只要能推开面前这扇门，再沿着那暗红的灯笼一路往前，而后穿过一个幽暗的洞穴……她能出去。这条路她在心里临摹了一遍又一遍，她一定能出去。
她用那双渗血的满是污泥的手，颤颤巍巍地撑起了上半身，腰间的木头挂坠从地面擦过，带出些许声响，她顿住，屏住呼吸，双手颤得厉害，指尖全是血痂，但她不在意。而后她咬了咬牙，再次使劲，然而下一瞬，她砰然倒地。
她看向自己的双腿，无声的叹了口气。上次她逃跑时，无忧帮的人打断了她的左腿；再上一次，是她的右腿。但那已经过去了月余，她本以为自己能战胜这种痛苦。看来她还是高估了自己。
彻骨的疼痛很快席卷而来，泪水和血渍掺杂着从脸庞滴落，很快模糊了她的视线。她下意识伸手擦拭，却感到更剧烈的疼痛。她这才后知后觉的想起，是了，再上上次，她为了反抗那些人，已自毁了容颜。
她支着身子，有一瞬的迷茫。但她又很快恢复了清明。不行，得出去，一定要出去。断了腿，可以医治。毁了容颜，娘亲也不会嫌弃。只要能出去，只要能回到娘亲的身边……她撑着身体，往前挪了一步，又一步……但大门却被人一脚踢开。

暗红的烛光透了进来，尘土飞扬间，无颜终于绝望地闭上了眼……好像离开家，已经好久了，不知道娘亲在哪？娘亲在做什么？娘亲有没有挂念自己？她思绪万千间，下颚被扣住，而后有苦涩的药水，灌入了她的喉咙。她落下了一滴泪来。
看来从今往后，她就要溃烂在这暗无天日的沟渠里了……
en:
It was Zi hour again.
Faceless lay on the dark room's floor, listening intently. This was her chance. The guests had left, and the guards were asleep. If she could push open the door, follow the dim red lanterns, and crawl through that shadowy tunnel... she could escape. She'd mapped the route in her mind a hundred times, she had to make it.
With bloodied, mud-caked hands, she trembled to her elbows. The wooden pendant at her waist scraped the floor, making a faint noise. She froze, breath held, fingers crusted with scabs. Gritting her teeth, she tried again, but collapsed with a thud.
Her eyes fell to her legs, and she sighed silently. The Unbound Cavern had broken her left leg during her last escape, her right, the time before. A month had passed, and she'd thought the pain would ease. She'd overestimated herself.
The pain came swiftly, piercing to the bone. Tears and blood mingled as they streamed down her face, soon blurring her vision. She instinctively raised a hand to wipe them away, only to be met with even sharper agony. Then she remembered, yes, the time before last, in her struggle against those people, she had deliberately ruined her own face.
She propped herself up, momentarily dazed, but clarity quickly returned. No. She must escape. She had to get out. Broken legs could heal. A ruined face wouldn't make her mother love her less. If she could just get out... if she could just return to her mother's side... Gritting her teeth, she dragged herself forward. One painful crawl. Then another. However, the door burst open with a crash.

The dim red candlelight spilled into the room, swirling dust particles in the air. Faceless finally closed her eyes in despair... It felt like an eternity since she'd left home. Where was mother now? What was she doing? Did she still think of her? As these thoughts flooded her mind, a rough hand clamped around her jaw, forcing her mouth open as bitter medicine poured down her throat. A single tear escaped her eye.
This ditch of rotting shadows would be her grave after all.

货郎赵五贪近路夜过坟岗，忽见所有红绸同时绷直如弓弦，拽得坟包簌簌落土。土里伸出青黑的手，每只手腕都系着半截红绸，拼命朝月亮抓挠。
“作孽啊……”老人拽走吓瘫的赵五。他说，去年大旱，村长说山神要娶亲。村长从外面抓了几个姑娘，用红绸裹上，送入了“山神”的“怀里”。老人劝赵五离去，莫要停留。
当夜村中起火，火苗如绸缎般缠上窗棂。村民扑救时，骇见火焰里扭动着数个焦黑人形，腕上红绸鲜亮如新。
天明后，凡参与过“送亲”的村民，脖颈都凭空多了圈红痕。不出三日，西坡添了新坟——整整二十座新坟头，都缠上起了滴血般的红绸。
en:
Ten fresh graves had appeared on the western slope of the common burial ground, each mound wrapped in strips of blood-red silk. Travelers who passed by admired the sight, assuming some wealthy family had arranged a ghost marriage with fine ceremony. Only the village elders turned their eyes away and said nothing.
One night, Zhao Wu, a peddler cutting through the burial ground to save time, watched in horror as all the red silks snapped suddenly taut, jerking at the mounds until soil crumbled and fell. Dark, mottled hands clawed their way out of the earth, each wrist tied with a length of crimson silk, grasping blindly toward the moon.
"What wickedness..." An old villager seized the trembling Zhao Wu and dragged him away. Last year's drought, he said, had driven the village chief to declare that the mountain god wanted a bride. He had seized several young women from outside the village, bound them in red silk, and fed them into the mountain god's "embrace." The old man told Zhao Wu to leave and not look back.
That same night, fire broke out across the village. The flames curled around window frames like ribbons of silk. As the villagers struggled to fight the blaze, they saw dark, charred figures writhing in the fire, the red silk at their wrists still vivid and unburned.
By dawn, every villager who had played a part in the "bride offering" bore a red ring around their neck, appearing from nowhere. Within three days, twenty new mounds had been raised on the western slope, each wound tight with blood-red silk that glistened like an open wound.

zh:
沈义伦，一直是一个“内敛”的孩子。
自小便总听别人说，他与家中那勇敢强势、总能在人群中成为“老大”的哥哥完全不一样。他瘦弱，怯懦，小心翼翼，仿佛随时准备将自己融入阴影中。人人都认为他是个怪人，自然，便没有孩童会愿意与他玩耍。久而久之，连沈义伦自己也认为，或许自己本就该独身一人，生活在黑暗中。

初入学堂，面对师长关于理想的询问，沈义伦的心中没有宏伟的志向，只有质朴的愿望：“只要能吃饱饭，做什么……都好。”此言一出，换来的是满堂哄笑。他不理解，自己这简单、真实的想法，为何会成为笑柄呢？他知道，学堂的生活，或许又会与往昔一样黑暗、孤独。

——他又想把自己藏起来了……

然而，这次的命运，似乎与之前不一样。
那个叫郑鄂的少年，清风俊朗，风度翩翩，一看就是个家中富裕的少爷。非但没有随波逐流的嘲笑自己，还主动靠近自己，说自己的志向让他醍醐灌顶。自己的话，让他找到了心中的理想。
可那明明是一句让大家都讥笑的话啊……

——“约定好了，我们要让大伙儿都吃饱饭，让‘天下常平，黎民无饥’！”
这位少爷，或许天生就是日光，和自己这种影子不一样。他是他可望不可及。他也从不奢望与日光做朋友。但他却说，他们是约定要完成共同理想的挚友了。
沈义伦看向郑鄂，说实话他不知道 “天下常平”的含义，他只知道，眼前的少年眼睛亮亮的。往后，他也拥有能够一起玩笑，并肩前行的朋友了。

——“到时候，你可不能再这样，躲在我身后了。”
改变一直以来的生活方式很难。但……如果是为了他，为了他口中的理想，好像，也不是不可以……
en:
Shen Yilun had always been the "quiet" child.
From childhood, people compared him to his bold, charismatic older brother, a natural leader who commanded attention. Yilun, by contrast, was slight and timid, perpetually shrinking into the background like a shadow. Others called him odd, and eventually, even he began to believe he was meant to dwell in solitude, swallowed by darkness.

On his first day at school, when the teacher asked about ambitions, Yilun's answer was painfully simple: "As long as I can eat my fill, any work would do..." The classroom erupted in laughter. He couldn't understand why his honest wish was mocked. School, it seemed, would be as lonely as the life he'd always known.

—He thought of disappearing again...

But fate had other plans this time.
Zheng E, a boy radiating confidence and charm, clearly born to privilege, approached him. Instead of joining the ridicule, he praised Yilun's answer, calling it "a revelation." Zheng E claimed Yilun's humble words had crystallized his own purpose.
How? Yilun wondered. It was just a joke to everyone else.

—"Let's make a promise. We'll ensure no one goes hungry. Peace will reign and famine will vanish!"
To Yilun, Zheng E seemed like sunlight incarnate. Everything he could never be. Friends with someone so radiant? Unthinkable. Yet here was this golden boy, insisting they were now "sworn allies" sharing a grand vision.
Yilun didn't fully grasp phrases like "peace reigns," but he understood the fire in Zheng E's gaze. For the first time, he had someone to laugh with, to walk beside.

—"When the time comes, you can't hide behind me anymore."
Changing his lifelong habits felt impossible. Yet... for Zheng E, and the dream they'd woven together, Yilun found himself willing to try.
Does anyone know what's wrong here?

zh:
这枚名为守心的射玦，出自鸦之手，是青第一次下山时的临别赠礼。

“青妹此去不知何时回山，唯愿此志不改……此心不易。”

故而当青戴着这枚射玦下山时，踌躇满志。

以执剑之武，以墨守之技，定能护得一方安宁。

她在山外遇见了个小哑巴。小哑巴没有名字，瘦得像风里的一根枯草，可“枯草”还在风里挣扎。

小哑巴很聪明，也很懂事，她从不问青从哪来，又要去哪，还会不会回来，她只是拼命地学，拼命地学。

仅三天，小哑巴就会做一些简单的陷阱了，她高兴地比划，意思是她能抓到兔子了，不会饿死了，大姐姐可以放心地离开了。

像她这样的枯草，就算被雨水滋养，也长成不了大树的。

青不懂为什么小哑巴不肯跟自己走，可恰逢彼时山外有事要办。她离开前想了又想，还是脱下了手上的射玦，送给小哑巴。

“送我这枚射玦的人说，佩之能守心明志。我把它借你几日，你要是想法变了，愿意和我走，就等我回来那天戴着它来找我。”



然而等青回山时，鸦却没看到青信中所说的小哑巴。

青说，她回去找了，可小哑巴不见了，村民说是小哑巴跑了出去，被狼咬死了。可……可为何那枚射玦戴在别人手上?

鸦看着青通红的眼睛，没有再问。

他只是将原本的射玦一拆为二，青一半，他一半。

“愿为你分担一半。”

与子同心，与子同念，与子同担。
en:
This Archery Jade named Perseverance was made by Raven, a parting gift for Halcyon when she left for the first time.

"Dear Halcyon, I know not when you will return. I only wish that this will remains unchanged... this heart unwavering."

Thus, when Halcyon wore this jade ring down the mountain, she was full of ambition.
With the martial art of the sword, with the skill of Mohist defense, she would surely protect the peace of a region.

Outside the mountains, she met a little mute. The little mute had no name, thin as a withered blade of grass in the wind. Yet the "withered grass" still struggled in the wind.

The little mute was very clever and very sensible. She never asked Halcyon where she came from, where she was going, or if she would ever return. She just studied desperately, studied desperately.

In just three days, the little mute could already make some simple traps. She gestured happily, meaning she could catch rabbits, wouldn't starve, and the big sister could leave with peace of mind.

A withered blade of grass like her, even nourished by rain, could never grow into a big tree.

Halcyon didn't understand why the little mute wouldn't go with her. But just then, she had matters to attend to outside the mountains. Before leaving, she thought and thought, then finally took off the jade ring and gave it to the little mute.

"The one who gave me this jade ring said wearing it helps keep the heart steadfast and the will clear. I'll lend it to you for a few days. If you change your mind and are willing to go with me, wear it to find me on the day I return."

But when Halcyon returned to the mountain, Raven didn't see the little mute mentioned in Halcyon's letter.

Halcyon said she went back to look, but the little mute was gone. The villagers said the little mute ran out and was bitten to death by wolves. But... but why was that jade ring being worn by someone else?

Raven looked at Halcyon's reddened eyes and asked no more.

He simply split the original jade ring in two, half for Halcyon, half for him.

"Willing to share half your burden."

Together in heart, together in mind, together in burden.

zh:
游侠：
      眼下就要到年关，终于要熬过这个冬天了。好在今年秋天收成不错，村里又囤了足够的薪柴物资，倒是没受冻挨饿。不知道游侠你在外面可好？有没有吃饱饭，穿暖和？

      村里人最近都很开心，家家都在张罗着过年。菱娘还用粮食熬了饴糖，孩子们都喜欢得很。这一年大伙都辛苦，最后总要吃点甜。我们也为你留了一份，若是有时间， 就回来尝尝吧。
      我代和全体村民向你问声新年好，希望你新的一年里别生病，平平安安的，村里人欢迎你随时回来。
en:
Dear Wanderer,
The end of the year draws near, and at last, we are enduring the final days of winter. Fortunately, the autumn harvest was bountiful, and the village has stockpiled enough firewood and supplies to be spared from the bite of cold and hunger. How are you out there in the jianghu? Are you eating well and keeping warm?
Word has it you have headed north; we're wondering when you might return. Most of us were refugees from those very lands, so the news has us all a little worried. It is said some dwelt south of the river, gathering duck eggs amidst the reed marshes; others lived at the mountain's foot, tending to terraced fields... We all pray for your safety on this journey. When your travels bring you past our village once more, please stay a while to rest and share with us the stories of the north.
The villagers have been in high spirits lately, each household busy with preparations for the New Year.
Lingniang even made malt candy from grain, and the kids love it. It has been a hard year for everyone, and we all deserve a taste of sweetness at its end. We have saved a portion for you; if you've got time, do come back and have a taste.
On behalf of the entire village, I wish you a joyous New Year. May you remain free from illness and find peace in the coming year. Welcome home at any time.

zh: 方入山时，年幼的燕整日整日地往山上跑，只为了试出哪种材料能乘着风飞得更远。 若是晴日，倒只是费些脚力。偏她一年四季，风雨无阻，在湿滑的山路上不知摔过多少次。 青笑说小孩子磕磕碰碰，是寻常事。鸦却看得心疼，借着给她缝补衣衫的功夫，悄悄在膝弯处多垫了几层厚布。 隼则是跑到燕上山的路口拦着。燕一板一眼地与他争辩，说器物本就要经历风雨，她当然要一一试过才知道。 无功而返的隼便攒了大半年的通宝，从易墨坊换来了一块上好的铜块，学着古书锻出了一双腿甲。 青瞧见了刚送到燕窗前的腿甲，觉着这手艺太糙，拿去大刀阔斧改了形制。 鸦瞧见了送回燕窗前的腿甲，觉着它粗犷有余，精巧不足，操起刻刀，加上了几道雅致的纹路。 腿甲很好，燕很喜欢。她取下窗台上的甲胄，在腿上比了又比，然后珍重地放到匣中。 一放就是数年，直至物是人非。
en:
When she first arrived at the mountain, young Swallow spent every day running up the peaks just to test which material could fly furthest on the wind.
On sunny days, it was just a matter of legwork. But she persisted through all seasons, rain or shine, slipping on the slick mountain paths more times than she could count.
Kingfisher joked that it was normal for children to get bumped and bruised. Raven, however, watched with heartache, quietly adding extra layers of thick cloth to the knees of the clothes she mended for her.
Falcon, returning empty-handed, saved up Coins for over half a year and traded them at the Exchange Quarter for a fine block of copper, forging a pair of greaves based on ancient texts.
Falcon, returning unsuccessful, saved up Mohist Tokens for over half a year and traded them at the Ink Workshop for a fine block of copper, forging a pair of greaves based on ancient texts.
Kingfisher saw the greaves delivered to Swallow's window and thought the craftsmanship too crude, so he boldly redesigned them.
Raven saw the greaves returned to Swallow's window and thought them rugged but lacking elegance, so she took her chisel and added graceful patterns.
The greaves were good; Swallow loved them. She took the armor from the windowsill, measured it against her legs again and again, then placed it reverently in a box.
There it stayed for years, until everything changed.

zh:
游侠亲启：

游侠，游侠！本叽等了一整年，盼了一整年，终于盼来了今天。本叽可以堂堂正正地说出——“我们相逢一载了”！今日江湖，风是暖的，云是轻的，正适合庆祝这个好日子。为了今天，本叽准备了好久，江湖各处都藏了惊喜与彩头，就等游侠来寻，可千万别忘了呀。

本叽还有个心愿，想把每一缕春风，都系在你的衣襟上。这样往后你走到哪儿，哪儿就是春天啦。江湖很大，前路也很长，就让燕叽陪着游侠一起，迈向明天吧！
en:
Dear Wanderer:

I've waited for this day all year long, and it's finally here at last! Now, I can say it with pride: "We have walked this path together for a full year!" Today, the breeze is warm and the clouds are light, a perfect day to celebrate our journey. I've been preparing for so long! Surprises are hidden all across the realm, just waiting for you to find them. Don't you forget now!

I have one more wish: to tie every wisp of the spring breeze to your lapel. This way, wherever your journey leads, spring will always be by your side. The jianghu is vast and the road ahead is long; let me walk with you as we head toward tomorrow!

zh:
在她看来，黑与白是分明的，恩与仇也如此。
结一次仇，就系上一个结；受一次恩，就解开一个结。
恩与仇，解与结，以最初的千里恩义为开端，在同一条旧绳上往复更迭。恩以命报，仇拿命偿。

一个简单的计数游戏。

一，皇帝能有什么好东西。
二，一场背弃信义的酒宴，真是奸人。
三，背离旧主又逐弃旧人，负义之徒。
四，贪欲不足更立私库，早就说皇帝能有什么好东西。

五个日夜，从恩义的千里，奔赴寻仇的千里。

四，这座山从前有匪寨，现在是果园。
三，这片田从前是荒地，现在是村庄。
二，这座城从前是焦土，现在遍炊烟。
仍有一。

旧情、旧事、旧人。
凡添上一个“旧”字，仿佛就多一分赦免。
人心若是麻绳，往往叫这些“旧”字搅得混沌。
但以麻绳作人心却简单。绳子旧则旧矣，计数依然明白。
生死遂也明白。
en:
To her, black and white were distinct, as were favors and feuds.
For every feud, a knot was tied; for every favor, a knot was undone.
Favors and feuds, knots and unravelings, began with the initial bond across a thousand miles and alternated on the same old rope. Favors were repaid with life, and feuds were settled with death.

A simple counting game:

One: What good could an Emperor ever have?
Two: A feast of betrayal; truly a villain.
Three: Betraying an old master and abandoning old friends; an ungrateful wretch.
Four: Insatiable greed to establish a private treasury... As they say, what good could an Emperor ever have?

Five days and nights, from a thousand miles of gratitude to a thousand miles of revenge.

Four: This mountain used to be a bandit camp; now it is an orchard.
Three: This field used to be a wasteland; now it is a village.
Two: This city used to be scorched earth; now it is filled with the smoke of hearths.
Still, there is one.

Old feelings, old matters, old friends.
Whenever the word "old" is added, it seems to grant a touch of absolution.
If the human heart is a hemp rope, it is often tangled in chaos by these "old" words.
But using a rope to represent the heart is simple. The rope may be old, but the counting remains clear.
Thus, life and death are also clear.
Shan Jin Hu

zh:
近日为堪舆、观星，往来穿行于太行东脉。那夜于山中，竟听得一孩童之声。循声而去，却见林隙之间，星月朗照处，有一尚在襁褓之婴孩。
漂泊之人，颠沛之身，恐照顾不周。只是甫一抱起，这孩童望我便笑。星照其瞳，发出亮来。其伸手，似要抓取天上星辰，却终抓住我之发。

阿聿曾说，将来我们若有孩子，便用天上星星为其取名。我们曾争论许久，到底用何方星宿。他执意，须选个有好兆头的，我却并不信那些。
这几日真到了取名的时候，我却没了主意。
这孩子是在朝南的山头遇见的，南方有一张宿，居朱雀宫身翼相连处，其势凌云，有高飞吉意。张宿为月为鹿，张月鹿，詹月鹿……好像是个好名字。
如此，我倒是成了俗人了。
en:
Lately, in order to survey the land and observe the stars, I have been traveling through the eastern ridges of the Taihang Mountains. One night in the mountains, I heard the cry of a child. Following the sound, I came upon an infant still in swaddling, lying in a gap among the trees where moon and starlight fell bright upon the ground.
I am a wanderer myself, with no settled place to belong, hardly someone fit to raise a child. And yet the moment I lifted the baby into my arms, the little one looked at me and smiled. Starlight shone in those eyes until they seemed almost to glow. Tiny hands reached upward, as though trying to catch the stars, and in the end only caught at my hair.

Yu once said that if we were ever blessed with a child of our own, we should name the child after a star. We argued over it for a long time, over which constellation it should be. He insisted it must be one with an auspicious meaning. I never put much faith in such things.
And now that the time has truly come to choose a name, I find myself at a loss.
I found this child on a south-facing ridge. In the southern heavens there is a Mansion of the Vermilion Bird, at the place where Wing and Chariot join, its form rising as though ready to soar. It is counted an auspicious sign, one of ascent and high flight. Within that region lies the Mansion of Extended Net. In the old star names, the Extended Net is matched with the moon and with the deer. Moon is yue. Deer is lu. I thought to name the child after the stars. Zhan Yuelu... it seems a good name after all.
So in the end, I too have become a little superstitious.

zh:
仇越海和古乐曾是生死好友，同过生，共过死的那种。哪怕在八俊里面，也是最意气相投的两个。他们曾经形影不离，后来却分道扬镳。

最先转身的是仇越海。
关于他们反目的原因，有很多种猜测。什么因爱生恨、什么求而不得……仇越海听到，一定狠狠啐一口。都他娘的瞎扯！
在仇越海看来，背后的原因其实很简单，就是这段友谊因为一个女孩，有了太多别的东西。
古乐和那个女孩，有一个共同的秘密，对他却只有缄口不言的沉默。
为什么不告而别，又为什么单单对他无法坦诚。

再见到古乐，只有野草般丛生的酸涩。
是你赢了。
他仇越海不会追问，所以先离开了，昂着头。
en:
Qiu Yuehai and Gu Le were once brothers bound by life and death. Even among the Eight Talents, none shared a bond as deep as theirs. They were inseparable—until the day they weren't.

Qiu Yuehai was the first to walk away.
There were many rumors about why they fell out: love turned to hate, unrequited desires... Whenever Qiu Yuehai heard such gossip, he'd spit in disgust. "A bunch of bull!" he'd snarl.
In his eyes, the reason was simple: their friendship had become tangled with too many other things because of a girl.
Gu Le and the girl shared a secret, yet they chose to stay silent with him.
Why leave without a word? Why couldn't they be honest with him of all people?

The next time they met, all Qiu Yuehai felt was an overgrown bitterness, like weeds choking his heart.
You win.
He would not stoop to begging for answers. So he left first, head held high.

凉州有美酒，谓之葡萄；凉州有明月，取之月华。相传，有佳酿月光酒，取葡萄精魄，融月华而成。饮者或言可睹故园烟景，然终是传闻。  
玉露台畔，曾有一方葡萄园，居者一家三人。晨起剪枝，暮至压榨，指节皆染碧紫。彼等深信掌中老茧可酿甘醴，瓮中浊浆能易安乐。
可葡萄滴翠甜美，可曾尝见人世甘苦？月轮几度满亏，岂能照亮命途褶皱？家人离散，只留稚女独守荒园。有人曾见她抱月而哭泣，或陶碗盛月，饮之则泪落如珠。
en:
Liangzhou has fine wine, called grape wine, Liangzhou has a bright moon, from which moonlight can be drawn. Legend tells of a fine brew called Moonlight Wine, made from the essence of grapes fused with moonlight. Drinkers claim to glimpse the misty scenes of their homeland, though this remains but a tale.   
Beside the Jade Dew Terrace, there once was a small vineyard where a family of three lived. They pruned vines at dawn and pressed grapes at dusk, their knuckles stained deep purple. They firmly believed the calluses on their palms could brew sweet nectar, and the turbid juice in their jars could be exchanged for peace and happiness. 
But can the emerald sweetness of grapes ever taste the bitterness of human life? How many waxings and wanings of the moon could ever illuminate the wrinkles of fate? The family scattered, leaving only a young girl to guard the desolate garden alone. Some have seen her embracing the moon and weeping, or holding the moon in a clay bowl, drinking it down with tears falling like pearls.

en:
The Tigers in Chains was once the elite force under the renowned general Ye Wanshan. Steadfast in their creed to protect the people and defend the cities they were a stalwart line of defense against the Khitan and a shield to the realm. However, during Emperor Shizong's reign, the court refused to wage war on the Khitan. Feeling their mission betrayed and their loyalty discarded, the Tigers in Chains turned to darkness. Following Ye Wanshan's order, they slaughtered an entire city and pinned the blame on the Khitan, hoping to force the imperial court into action. Wracked with guilt, the soldiers ultimately chose to bind themselves in chains and enter the Pagoda of Karma with their general, seeking redemption for their unforgivable crime. 
But now, troubling news stirs once more. General Ye Wanshan has been released, and his whereabouts are unknown.

zh:
仆在行间，每闻京畿及诸道同僚赴义奔走，未尝不感泣于怀。
定州李殷，吾总角之交，性本温仁。自领节钺以来，夙夜劳形，手书军前凡三百余札，协济粮秣，通报机宜，遂使边军无匮粮之虞。
方千山，吾同门也。虽平生持论与吾相左，自战事起，方兄捐弃前嫌，于朝中力排众议，只为供我麾下将士一饭之饱。
朝外则有寒江子、穆齐、丰云长等文士，振笔醒世，不惧威权；更有桑维翰辈立于朝堂，直言如剑。
夫文道者，江山之脊骨也。赖诸君内外相支，而后天下苍生，方得这一夕之安枕。
en:
Serving here among the ranks, whenever I hear of comrades in the capital and across the circuits rushing to the cause, I am never unmoved to tears.
Li Yin of Dingzhou, my friend since boyhood, is gentle by nature. Since he took up his command, he has toiled from dawn to deep night, penning more than three hundred dispatches to the front, coordinating provisions and relaying intelligence, so that the border troops have never once wanted for grain.
Fang Qianshan and I studied under the same master. Though all his life his views have run counter to mine, since the war began he has set aside our old discord, standing firm against the whole court, only that the soldiers under my command might eat their fill.
Beyond the court there are scholars such as Han Jiangzi, Mu Qi, and Feng Yunchang, who wield their brushes to wake the world and do not flinch before power; and within it stand men like Sang Weihan, whose plain words cut like a blade.
For the way of the written word is the very backbone of a nation. It is only through such men, upholding it within the court and without, that the people of the realm may lay their heads down in peace, if only for a single night.
